zh.name: 主格代词
zh.meaning: 主格代词（I, you, he 等）作句子的主语，指做动作或处于某种状态的人或事物。英语句子一般不能省略主语。
zh.formation: I / you / he / she / it / we / they（you 可指“你”或“你们”）
zh.contrast: 主格与宾格：I / he / she / we / they 放在动词前作主语，me / him / her / us / them 放在动词或介词后（She helps me）。he 指男性，she 指女性，事物和动物用 it。
zh.example: She likes reading books in the library.
zh.exampleTranslation: 她喜欢在图书馆里读书。

en.name: Subject pronouns
en.meaning: Subject pronouns (I, you, he…) replace the noun that does the action. An English sentence almost always needs a subject.
en.formation: I / you / he / she / it / we / they
en.contrast: Subject vs object pronouns: I/he/she/we/they come before the verb, me/him/her/us/them after a verb or preposition (She helps me). Use he for a man, she for a woman and it for things.
en.example: She likes reading books in the library.
en.exampleTranslation: She likes reading books in the library.

fr.name: Pronoms sujets
fr.meaning: Les pronoms sujets (I, you, he…) remplacent le nom de la personne ou de la chose qui fait l'action. En anglais, le sujet est presque toujours exprimé.
fr.formation: I / you / he / she / it / we / they (you = tu ou vous ; they = ils ou elles)
fr.contrast: Pronoms sujets ou objets : I/he/she/we/they avant le verbe, me/him/her/us/them après un verbe ou une préposition (She helps me). Pour une chose, on dit it, jamais he ou she (la table → it).
fr.example: She likes reading books in the library.
fr.exampleTranslation: Elle aime lire des livres à la bibliothèque.

zh.name: be动词现在时
zh.meaning: be 动词现在时有 am、is、are 三种形式，用来说明身份、状态、特征、年龄或位置，形式随主语变化。
zh.formation: I am；he / she / it is；you / we / they are。缩写：I'm, she's, they're；否定：isn't, aren't
zh.contrast: 形容词前不能漏掉 be（She is happy，不说 *She happy），普通动词前不能多加 be（I like it，不说 *I am like it）。
zh.example: My parents are teachers, and I am a student.
zh.exampleTranslation: 我父母是老师，我是学生。

en.name: Present simple of 'be'
en.meaning: The present of be has three forms: am, is and are. It describes identity, states, qualities, age and place, and changes with the subject.
en.formation: I am; he / she / it is; you / we / they are. Short forms: I'm, she's, they're; negatives: isn't, aren't
en.contrast: Don't drop be before an adjective (She is happy, not *She happy) and don't add it before another verb (I like it, not *I am like it). Age and feelings take be: I am 20, I am hungry.
en.example: My parents are teachers, and I am a student.
en.exampleTranslation: My parents are teachers, and I am a student.

fr.name: Présent du verbe être
fr.meaning: Le présent de be a trois formes : am, is et are. Il exprime l'identité, l'état, une qualité, l'âge ou le lieu, et change selon le sujet.
fr.formation: I am ; he / she / it is ; you / we / they are. Formes courtes : I'm, she's, they're ; négation : isn't, aren't
fr.contrast: L'anglais utilise be là où le français dit avoir : I am 20 (j'ai 20 ans), I am hungry (j'ai faim), I am cold (j'ai froid). Pas de be devant un autre verbe : I like it, et non *I am like it.
fr.example: My parents are teachers, and I am a student.
fr.exampleTranslation: Mes parents sont professeurs, et moi, je suis étudiant.

zh.name: 指示代词
zh.meaning: this / these 指近处的人或物，that / those 指远处的人或物；可以放在名词前，也可以单独使用。
zh.formation: this / that + 单数名词（this book）；these / those + 复数名词（those shoes）；单独用：What's this?
zh.contrast: 单复数要一致：these books，不说 *this books。提到刚说过的事常用 that：That's a good idea。
zh.example: These apples on the table are sweet.
zh.exampleTranslation: 桌子上的这些苹果很甜。

en.name: Demonstratives
en.meaning: This and these point to people or things near the speaker; that and those point to things farther away. They can go before a noun or stand alone.
en.formation: this / that + singular noun (this book); these / those + plural noun (those shoes); alone: What's this?
en.contrast: The word must agree in number: these books, not *this books. Use that for something just said: That's a good idea.
en.example: These apples on the table are sweet.
en.exampleTranslation: These apples on the table are sweet.

fr.name: Démonstratifs
fr.meaning: This et these désignent ce qui est proche ; that et those, ce qui est plus loin. Ils se placent devant un nom ou s'emploient seuls.
fr.formation: this / that + nom singulier (this book) ; these / those + nom pluriel (those shoes) ; seul : What's this?
fr.contrast: Le français ce/cette/ces ne marque pas la distance, l'anglais oui : this book (ce livre-ci), that book (ce livre-là). Accordez au pluriel : these books, et non *this books.
fr.example: These apples on the table are sweet.
fr.exampleTranslation: Ces pommes sur la table sont sucrées.

zh.name: 名词复数规则
zh.meaning: 可数名词表示两个或更多时用复数：一般加 -s；以 s、x、z、ch、sh 结尾加 -es；辅音字母 + y 结尾，变 y 为 i 再加 -es。
zh.formation: book → books；bus → buses，box → boxes，watch → watches；city → cities（但 boy → boys）；knife → knives
zh.contrast: 例外：不规则复数（man → men，child → children，foot → feet）；单复同形（sheep，fish）；以 -o 结尾的词有的加 -es（potatoes），有的只加 -s（photos）；不可数名词（water, advice）没有复数。
zh.example: My two cousins live in big cities.
zh.exampleTranslation: 我的两个表亲住在大城市里。

en.name: Plural nouns: spelling
en.meaning: Countable nouns take a plural form for two or more. Add -s; add -es after s, x, z, ch or sh; change consonant + y to -ies.
en.formation: book → books; bus → buses, box → boxes, watch → watches; city → cities (but boy → boys); knife → knives
en.contrast: Exceptions: irregular plurals (man → men, child → children, foot → feet); same form (sheep, fish); some -o nouns add -es (potatoes), others only -s (photos); uncountable nouns (water, advice) have no plural.
en.example: My two cousins live in big cities.
en.exampleTranslation: My two cousins live in big cities.

fr.name: Pluriel des noms
fr.meaning: Un nom comptable prend le pluriel à partir de deux. On ajoute -s ; -es après s, x, z, ch ou sh ; consonne + y devient -ies.
fr.formation: book → books ; bus → buses, box → boxes, watch → watches ; city → cities (mais boy → boys) ; knife → knives
fr.contrast: Exceptions : pluriels irréguliers (man → men, child → children, foot → feet) ; forme identique (sheep, fish) ; certains noms en -o prennent -es (potatoes), d'autres -s (photos) ; les indénombrables (advice, information) restent au singulier, contrairement à « des conseils, des informations ».
fr.example: My two cousins live in big cities.
fr.exampleTranslation: Mes deux cousins habitent dans de grandes villes.

zh.name: 形容词性物主代词
zh.meaning: 所有格形容词（如 my, your, his）放在名词前面，用来表示某物属于谁。
zh.formation: my / your / his / her / its / our / their + 名词
zh.contrast: his / her 取决于“拥有者”的性别：Tom loves his mother；Anna loves her father。its 是物主词，it's 是 it is 的缩写。mine、yours 等名词性物主代词后面不接名词。
zh.example: My brother plays football every weekend.
zh.exampleTranslation: 我哥哥每个周末都踢足球。

en.name: Possessive adjectives
en.meaning: Possessive adjectives (like my, your, his) are placed before nouns to show ownership or belonging.
en.formation: my / your / his / her / its / our / their + noun
en.contrast: His or her depends on the owner, not the thing: Tom loves his mother; Anna loves her father. Its (possessive) is not it's (it is). Mine, yours… stand alone without a noun.
en.example: My brother plays football every weekend.
en.exampleTranslation: My brother plays football every weekend.

fr.name: Adjectifs possessifs
fr.meaning: Les adjectifs possessifs (comme my, your, his) se placent devant un nom pour indiquer à qui appartient quelque chose.
fr.formation: my / your / his / her / its / our / their + nom
fr.contrast: His ou her dépend du possesseur, pas de l'objet : Tom loves his mother (sa mère), Anna loves her father (son père). Ne confondez pas its (possessif) et it's (it is).
fr.example: My brother plays football every weekend.
fr.exampleTranslation: Mon frère joue au foot tous les week-ends.

points.pattern: indefinite and definite articles (a, an, the)

zh.name: 冠词
zh.meaning: a / an 用于第一次提到或不特指的单数可数名词；the 用于双方都知道的特定事物，或前面已经提到过的事物。
zh.formation: a + 辅音音素开头（a cat, a university）；an + 元音音素开头（an apple, an hour）；the + 单数、复数或不可数名词
zh.contrast: 单数可数名词前不能什么都不加（I saw a dog，不说 *I saw dog）。泛指复数或不可数名词时不用 the：I like cats，Water is important。
zh.example: I saw a dog in the park, and the dog was very friendly.
zh.exampleTranslation: 我在公园里看到一只狗，那只狗非常友好。

en.name: Articles (a, an, the)
en.meaning: Use a / an with a singular countable noun that is new or not specific. Use the when both speakers know which one, or it was mentioned before.
en.formation: a + consonant sound (a cat, a university); an + vowel sound (an apple, an hour); the + singular, plural or uncountable nouns
en.contrast: A singular countable noun needs an article or a similar word (I saw a dog, not *I saw dog). For things in general, use no article: I like cats, not *I like the cats.
en.example: I saw a dog in the park, and the dog was very friendly.
en.exampleTranslation: I saw a dog in the park, and the dog was very friendly.

fr.name: Articles (a, an, the)
fr.meaning: A / an s'emploie devant un nom comptable singulier nouveau ou non précis. The s'emploie quand on sait de quelle chose on parle, ou qu'on l'a déjà mentionnée.
fr.formation: a + son consonne (a cat, a university) ; an + son voyelle (an apple, an hour) ; the + nom singulier, pluriel ou indénombrable
fr.contrast: Pour parler en général, l'anglais n'utilise pas d'article, contrairement au français : I like cats (j'aime les chats), Life is short (la vie est courte). A n'a pas de pluriel : books ou some books.
fr.example: I saw a dog in the park, and the dog was very friendly.
fr.exampleTranslation: J'ai vu un chien dans le parc, et le chien était très gentil.

zh.name: 一般现在时
zh.meaning: 一般现在时表示习惯、经常发生的事和普遍事实。主语是第三人称单数（he, she, it）时，动词加 -s 或 -es。
zh.formation: I / you / we / they work；he / she / it works（watch → watches，study → studies，have → has）
zh.contrast: 现在进行时（be + -ing）表示此刻正在发生的事：She drinks tea every day（习惯）/ She is drinking tea now（现在正在喝）。
zh.example: She drinks a cup of tea every morning.
zh.exampleTranslation: 她每天早晨喝一杯茶。

en.name: Present simple tense
en.meaning: The present simple is for habits, routines and general facts. With he, she or it, the verb takes -s or -es.
en.formation: I / you / we / they work; he / she / it works (watch → watches, study → studies, have → has)
en.contrast: The present continuous (be + -ing) is for what is happening now: She drinks tea every day (habit) vs She is drinking tea now (at this moment).
en.example: She drinks a cup of tea every morning.
en.exampleTranslation: She drinks a cup of tea every morning.

fr.name: Présent simple
fr.meaning: Le présent simple exprime les habitudes, les routines et les vérités générales. Avec he, she ou it, le verbe prend -s ou -es.
fr.formation: I / you / we / they work ; he / she / it works (watch → watches, study → studies, have → has)
fr.contrast: Le présent français couvre deux temps anglais : pour une action en cours, on emploie le présent continu. She drinks tea every day (habitude) / She is drinking tea now (en ce moment).
fr.example: She drinks a cup of tea every morning.
fr.exampleTranslation: Elle boit une tasse de thé tous les matins.

aliases: 一般现在时否定句和疑问句

zh.name: 一般现在时否定和疑问
zh.meaning: 一般现在时的否定句和疑问句要用助动词 do / does，主要动词用原形。
zh.formation: 否定：主语 + don't / doesn't + 动词原形；疑问：Do / Does + 主语 + 动词原形？简答：Yes, I do. / No, she doesn't.
zh.contrast: -s 已经在 does 上，主要动词不再加 -s（She doesn't like，不说 *doesn't likes）。be 动词不用 do：Are you tired?，不说 *Do you are tired?
zh.example: My brother doesn't like coffee, but he drinks a lot of tea.
zh.exampleTranslation: 我哥哥不喜欢咖啡，但他喝很多茶。

en.name: Present simple negatives and questions
en.meaning: Negatives and questions in the present simple use the helper do or does, and the main verb stays in the base form.
en.formation: Negative: subject + don't / doesn't + base verb; question: Do / Does + subject + base verb? Short answers: Yes, I do. / No, she doesn't.
en.contrast: The -s moves to does, so the main verb has none (She doesn't like, not *doesn't likes). Be needs no do: Are you tired?, not *Do you are tired?
en.example: My brother doesn't like coffee, but he drinks a lot of tea.
en.exampleTranslation: My brother doesn't like coffee, but he drinks a lot of tea.

fr.name: Négation et questions au présent
fr.meaning: Au présent simple, la négation et la question se forment avec l'auxiliaire do ou does, et le verbe reste à la base verbale.
fr.formation: Négation : sujet + don't / doesn't + base verbale ; question : Do / Does + sujet + base verbale ? Réponses courtes : Yes, I do. / No, she doesn't.
fr.contrast: Pas de question par simple inversion comme en français (*Like you coffee?) : Do you like coffee? Le -s passe sur does : She doesn't like, et non *doesn't likes.
fr.example: My brother doesn't like coffee, but he drinks a lot of tea.
fr.exampleTranslation: Mon frère n'aime pas le café, mais il boit beaucoup de thé.

aliases: who what where when why how

zh.name: 特殊疑问词
zh.meaning: 疑问词（who, what, where, when, why, how, which, whose）用来询问具体信息，放在问句开头，回答不能只用 yes 或 no。
zh.formation: 疑问词 + do / does / did 或 be + 主语 + …？（Where does she work? / Why are you late?）
zh.contrast: 疑问词后要用疑问语序：Where does she work?，不说 *Where she works?。但 who / what 作主语时不用 do：Who called you?
zh.example: Where does your sister work?
zh.exampleTranslation: 你姐姐在哪儿工作？

en.name: Question words
en.meaning: Question words (who, what, where, when, why, how, which, whose) ask for specific information. They start the question, and the answer is not just yes or no.
en.formation: Question word + do / does / did or be + subject + …? (Where does she work? / Why are you late?)
en.contrast: Use question word order after the question word: Where does she work?, not *Where she works? But when who or what is the subject, there is no do: Who called you?
en.example: Where does your sister work?
en.exampleTranslation: Where does your sister work?

fr.name: Mots interrogatifs
fr.meaning: Les mots interrogatifs (who, what, where, when, why, how, which, whose) demandent une information précise. Ils ouvrent la question ; on ne répond pas par oui ou non.
fr.formation: Mot interrogatif + do / does / did ou be + sujet + … ? (Where does she work? / Why are you late?)
fr.contrast: L'anglais n'accepte pas l'ordre « Tu travailles où ? » : le mot interrogatif vient en tête, suivi de do/does/did. Si who ou what est sujet, pas de do : Who called you?
fr.example: Where does your sister work?
fr.exampleTranslation: Où travaille ta sœur ?

zh.name: 频率副词
zh.meaning: 频率副词（always, usually, often, sometimes, rarely, never）说明动作多久发生一次，常用来描述习惯。
zh.formation: 放在实义动词前（She often walks）；放在 be 动词和助动词后（He is never late / I have never been there）
zh.contrast: 频率副词不放在动词和宾语之间：I often drink tea，不说 *I drink often tea。sometimes 和 usually 也可以放在句首。
zh.example: He always reads before bed.
zh.exampleTranslation: 他睡前总是看书。

en.name: Adverbs of frequency
en.meaning: Adverbs of frequency (always, usually, often, sometimes, rarely, never) say how often something happens. They are common with habits.
en.formation: Before a main verb (She often walks); after be and auxiliaries (He is never late / I have never been there)
en.contrast: Don't put them between the verb and its object: I often drink tea, not *I drink often tea. Sometimes and usually can also start the sentence.
en.example: He always reads before bed.
en.exampleTranslation: He always reads before bed.

fr.name: Adverbes de fréquence
fr.meaning: Les adverbes de fréquence (always, usually, often, sometimes, rarely, never) indiquent à quelle fréquence une action se produit, surtout pour les habitudes.
fr.formation: Avant le verbe principal (She often walks) ; après be et les auxiliaires (He is never late / I have never been there)
fr.contrast: Contrairement au français (« Il lit toujours »), l'adverbe se place avant le verbe principal : He always reads, et non *He reads always. Avec be, il vient après : He is always late.
fr.example: He always reads before bed.
fr.exampleTranslation: Il lit toujours avant de dormir.

zh.name: 祈使句
zh.meaning: 用来发出指令、提出请求或给出建议的句子，主语“you”通常被省略。
zh.formation: 动词原形 + …（Sit down.）；否定：Don't + 动词原形（Don't run.）；加 please 更礼貌
zh.contrast: 否定祈使句用 Don't + 动词原形，不说 *No run 或 *Not run。包括自己在内的建议用 Let's（Let's go）。直接用祈使句有时显得生硬，礼貌请求可以用 Could you …?
zh.example: Please close the door when you leave.
zh.exampleTranslation: 你离开时请把门关上。

en.name: Imperative sentences
en.meaning: Used to give orders, make requests, or offer advice, where the subject 'you' is usually omitted.
en.formation: Base verb + … (Sit down.); negative: Don't + base verb (Don't run.); add please to be polite
en.contrast: The negative is Don't + base verb, never *No run or *Not run. To include yourself, use Let's (Let's go). A bare imperative can sound rude; for polite requests use Could you…?
en.example: Please close the door when you leave.
en.exampleTranslation: Please close the door when you leave.

fr.name: Phrases impératives
fr.meaning: Utilisées pour donner des ordres, faire des demandes ou donner des conseils, le sujet « you » étant généralement omis.
fr.formation: Base verbale + … (Sit down.) ; négation : Don't + base verbale (Don't run.) ; please rend la phrase polie
fr.contrast: Une seule forme pour tu et vous (Sit down = assieds-toi / asseyez-vous). Pour « allons-y », on dit Let's go. Un impératif seul peut sembler sec ; pour demander poliment, utilisez Could you…?
fr.example: Please close the door when you leave.
fr.exampleTranslation: Ferme la porte en partant, s'il te plaît.

zh.name: 情态动词can表示能力
zh.meaning: can 表示某人有能力做某事，后接动词原形；否定是 can't / cannot。
zh.formation: 主语 + can / can't + 动词原形；疑问：Can you swim? — Yes, I can. / No, I can't.
zh.contrast: can 没有 -s，后面不加 to（She can swim，不说 *She cans / *can to swim）。过去的能力用 could，其他时态用 be able to（I will be able to come）。
zh.example: My little brother can swim very fast.
zh.exampleTranslation: 我弟弟能游得很快。

en.name: Can for ability
en.meaning: Can says that someone is able to do something. It is followed by the base verb; the negative is can't or cannot.
en.formation: Subject + can / can't + base verb; question: Can you swim? — Yes, I can. / No, I can't.
en.contrast: Can never takes -s or to (She can swim, not *She cans / *can to swim). For past ability use could; for other tenses use be able to (I will be able to come).
en.example: My little brother can swim very fast.
en.exampleTranslation: My little brother can swim very fast.

fr.name: Can pour exprimer la capacité
fr.meaning: Can exprime la capacité de faire quelque chose. Il est suivi de la base verbale ; la négation est can't ou cannot.
fr.formation: Sujet + can / can't + base verbale ; question : Can you swim? — Yes, I can. / No, I can't.
fr.contrast: Can traduit à la fois savoir et pouvoir (I can swim = je sais nager). Il est invariable et sans to : She can swim, et non *She cans / *can to swim. Au futur : will be able to.
fr.example: My little brother can swim very fast.
fr.exampleTranslation: Mon petit frère sait nager très vite.

zh.name: 现在进行时
zh.meaning: 现在进行时表示说话时正在进行的动作，也可以表示最近一段时间暂时在做的事。
zh.formation: 主语 + am / is / are + 动词-ing（She is reading. / Are you working? / I'm not sleeping.）
zh.contrast: 一般现在时表示习惯：I work in a bank（长期）/ I'm working now（此刻）。know、like、want 等状态动词一般不用进行时：I know him，不说 *I am knowing him。
zh.example: She is reading a book in the living room.
zh.exampleTranslation: 她正在客厅里看书。

en.name: Present continuous
en.meaning: The present continuous describes an action in progress now, or a temporary situation around now.
en.formation: Subject + am / is / are + verb-ing (She is reading. / Are you working? / I'm not sleeping.)
en.contrast: The present simple is for habits: I work in a bank (always) vs I'm working now (at the moment). State verbs like know, like and want are not usually continuous: I know him, not *I am knowing him.
en.example: She is reading a book in the living room.
en.exampleTranslation: She is reading a book in the living room.

fr.name: Présent continu
fr.meaning: Le présent continu décrit une action en cours au moment où l'on parle, ou une situation temporaire.
fr.formation: Sujet + am / is / are + verbe-ing (She is reading. / Are you working? / I'm not sleeping.)
fr.contrast: Le présent français suffit (« elle lit »), mais l'anglais exige le présent continu pour une action en cours : She is reading now, et non *She reads now. Les verbes d'état (know, like, want) restent au présent simple.
fr.example: She is reading a book in the living room.
fr.exampleTranslation: Elle est en train de lire un livre dans le salon.

zh.name: 宾格代词
zh.meaning: 宾格代词（me, him, her, us, them 等）放在动词或介词后面，指动作的对象。
zh.formation: 动词/介词 + me / you / him / her / it / us / them
zh.contrast: 主格作主语、放在动词前（She likes him），宾格放在动词或介词后（He likes her / with me）。介词后一定用宾格：between you and me，不说 *between you and I。
zh.example: Please help me with this heavy box.
zh.exampleTranslation: 请帮我搬一下这个重箱子。

en.name: Object pronouns
en.meaning: Object pronouns (me, him, her, us, them…) come after a verb or a preposition and refer to the person or thing receiving the action.
en.formation: Verb / preposition + me / you / him / her / it / us / them
en.contrast: Subject forms go before the verb, object forms after a verb or preposition: She likes him; he likes her. After a preposition always use the object form: between you and me, not *between you and I.
en.example: Please help me with this heavy box.
en.exampleTranslation: Please help me with this heavy box.

fr.name: Pronoms compléments
fr.meaning: Les pronoms compléments (me, him, her, us, them…) se placent après un verbe ou une préposition et désignent celui qui reçoit l'action.
fr.formation: Verbe / préposition + me / you / him / her / it / us / them
fr.contrast: Contrairement au français (« je l'aime »), le pronom se place après le verbe : I love her. Une seule forme pour COD et COI : I see him (je le vois), I talk to him (je lui parle).
fr.example: Please help me with this heavy box.
fr.exampleTranslation: Aide-moi avec ce carton lourd, s'il te plaît.

zh.name: 名词所有格
zh.meaning: 在名词后加 's 表示“某人的”，主要用于人和动物。
zh.formation: 单数名词 + 's（my brother's bike）；以 -s 结尾的复数只加 '（my parents' house）；其他复数加 's（the children's toys）
zh.contrast: 表示人的所属用 's，不用 of：my brother's bike，不说 *the bike of my brother。注意区分 's 和 is 的缩写：Tom's bike（Tom 的）/ Tom's tired（Tom is）。
zh.example: This is my brother's new bicycle.
zh.exampleTranslation: 这是我弟弟的新自行车。

en.name: Possessive 's
en.meaning: Add 's to a noun to show who something belongs to. It is used mainly with people and animals.
en.formation: Singular noun + 's (my brother's bike); plural ending in -s + ' (my parents' house); other plurals + 's (the children's toys)
en.contrast: For people, use 's rather than of: my brother's bike, not *the bike of my brother. For things, of is common: the end of the film. Don't confuse it with 's = is: Tom's tired.
en.example: This is my brother's new bicycle.
en.exampleTranslation: This is my brother's new bicycle.

fr.name: Génitif en 's
fr.meaning: On ajoute 's à un nom pour indiquer à qui appartient quelque chose, surtout avec les personnes et les animaux.
fr.formation: Nom singulier + 's (my brother's bike) ; pluriel en -s + ' (my parents' house) ; autres pluriels + 's (the children's toys)
fr.contrast: Le français dit « le vélo de mon frère », mais l'anglais met le possesseur en premier : my brother's bike, et non *the bike of my brother. Pour les choses, of reste courant : the end of the film.
fr.example: This is my brother's new bicycle.
fr.exampleTranslation: C'est le nouveau vélo de mon frère.

zh.name: 可数与不可数名词
zh.meaning: 可数名词有单复数，可以直接用数字计数；不可数名词（如 water, rice, advice）没有复数，不能直接加 a / an。
zh.formation: 可数：a / an + 单数，或用复数（an apple, two apples）；不可数：some / much / a little + 名词，或用量词（a glass of water, a piece of advice）
zh.contrast: 有些名词在英语里不可数，但在中文或法语里可以数：advice, information, furniture, homework, news。要说 some advice 或 a piece of advice，不说 *an advice / *advices。
zh.example: I would like an apple and some water.
zh.exampleTranslation: 我想要一个苹果和一些水。

en.name: Countable and uncountable nouns
en.meaning: Countable nouns have singular and plural forms and can be counted. Uncountable nouns (water, rice, advice) have no plural and can't take a/an.
en.formation: Countable: a / an + singular, or a plural (an apple, two apples); uncountable: some / much / a little + noun, or a unit (a glass of water, a piece of advice)
en.contrast: Some nouns are uncountable in English but countable in other languages: advice, information, furniture, homework, news. Say some advice or a piece of advice, not *an advice or *advices.
en.example: I would like an apple and some water.
en.exampleTranslation: I would like an apple and some water.

fr.name: Noms comptables et indénombrables
fr.meaning: Les noms comptables ont un singulier et un pluriel. Les indénombrables (water, rice, advice) n'ont pas de pluriel et ne prennent pas a/an.
fr.formation: Comptable : a / an + singulier, ou pluriel (an apple, two apples) ; indénombrable : some / much / a little + nom, ou une unité (a glass of water, a piece of advice)
fr.contrast: Certains noms comptables en français sont indénombrables en anglais : advice, information, furniture, homework, news. On dit some advice (des conseils), et non *advices.
fr.example: I would like an apple and some water.
fr.exampleTranslation: Je voudrais une pomme et de l'eau.

zh.name: 数量词 much / many
zh.meaning: many 和 much 都表示“很多”：many 修饰可数名词复数，much 修饰不可数名词；a lot of 两者都可以修饰。
zh.formation: many + 可数名词复数（many cars）；much + 不可数名词（much time）；a lot of + 两者皆可；提问：How many …? / How much …?
zh.contrast: 肯定句里一般用 a lot of，不用 much：I have a lot of money（不说 *I have much money）。much 主要用于否定句和疑问句：I don't have much time. / How much is it?
zh.example: There are many cars on the street today.
zh.exampleTranslation: 今天街上有许多汽车。

en.name: Much, many, a lot of
en.meaning: Many and much both mean a large amount: many goes with plural countable nouns, much with uncountable nouns. A lot of goes with both.
en.formation: many + plural noun (many cars); much + uncountable noun (much time); a lot of + either; questions: How many …? / How much …?
en.contrast: In positive statements, a lot of sounds more natural than much: I have a lot of money (not *I have much money). Much is mainly used in negatives and questions: I don't have much time.
en.example: There are many cars on the street today.
en.exampleTranslation: There are many cars on the street today.

fr.name: Much, many, a lot of
fr.meaning: Many et much signifient beaucoup : many avec un nom pluriel comptable, much avec un nom indénombrable. A lot of s'emploie avec les deux.
fr.formation: many + nom pluriel (many cars) ; much + nom indénombrable (much time) ; a lot of + les deux ; questions : How many …? / How much …?
fr.contrast: « Beaucoup de » se traduit selon le nom : many books, much water. À la forme affirmative, préférez a lot of : I have a lot of money, plutôt que *I have much money ; much s'emploie surtout dans les négations et les questions.
fr.example: There are many cars on the street today.
fr.exampleTranslation: Il y a beaucoup de voitures dans la rue aujourd'hui.

zh.name: 方位介词 in/on/at
zh.meaning: in、on、at 表示位置：in 表示在空间或区域里面，on 表示在表面上，at 表示在某个点或地点。
zh.formation: in + 房间 / 城市 / 国家（in the box, in Paris）；on + 表面 / 楼层 / 街道（on the table, on the second floor）；at + 具体地点（at the door, at home, at school）
zh.contrast: 中文都说“在”，英语要区分：城市和国家用 in（in Beijing，不说 *at Beijing）；固定说 at home, at work, at school；公交和火车用 on（on the bus），轿车用 in（in the car）。
zh.example: My keys are on the kitchen table.
zh.exampleTranslation: 我的钥匙在厨房的桌子上。

en.name: Prepositions of place
en.meaning: In, on and at show where something is: in for inside a space or area, on for a surface, at for a point or place.
en.formation: in + room / city / country (in the box, in Paris); on + surface / floor / street (on the table, on the second floor); at + point or place (at the door, at home, at school)
en.contrast: Use in with cities and countries (in Paris, not *at Paris), at in fixed phrases (at home, at work, at school), and on for buses and trains (on the bus) but in for cars (in the car).
en.example: My keys are on the kitchen table.
en.exampleTranslation: My keys are on the kitchen table.

fr.name: Prépositions de lieu
fr.meaning: In, on et at indiquent le lieu : in pour l'intérieur d'un espace, on pour une surface, at pour un point précis.
fr.formation: in + pièce / ville / pays (in the box, in Paris) ; on + surface / étage / rue (on the table, on the second floor) ; at + point précis (at the door, at home, at school)
fr.contrast: « À » se traduit de plusieurs façons : in Paris (à Paris), at home (à la maison), at the station (à la gare). Transports : on the bus (dans le bus), mais in the car (dans la voiture).
fr.example: My keys are on the kitchen table.
fr.exampleTranslation: Mes clés sont sur la table de la cuisine.

zh.name: 时间介词 in/on/at
zh.meaning: at、on、in 表示时间：at 用于钟点和时刻，on 用于星期和具体日期，in 用于月份、年份、季节和较长的时段。
zh.formation: at + 钟点（at 7:30, at noon, at night）；on + 星期 / 日期（on Monday, on 5 May）；in + 月 / 年 / 季节（in July, in 2025, in winter, in the morning）
zh.contrast: this、next、last、every、tomorrow、yesterday 前不用介词：next Monday，不说 *on next Monday。注意 in the morning，但 at night；某一天的早上用 on：on Monday morning。
zh.example: I have an English class at nine o'clock on Monday.
zh.exampleTranslation: 我星期一九点有一节英语课。

en.name: Prepositions of time
en.meaning: At, on and in show when something happens: at for clock times, on for days and dates, in for months, years, seasons and longer periods.
en.formation: at + clock time (at 7:30, at noon, at night); on + day / date (on Monday, on 5 May); in + month / year / season (in July, in 2025, in winter, in the morning)
en.contrast: No preposition before this, next, last, every, tomorrow or yesterday: next Monday, not *on next Monday. Note in the morning but at night, and on Monday morning for one specific day.
en.example: I have an English class at nine o'clock on Monday.
en.exampleTranslation: I have an English class at nine o'clock on Monday.

fr.name: Prépositions de temps
fr.meaning: At, on et in indiquent le moment : at pour l'heure, on pour les jours et les dates, in pour les mois, les années, les saisons et les périodes plus longues.
fr.formation: at + heure (at 7:30, at noon, at night) ; on + jour / date (on Monday, on 5 May) ; in + mois / année / saison (in July, in 2025, in winter, in the morning)
fr.contrast: Pas de préposition devant this, next, last, every, tomorrow : next Monday (lundi prochain), et non *on next Monday. On dit in the morning (le matin) mais at night (la nuit), et in 2025 (en 2025).
fr.example: I have an English class at nine o'clock on Monday.
fr.exampleTranslation: J'ai un cours d'anglais lundi à neuf heures.

zh.name: 形容词比较级
zh.meaning: 比较级用来比较两个人或事物，后面常接 than。短形容词加 -er，较长的形容词前加 more。
zh.formation: small → smaller，nice → nicer，big → bigger（双写辅音），easy → easier；more expensive, more interesting；A + be + 比较级 + than + B
zh.contrast: 不规则：good → better，bad → worse，far → farther / further。more 和 -er 不能同时用（*more bigger）。than 后面常用宾格：She is taller than me。
zh.example: My dog is smaller than my sister's cat.
zh.exampleTranslation: 我的狗比我姐姐的猫小。

en.name: Comparative adjectives
en.meaning: Comparatives compare two people or things, usually with than. Short adjectives add -er; longer ones use more.
en.formation: small → smaller, nice → nicer, big → bigger (double consonant), easy → easier; more expensive, more interesting; A + be + comparative + than + B
en.contrast: Irregular: good → better, bad → worse, far → farther/further. Never use more and -er together (*more bigger). After than, the object form is normal: She is taller than me.
en.example: My dog is smaller than my sister's cat.
en.exampleTranslation: My dog is smaller than my sister's cat.

fr.name: Adjectifs comparatifs
fr.meaning: Le comparatif compare deux personnes ou choses, en général avec than. Les adjectifs courts prennent -er ; les longs prennent more.
fr.formation: small → smaller, nice → nicer, big → bigger (consonne doublée), easy → easier ; more expensive, more interesting ; A + be + comparatif + than + B
fr.contrast: « Plus … que » ne se traduit pas toujours par more : bigger than, et non *more big than. Irréguliers : good → better, bad → worse. « Que » se dit than, jamais *that.
fr.example: My dog is smaller than my sister's cat.
fr.exampleTranslation: Mon chien est plus petit que le chat de ma sœur.

zh.name: 形容词最高级
zh.meaning: 最高级表示在一个群体（三个或以上）中程度最高，前面通常加 the。
zh.formation: the + 形容词-est（the smallest, the biggest, the happiest）；the most + 较长形容词（the most beautiful）；后接 in + 地点 / 群体，或 of + 时间 / 数量
zh.contrast: 不规则：good → the best，bad → the worst，far → the farthest / furthest。most 和 -est 不能同时用（*the most tallest）。地点和群体前用 in：the tallest in the class。
zh.example: This is the happiest day of my life.
zh.exampleTranslation: 这是我一生中最快乐的一天。

en.name: Superlative adjectives
en.meaning: Superlatives show that one person or thing has the most of a quality in a group of three or more. They usually take the.
en.formation: the + -est (the smallest, the biggest, the happiest); the most + longer adjective (the most beautiful); + in + place/group, or of + period/number
en.contrast: Irregular: good → the best, bad → the worst, far → the farthest/furthest. Never combine most and -est (*the most tallest). Use in for places and groups: the tallest in the class.
en.example: This is the happiest day of my life.
en.exampleTranslation: This is the happiest day of my life.

fr.name: Adjectifs superlatifs
fr.meaning: Le superlatif indique qu'une personne ou une chose a le plus une qualité dans un groupe de trois ou plus. Il prend en général the.
fr.formation: the + -est (the smallest, the biggest, the happiest) ; the most + adjectif long (the most beautiful) ; + in + lieu/groupe, ou of + période/nombre
fr.contrast: « Le plus grand de la classe » se dit the tallest in the class, et non *of the class : in pour un lieu ou un groupe. Irréguliers : good → the best, bad → the worst.
fr.example: This is the happiest day of my life.
fr.exampleTranslation: C'est le plus beau jour de ma vie.

zh.name: be动词过去式
zh.meaning: was / were 是 be 动词的过去式，表示过去的身份、状态、年龄或位置。
zh.formation: I / he / she / it was；you / we / they were；否定：wasn't / weren't；疑问：Were you tired? / Was she at home?
zh.contrast: “出生”要用过去式：I was born in 2005，不说 *I am born / *I born。普通动词的过去式前不加 was：I went home，不说 *I was go home。
zh.example: We were very tired after the long trip.
zh.exampleTranslation: 长途旅行后我们非常累。

en.name: Past simple of be
en.meaning: Was and were are the past forms of be. They describe past identities, states, ages and places.
en.formation: I / he / she / it was; you / we / they were; negative: wasn't / weren't; question: Were you tired? / Was she at home?
en.contrast: Born takes the past of be: I was born in 2005, not *I am born or *I born. Don't put was before another past verb: I went home, not *I was go home.
en.example: We were very tired after the long trip.
en.exampleTranslation: We were very tired after the long trip.

fr.name: Be au prétérit
fr.meaning: Was et were sont les formes passées de be. Ils décrivent une identité, un état, un âge ou un lieu dans le passé.
fr.formation: I / he / she / it was ; you / we / they were ; négation : wasn't / weren't ; question : Were you tired? / Was she at home?
fr.contrast: « Je suis né » se dit I was born, au passé, et non *I am born. Was/were traduit à la fois l'imparfait et le passé composé d'être : I was tired (j'étais / j'ai été fatigué).
fr.example: We were very tired after the long trip.
fr.exampleTranslation: Nous étions très fatigués après le long voyage.

zh.name: 一般过去时（规则动词）
zh.meaning: 一般过去时表示过去某个时间发生并已结束的动作。规则动词加 -ed，所有人称形式相同。
zh.formation: 动词 + -ed（walk → walked，play → played）；以 e 结尾加 -d（live → lived）；常见时间词：yesterday, last week, two days ago
zh.contrast: 有明确的过去时间（yesterday, last year, ago）时用一般过去时，不用现在完成时：I walked there yesterday，不说 *I have walked there yesterday。
zh.example: She walked to the park with her friend yesterday.
zh.exampleTranslation: 她昨天和朋友一起散步去了公园。

en.name: Past simple: regular verbs
en.meaning: The past simple describes actions that happened and finished at a time in the past. Regular verbs add -ed, with the same form for every person.
en.formation: verb + -ed (walk → walked, play → played); after -e add -d (live → lived); time words: yesterday, last week, two days ago
en.contrast: With a finished past time (yesterday, last year, ago), use the past simple, not the present perfect: I walked there yesterday, not *I have walked there yesterday.
en.example: She walked to the park with her friend yesterday.
en.exampleTranslation: She walked to the park with her friend yesterday.

fr.name: Prétérit : verbes réguliers
fr.meaning: Le prétérit exprime une action passée et terminée à un moment précis. Les verbes réguliers prennent -ed, à toutes les personnes.
fr.formation: verbe + -ed (walk → walked, play → played) ; après -e, ajouter -d (live → lived) ; repères : yesterday, last week, two days ago
fr.contrast: Le passé composé se traduit le plus souvent par le prétérit : Yesterday I walked…, et non *I have walked yesterday. Avec un moment passé précis, pas de present perfect.
fr.example: She walked to the park with her friend yesterday.
fr.exampleTranslation: Hier, elle est allée au parc à pied avec son amie.

aliases: 一般过去时（不规则动词）

zh.name: 一般过去时（不规则动词）
zh.meaning: 很多常用动词的过去式不是加 -ed，而是有特殊形式，需要逐个记住；所有人称形式相同。
zh.formation: go → went，eat → ate，see → saw，have → had，buy → bought，swim → swam；有些不变：put → put，cut → cut
zh.contrast: did / didn't 后面用动词原形：Did you go?，不说 *Did you went?。过去式和过去分词不一定相同：I went（过去式）/ I have gone（过去分词）。
zh.example: We went to the beach and swam in the sea.
zh.exampleTranslation: 我们去了海边，还在海里游了泳。

en.name: Past simple: irregular verbs
en.meaning: Many common verbs have a special past form instead of -ed, and it must be learned. The form is the same for every person.
en.formation: go → went, eat → ate, see → saw, have → had, buy → bought, swim → swam; some don't change: put → put, cut → cut
en.contrast: After did / didn't use the base form: Did you go?, not *Did you went? The past form and past participle can differ: I went vs I have gone.
en.example: We went to the beach and swam in the sea.
en.exampleTranslation: We went to the beach and swam in the sea.

fr.name: Prétérit : verbes irréguliers
fr.meaning: Beaucoup de verbes courants ont une forme passée spéciale au lieu de -ed, qu'il faut apprendre. Elle est la même à toutes les personnes.
fr.formation: go → went, eat → ate, see → saw, have → had, buy → bought, swim → swam ; certains ne changent pas : put → put, cut → cut
fr.contrast: Après did / didn't, on reprend la base verbale : Did you go?, et non *Did you went? Prétérit et participe passé peuvent différer : I went / I have gone.
fr.example: We went to the beach and swam in the sea.
fr.exampleTranslation: Nous sommes allés à la plage et nous avons nagé dans la mer.

aliases: 一般过去时否定句和疑问句

zh.name: 一般过去时否定和疑问
zh.meaning: 一般过去时的否定句和疑问句用助动词 did / didn't，所有人称都一样，主要动词用原形。
zh.formation: 否定：主语 + didn't + 动词原形；疑问：Did + 主语 + 动词原形？简答：Yes, I did. / No, I didn't.
zh.contrast: did 已经表示过去，主要动词要用原形：I didn't go，不说 *I didn't went；Did you see it?，不说 *Did you saw it?。be 动词不用 did：Were you there?
zh.example: Did you watch the movie yesterday?
zh.exampleTranslation: 你昨天看电影了吗？

en.name: Past simple: negatives, questions
en.meaning: Past simple negatives and questions use did / didn't for every person, and the main verb goes back to the base form.
en.formation: Negative: subject + didn't + base verb; question: Did + subject + base verb? Short answers: Yes, I did. / No, I didn't.
en.contrast: Did already shows the past, so the main verb stays in the base form: I didn't go, not *I didn't went; Did you see it?, not *Did you saw it? Be needs no did: Were you there?
en.example: Did you watch the movie yesterday?
en.exampleTranslation: Did you watch the movie yesterday?

fr.name: Négation et questions au prétérit
fr.meaning: Au prétérit, la négation et la question se forment avec did / didn't à toutes les personnes, et le verbe revient à la base verbale.
fr.formation: Négation : sujet + didn't + base verbale ; question : Did + sujet + base verbale ? Réponses : Yes, I did. / No, I didn't.
fr.contrast: Did porte déjà le passé : le verbe reste à la base verbale (I didn't go, et non *I didn't went ; Did you see it?, et non *Did you saw it?). Avec be, pas de did : Were you there?
fr.example: Did you watch the movie yesterday?
fr.exampleTranslation: As-tu regardé le film hier ?

zh.name: be going to表将来
zh.meaning: be going to 表示已经打算好的计划，或根据眼前迹象判断即将发生的事。
zh.formation: 主语 + am / is / are + going to + 动词原形（I'm going to study. / Look at the clouds — it's going to rain.）
zh.contrast: will 常用于说话时临时做的决定：The phone's ringing — I'll answer it。事先决定好的计划用 be going to：I'm going to visit my aunt next week。
zh.example: We are going to visit our grandparents this weekend.
zh.exampleTranslation: 我们打算这周末去探望祖父母。

en.name: Be going to (future)
en.meaning: Be going to talks about plans already decided, or predictions based on what we can see now.
en.formation: Subject + am / is / are + going to + base verb (I'm going to study. / Look at those clouds — it's going to rain.)
en.contrast: Will is often used for decisions made at the moment of speaking: The phone's ringing — I'll answer it. For a plan decided earlier, use be going to: I'm going to visit my aunt next week.
en.example: We are going to visit our grandparents this weekend.
en.exampleTranslation: We are going to visit our grandparents this weekend.

fr.name: Futur avec be going to
fr.meaning: Be going to exprime un projet déjà décidé, ou une prédiction fondée sur ce qu'on voit. C'est proche du futur proche « aller + infinitif ».
fr.formation: Sujet + am / is / are + going to + base verbale (I'm going to study. / Look at those clouds — it's going to rain.)
fr.contrast: Will s'emploie pour une décision prise sur le moment : The phone's ringing — I'll answer it. Pour un projet déjà décidé, be going to : I'm going to visit my aunt next week. N'oubliez pas be : *I going to.
fr.example: We are going to visit our grandparents this weekend.
fr.exampleTranslation: Nous allons rendre visite à nos grands-parents ce week-end.

zh.name: there is / are
zh.meaning: there is / there are 表示“某处有某物”，说明某人或某物的存在。真正的主语在 be 后面。
zh.formation: There is + 单数 / 不可数名词（There is a book / some milk）；There are + 复数名词（There are three apples）；否定：There isn't / aren't；疑问：Is there …? / Are there …?
zh.contrast: 表示存在的“有”不能译成 have：桌上有三个苹果 = There are three apples on the table，不说 *There have three apples。人拥有某物才用 have：I have a car。
zh.example: There are three apples on the kitchen table.
zh.exampleTranslation: 厨房桌子上有三个苹果。

en.name: There is and there are
en.meaning: There is / there are say that something exists or is in a place. The real subject comes after be.
en.formation: There is + singular / uncountable noun (There is a book / some milk); There are + plural noun (There are three apples); negative: There isn't / aren't; question: Is there …? / Are there …?
en.contrast: Don't use have for existence: There are three apples on the table, not *There have three apples. Use have when a person owns something: I have a car.
en.example: There are three apples on the kitchen table.
en.exampleTranslation: There are three apples on the kitchen table.

fr.name: There is et there are
fr.meaning: There is / there are disent qu'une chose existe ou se trouve quelque part, comme « il y a ». Le vrai sujet vient après be.
fr.formation: There is + nom singulier / indénombrable (There is a book / some milk) ; There are + nom pluriel (There are three apples) ; négation : There isn't / aren't ; question : Is there …? / Are there …?
fr.contrast: « Il y a » change selon le nombre : there is + singulier, there are + pluriel. Et « il y a » de temps se dit ago : two years ago (il y a deux ans), et non *there are two years.
fr.example: There are three apples on the kitchen table.
fr.exampleTranslation: Il y a trois pommes sur la table de la cuisine.

zh.name: 喜好动词 + -ing
zh.meaning: like、love、hate 表示喜欢或讨厌，后面可以接名词，也可以接动词-ing 表示喜欢或讨厌做某事。
zh.formation: like / love / hate + 名词（I love music）；+ 动词-ing（She likes swimming）；否定：don't like + -ing
zh.contrast: 不能直接接动词原形：I like swimming 或 I like to swim，不说 *I like swim。would like 表示现在想要：I like swimming（平时喜欢）/ I'd like to swim now（现在想游）。
zh.example: My little brother hates eating vegetables for dinner.
zh.exampleTranslation: 我弟弟讨厌晚餐吃蔬菜。

en.name: Like, love, hate + -ing
en.meaning: Like, love and hate express what we enjoy or dislike. They take a noun, or a verb in -ing for activities.
en.formation: like / love / hate + noun (I love music); + verb-ing (She likes swimming); negative: don't like + -ing
en.contrast: Never use the bare verb: I like swimming or I like to swim, not *I like swim. Would like is about a wish now: I like swimming (in general) vs I'd like to swim now.
en.example: My little brother hates eating vegetables for dinner.
en.exampleTranslation: My little brother hates eating vegetables for dinner.

fr.name: Like, love, hate + -ing
fr.meaning: Like, love et hate expriment ce qu'on aime ou déteste. Ils sont suivis d'un nom, ou d'un verbe en -ing pour une activité.
fr.formation: like / love / hate + nom (I love music) ; + verbe-ing (She likes swimming) ; négation : don't like + -ing
fr.contrast: « J'aime nager » se dit I like swimming (ou I like to swim), et non *I like swim. Would like exprime un souhait présent : I like swimming (en général) / I'd like to swim now (maintenant).
fr.example: My little brother hates eating vegetables for dinner.
fr.exampleTranslation: Mon petit frère déteste manger des légumes au dîner.

zh.name: have got 表示拥有
zh.meaning: have got 表示拥有（物品、家人、外貌特征、疾病等），意思和 have 相同，英式口语常用。
zh.formation: I / you / we / they have got（'ve got）；he / she / it has got（'s got）；否定：haven't / hasn't got；疑问：Have you got …?
zh.contrast: have got 只用于现在时的“拥有”；过去用 had（I had a dog，不说 *I had got a dog）。两种问法不要混用：Have you got a car? 或 Do you have a car?，不说 *Do you have got a car?
zh.example: Tom has got a fast computer in his bedroom.
zh.exampleTranslation: 汤姆的卧室里有一台很快的电脑。

en.name: Have got
en.meaning: Have got means the same as have for possession (things, family, features, illnesses). It is common in spoken British English.
en.formation: I / you / we / they have got ('ve got); he / she / it has got ('s got); negative: haven't / hasn't got; question: Have you got …?
en.contrast: Have got is only for possession in the present; for the past use had (I had a dog, not *I had got a dog). Don't mix the questions: Have you got a car? or Do you have a car?, not *Do you have got a car?
en.example: Tom has got a fast computer in his bedroom.
en.exampleTranslation: Tom has got a fast computer in his bedroom.

fr.name: Have got
fr.meaning: Have got signifie « avoir » (objets, famille, traits physiques, maladies), comme have. Il est très courant à l'oral en anglais britannique.
fr.formation: I / you / we / they have got ('ve got) ; he / she / it has got ('s got) ; négation : haven't / hasn't got ; question : Have you got …?
fr.contrast: Have got ne s'emploie qu'au présent pour la possession ; au passé, on dit had (I had a dog). Ne mélangez pas les questions : Have you got a car? ou Do you have a car?, et non *Do you have got a car?
fr.example: Tom has got a fast computer in his bedroom.
fr.exampleTranslation: Tom a un ordinateur rapide dans sa chambre.

zh.name: 基础连词
zh.meaning: and、but、because 用来连接词语或句子：and 表示并列和补充，but 表示转折，because 表示原因。
zh.formation: A and B（I like tea and coffee）；分句, but 分句（It's cheap, but it's good）；分句 + because + 原因（I stayed home because I was ill）
zh.contrast: because 和 so 不能同时用：Because it rained, we stayed home 或 It rained, so we stayed home，不说 *Because it rained, so we stayed home（中文的“因为……所以……”）。
zh.example: I was very tired, but I finished my homework.
zh.exampleTranslation: 我很累，但我还是写完了作业。

en.name: Basic conjunctions
en.meaning: And, but and because join words or clauses: and adds information, but shows contrast, and because gives a reason.
en.formation: A and B (I like tea and coffee); clause, but clause (It's cheap, but it's good); clause + because + reason (I stayed home because I was ill)
en.contrast: Don't use because and so together: Because it rained, we stayed home, or It rained, so we stayed home — not *Because it rained, so we stayed home.
en.example: I was very tired, but I finished my homework.
en.exampleTranslation: I was very tired, but I finished my homework.

fr.name: Les conjonctions de base
fr.meaning: And, but et because relient des mots ou des propositions : and ajoute, but oppose, because donne une raison.
fr.formation: A and B (I like tea and coffee) ; proposition, but proposition (It's cheap, but it's good) ; proposition + because + raison (I stayed home because I was ill)
fr.contrast: Because (parce que) est suivi d'une proposition ; devant un nom, on dit because of (à cause de) : because of the rain, et non *because the rain.
fr.example: I was very tired, but I finished my homework.
fr.exampleTranslation: J'étais très fatigué, mais j'ai fini mes devoirs.

zh.name: would like 想要
zh.meaning: would like 表示“想要”，比 want 更礼貌，常用于点餐、购物和邀请（Would you like …?）。
zh.formation: would like（'d like）+ 名词（I'd like a coffee）；+ to + 动词原形（I'd like to go）；邀请：Would you like some tea?
zh.contrast: like 表示平时喜欢，would like 表示现在想要：I like tea（喜欢喝茶）/ I'd like a tea（现在想要一杯）。接动词时要用 to：I'd like to go，不说 *I'd like go。
zh.example: I would like a cup of hot tea, please.
zh.exampleTranslation: 请给我一杯热茶。

en.name: Would like
en.meaning: Would like means want, but it is more polite. It is used for ordering, shopping and invitations (Would you like…?).
en.formation: would like ('d like) + noun (I'd like a coffee); + to + base verb (I'd like to go); offers: Would you like some tea?
en.contrast: Like is a general preference; would like is a wish now: I like tea (always) vs I'd like a tea (now, please). Before a verb use to: I'd like to go, not *I'd like go.
en.example: I would like a cup of hot tea, please.
en.exampleTranslation: I would like a cup of hot tea, please.

fr.name: Would like
fr.meaning: Would like signifie « vouloir », mais de façon plus polie, comme « je voudrais ». On l'emploie pour commander, acheter ou proposer (Would you like…?).
fr.formation: would like ('d like) + nom (I'd like a coffee) ; + to + base verbale (I'd like to go) ; proposer : Would you like some tea?
fr.contrast: Like = aimer en général, would like = vouloir maintenant : I like tea (j'aime le thé) / I'd like a tea (je voudrais un thé). Devant un verbe, il faut to : I'd like to go, et non *I'd like go.
fr.example: I would like a cup of hot tea, please.
fr.exampleTranslation: Je voudrais une tasse de thé chaud, s'il vous plaît.

zh.name: let's 提建议
zh.meaning: let's（= let us）用来提出包括自己在内的建议，意思是“我们……吧”。
zh.formation: Let's + 动词原形（Let's go）；否定：Let's not + 动词原形（Let's not wait）；附加问句：Let's go, shall we?
zh.contrast: let's 后面直接用动词原形：Let's go，不说 *Let's to go / *Let's going。不缩写的 let us 常表示“请允许我们”：Please let us in。
zh.example: Let's walk to the park this sunny afternoon.
zh.exampleTranslation: 趁着这个晴朗的下午，我们步行去公园吧。

en.name: Let's for suggestions
en.meaning: Let's (let us) makes a suggestion that includes the speaker, like 'we should…'.
en.formation: Let's + base verb (Let's go); negative: Let's not + base verb (Let's not wait); tag: Let's go, shall we?
en.contrast: Use the bare verb after let's: Let's go, not *Let's to go or *Let's going. Uncontracted let us often means 'allow us': Please let us in.
en.example: Let's walk to the park this sunny afternoon.
en.exampleTranslation: Let's walk to the park this sunny afternoon.

fr.name: Let's pour proposer
fr.meaning: Let's (let us) sert à faire une proposition qui inclut celui qui parle, comme l'impératif en « -ons ».
fr.formation: Let's + base verbale (Let's go) ; négation : Let's not + base verbale (Let's not wait) ; question tag : Let's go, shall we?
fr.contrast: Let's correspond à l'impératif en « -ons » (Let's go = allons-y). Sans contraction, let us signifie souvent « laissez-nous » : Please let us in.
fr.example: Let's walk to the park this sunny afternoon.
fr.exampleTranslation: Allons au parc à pied cet après-midi, il fait beau.

zh.name: 缩写形式
zh.meaning: 缩写是把两个词合成一个，用撇号（'）代替省略的字母，常用于口语和非正式书面语。
zh.formation: I am → I'm，you are → you're，he is / has → he's，we have → we've，I will → I'll，I would / had → I'd；do not → don't，is not → isn't，cannot → can't
zh.contrast: 例外：will not → won't；am not 没有 *amn't（问句用 Aren't I?）；'s 可以是 is 或 has，'d 可以是 would 或 had；肯定简答不缩写：Yes, I am（不说 *Yes, I'm）；its（它的）没有撇号。
zh.example: I'm a student at this school.
zh.exampleTranslation: 我是这所学校的学生。

en.name: Contractions
en.meaning: A contraction joins two words into one, with an apostrophe in place of the missing letters. Contractions are normal in speech and informal writing.
en.formation: I am → I'm, you are → you're, he is / has → he's, we have → we've, I will → I'll, I would / had → I'd; do not → don't, is not → isn't, cannot → can't
en.contrast: Exceptions: will not → won't; there is no *amn't (use Aren't I? in questions); 's can be is or has, 'd can be would or had; don't contract short positive answers (Yes, I am, not *Yes, I'm); its (possessive) has no apostrophe.
en.example: I'm a student at this school.
en.exampleTranslation: I'm a student at this school.

fr.name: Contractions
fr.meaning: Une contraction réunit deux mots en un seul ; l'apostrophe remplace les lettres supprimées. Elle est normale à l'oral et à l'écrit informel.
fr.formation: I am → I'm, you are → you're, he is / has → he's, we have → we've, I will → I'll, I would / had → I'd ; do not → don't, is not → isn't, cannot → can't
fr.contrast: Exceptions : will not → won't ; pas de *amn't (on dit Aren't I?) ; 's peut être is ou has, 'd peut être would ou had ; pas de contraction dans une réponse courte affirmative (Yes, I am) ; its (possessif) n'a pas d'apostrophe.
fr.example: I'm a student at this school.
fr.exampleTranslation: Je suis élève dans cette école.

zh.name: 第三人称单数 -s 拼写
zh.meaning: 一般现在时中，主语是第三人称单数时动词要加词尾：一般加 -s；以 s、sh、ch、x、z、o 结尾加 -es；辅音字母 + y 结尾，变 y 为 i 再加 -es。
zh.formation: work → works，play → plays；watch → watches，fix → fixes，go → goes；study → studies，fly → flies
zh.contrast: 例外：have → has，be → is；元音字母 + y 只加 -s（play → plays，buy → buys）；can、must 等情态动词不加 -s（She can swim）。
zh.example: She watches a movie every weekend.
zh.exampleTranslation: 她每个周末看一部电影。

en.name: Third person -s spelling
en.meaning: In the present simple, a verb after he, she or it takes an ending: usually -s; -es after s, sh, ch, x, z or o; consonant + y becomes -ies.
en.formation: work → works, play → plays; watch → watches, fix → fixes, go → goes; study → studies, fly → flies
en.contrast: Exceptions: have → has, be → is; vowel + y just adds -s (play → plays, buy → buys); modals like can and must never take -s (She can swim).
en.example: She watches a movie every weekend.
en.exampleTranslation: She watches a movie every weekend.

fr.name: Orthographe du -s (3e pers.)
fr.meaning: Au présent simple, après he, she ou it, le verbe prend une terminaison : en général -s ; -es après s, sh, ch, x, z ou o ; consonne + y devient -ies.
fr.formation: work → works, play → plays ; watch → watches, fix → fixes, go → goes ; study → studies, fly → flies
fr.contrast: Exceptions : have → has, be → is ; voyelle + y prend seulement -s (play → plays, buy → buys) ; les modaux comme can et must ne prennent jamais de -s (She can swim).
fr.example: She watches a movie every weekend.
fr.exampleTranslation: Elle regarde un film chaque week-end.

zh.name: 不规则复数名词
zh.meaning: 有些名词的复数不加 -s，而是改变元音或用特殊形式，需要单独记忆。
zh.formation: man → men，woman → women，child → children，foot → feet，tooth → teeth，mouse → mice，person → people
zh.contrast: 单复同形：sheep, fish, deer；people 本身是复数（People are friendly，不说 *People is）；-f / -fe 常变 -ves（knife → knives，leaf → leaves），但 roof → roofs。不规则复数后不再加 -s（*childrens）。
zh.example: The children are playing in the park.
zh.exampleTranslation: 孩子们正在公园里玩。

en.name: Irregular plural nouns
en.meaning: Some nouns don't add -s in the plural; they change a vowel or use a special form, which must be learned.
en.formation: man → men, woman → women, child → children, foot → feet, tooth → teeth, mouse → mice, person → people
en.contrast: Same form: sheep, fish, deer. People is plural (People are friendly, not *People is). -f / -fe often becomes -ves (knife → knives, leaf → leaves), but roof → roofs. Never add -s to an irregular plural (*childrens).
en.example: The children are playing in the park.
en.exampleTranslation: The children are playing in the park.

fr.name: Pluriels irréguliers
fr.meaning: Certains noms ne prennent pas -s au pluriel : ils changent de voyelle ou ont une forme spéciale, à apprendre par cœur.
fr.formation: man → men, woman → women, child → children, foot → feet, tooth → teeth, mouse → mice, person → people
fr.contrast: Forme identique : sheep, fish, deer. People est pluriel (People are friendly). -f / -fe devient souvent -ves (knife → knives, leaf → leaves), mais roof → roofs. Pas de -s en plus : *childrens.
fr.example: The children are playing in the park.
fr.exampleTranslation: Les enfants jouent dans le parc.

zh.name: -ing 形式拼写
zh.meaning: 加 -ing 的规则：一般直接加 -ing；以不发音的 e 结尾，去 e 加 -ing；以“单个元音字母 + 单个辅音字母”结尾的重读音节，双写辅音再加 -ing。
zh.formation: play → playing；make → making，dance → dancing；run → running，sit → sitting
zh.contrast: 例外：以 -ee、-ye 结尾的词保留 e（seeing）；-ie 变 -ying（lie → lying）；两个元音后或以 w、x、y 结尾不双写（raining, fixing, playing）。
zh.example: I am making a cake for my mom.
zh.exampleTranslation: 我正在给妈妈做一个蛋糕。

en.name: -ing spelling rules
en.meaning: Usually just add -ing. Drop a silent -e (make → making). Double a single final consonant after a single stressed vowel (run → running).
en.formation: play → playing; make → making, dance → dancing; run → running, sit → sitting
en.contrast: Exceptions: keep the e in -ee and -ye words (seeing); -ie becomes -ying (lie → lying); no doubling after two vowels or after w, x, y (raining, fixing, playing).
en.example: I am making a cake for my mom.
en.exampleTranslation: I am making a cake for my mom.

fr.name: Orthographe en -ing
fr.meaning: En général, on ajoute -ing. On supprime le e muet (make → making). On double la consonne finale précédée d'une seule voyelle accentuée (run → running).
fr.formation: play → playing ; make → making, dance → dancing ; run → running, sit → sitting
fr.contrast: Exceptions : on garde le e des mots en -ee et -ye (seeing) ; -ie devient -ying (lie → lying) ; pas de consonne doublée après deux voyelles ni après w, x, y (raining, fixing, playing).
fr.example: I am making a cake for my mom.
fr.exampleTranslation: Je suis en train de préparer un gâteau pour ma mère.

zh.name: -ed 拼写规则
zh.meaning: 规则动词变过去式和过去分词：一般加 -ed；以 e 结尾只加 -d；辅音字母 + y 结尾变 y 为 i 加 -ed；以“单个元音字母 + 单个辅音字母”结尾的重读音节，双写辅音再加 -ed。
zh.formation: walk → walked；live → lived；study → studied；stop → stopped，plan → planned
zh.contrast: 例外：元音字母 + y 直接加 -ed（play → played）；以 w、x、y 结尾不双写（fix → fixed）；最后音节不重读不双写（visit → visited，open → opened）；英式 travel → travelled，美式 traveled。
zh.example: He stopped the car at the red light.
zh.exampleTranslation: 他在红灯前停下了车。

en.name: -ed spelling rules
en.meaning: Regular verbs add -ed for the past. Add only -d after -e; change consonant + y to -ied; double a single final consonant after a single stressed vowel.
en.formation: walk → walked; live → lived; study → studied; stop → stopped, plan → planned
en.contrast: Exceptions: vowel + y just adds -ed (play → played); no doubling after w, x or y (fix → fixed) or when the last syllable is unstressed (visit → visited, open → opened); British travelled, American traveled.
en.example: He stopped the car at the red light.
en.exampleTranslation: He stopped the car at the red light.

fr.name: Orthographe en -ed
fr.meaning: Les verbes réguliers prennent -ed au passé. Après un -e, on ajoute seulement -d ; consonne + y devient -ied ; on double la consonne finale précédée d'une seule voyelle accentuée.
fr.formation: walk → walked ; live → lived ; study → studied ; stop → stopped, plan → planned
fr.contrast: Exceptions : voyelle + y prend simplement -ed (play → played) ; pas de doublement après w, x ou y (fix → fixed), ni si la dernière syllabe n'est pas accentuée (visit → visited, open → opened) ; travelled (GB), traveled (US).
fr.example: He stopped the car at the red light.
fr.exampleTranslation: Il a arrêté la voiture au feu rouge.

zh.name: some 和 any
zh.meaning: some 和 any 表示“一些”，用在复数名词和不可数名词前：some 主要用于肯定句，any 主要用于否定句和疑问句。
zh.formation: 肯定：some + 复数 / 不可数名词（I have some apples）；否定：not … any（There isn't any milk）；疑问：Are there any eggs?；请求和提供东西时用 some：Would you like some tea?
zh.contrast: 请求或提供东西时，疑问句也用 some：Can I have some water?。肯定句中的 any 意思是“随便哪个都行”：Take any book you like。no = not any：There's no milk。
zh.example: There isn't any milk, but there are some eggs.
zh.exampleTranslation: 没有牛奶了，不过还有一些鸡蛋。

en.name: Some and any
en.meaning: Some and any mean an amount or number that is not exact, with plural and uncountable nouns: some mainly in positive sentences, any in negatives and questions.
en.formation: positive: some + plural / uncountable noun (I have some apples); negative: not … any (There isn't any milk); question: Are there any eggs?; offers and requests use some: Would you like some tea?
en.contrast: In offers and requests, use some even in questions: Can I have some water? Any in a positive sentence means 'it doesn't matter which': Take any book you like. No = not any: There's no milk.
en.example: There isn't any milk, but there are some eggs.
en.exampleTranslation: There isn't any milk, but there are some eggs.

fr.name: Some et any
fr.meaning: Some et any expriment une quantité non précise (« du, de la, des ») avec un nom pluriel ou indénombrable : some surtout à l'affirmative, any dans les négations et les questions.
fr.formation: affirmatif : some + nom pluriel / indénombrable (I have some apples) ; négatif : not … any (There isn't any milk) ; question : Are there any eggs? ; pour offrir ou demander : Would you like some tea?
fr.contrast: « Du, de la, des » ne se traduit pas toujours : I bought (some) bread. « Pas de » = not any ou no : There isn't any milk = There's no milk. Pour une offre, some même dans une question : Would you like some tea?
fr.example: There isn't any milk, but there are some eggs.
fr.exampleTranslation: Il n'y a pas de lait, mais il y a des œufs.

aliases: mine yours his hers ours theirs

zh.name: 名词性物主代词
zh.meaning: 名词性物主代词（mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs）相当于“物主词 + 名词”，单独使用，后面不接名词。
zh.formation: mine / yours / his / hers / ours / theirs（This book is mine = This is my book）；a friend of mine
zh.contrast: 形容词性物主代词后面要接名词（my book），名词性物主代词单独用（The book is mine），不说 *The book is my。这些词没有撇号：yours，不写 *your's。
zh.example: That blue jacket on the chair is mine.
zh.exampleTranslation: 椅子上那件蓝色夹克是我的。

en.name: Possessive pronouns
en.meaning: Possessive pronouns (mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs) replace a possessive adjective + noun and stand alone.
en.formation: mine / yours / his / hers / ours / theirs (This book is mine = This is my book); a friend of mine
en.contrast: Possessive adjectives need a noun (my book); possessive pronouns stand alone (The book is mine, not *The book is my). They never take an apostrophe: yours, not *your's.
en.example: That blue jacket on the chair is mine.
en.exampleTranslation: That blue jacket on the chair is mine.

fr.name: Pronoms possessifs
fr.meaning: Les pronoms possessifs (mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs) remplacent un adjectif possessif + nom et s'emploient seuls.
fr.formation: mine / yours / his / hers / ours / theirs (This book is mine = This is my book) ; a friend of mine (un de mes amis)
fr.contrast: Pas d'article comme dans « le mien » : It's mine, et non *It's the mine. His ou hers dépend du possesseur : c'est le sien → it's his (à lui) / it's hers (à elle).
fr.example: That blue jacket on the chair is mine.
fr.exampleTranslation: Cette veste bleue sur la chaise est à moi.

zh.name: 过去进行时
zh.meaning: 过去进行时表示过去某一时刻或某段时间正在进行的动作，常用来描写背景。
zh.formation: I / he / she / it was + 动词-ing；you / we / they were + 动词-ing；否定：wasn't / weren't + -ing；疑问：Were you sleeping?
zh.contrast: 一般过去时表示完整、已结束的动作：I read a book last night（读了）/ I was reading at eight（八点时正在读）。know、want 等状态动词不用进行时：I knew him，不说 *I was knowing him。
zh.example: At eight last night, I was reading a book.
zh.exampleTranslation: 昨晚八点时，我正在看书。

en.name: Past continuous
en.meaning: The past continuous describes an action in progress at a moment or during a period in the past. It often sets the background.
en.formation: I / he / she / it was + verb-ing; you / we / they were + verb-ing; negative: wasn't / weren't + -ing; question: Were you sleeping?
en.contrast: The past simple shows a complete, finished action: I read a book last night (finished) vs I was reading at eight (in progress then). State verbs aren't continuous: I knew him, not *I was knowing him.
en.example: At eight last night, I was reading a book.
en.exampleTranslation: At eight last night, I was reading a book.

fr.name: Passé continu
fr.meaning: Le passé continu décrit une action en cours à un moment ou pendant une période du passé. Il sert souvent à planter le décor.
fr.formation: I / he / she / it was + verbe-ing ; you / we / they were + verbe-ing ; négation : wasn't / weren't + -ing ; question : Were you sleeping?
fr.contrast: L'imparfait ne se traduit pas toujours par was + -ing : pour un état ou une habitude, on emploie le prétérit ou used to (I lived in Paris = j'habitais à Paris). Was + -ing = « être en train de ».
fr.example: At eight last night, I was reading a book.
fr.exampleTranslation: Hier soir à huit heures, j'étais en train de lire un livre.

aliases: 过去进行时和一般过去时

zh.name: 一般过去时与过去进行时
zh.meaning: 过去进行时描写正在进行的较长动作（背景），一般过去时表示其间发生的较短动作。
zh.formation: while + 过去进行时（While I was cooking, the phone rang）；when + 一般过去时（I was cooking when the phone rang）
zh.contrast: 两个动词都用一般过去时，表示先后发生：When she arrived, we ate（她到了以后我们才吃）；用过去进行时表示当时正在进行：When she arrived, we were eating（她到的时候我们正在吃）。
zh.example: My phone rang while I was cooking dinner.
zh.exampleTranslation: 我正在做晚饭时，我的电话响了。

en.name: Past simple and continuous
en.meaning: The past continuous gives a longer action in progress (the background); the past simple gives a shorter action that happened during it.
en.formation: while + past continuous (While I was cooking, the phone rang); when + past simple (I was cooking when the phone rang)
en.contrast: Two past simple verbs show a sequence: When she arrived, we ate (we ate after). With the past continuous, the action was already in progress: When she arrived, we were eating.
en.example: My phone rang while I was cooking dinner.
en.exampleTranslation: My phone rang while I was cooking dinner.

fr.name: Prétérit et passé continu
fr.meaning: Le passé continu décrit l'action longue en cours (le décor) ; le prétérit, l'action courte qui survient pendant ce temps.
fr.formation: while + passé continu (While I was cooking, the phone rang) ; when + prétérit (I was cooking when the phone rang)
fr.contrast: C'est l'opposition imparfait / passé composé : When she arrived, we were eating (nous mangions quand elle est arrivée). Deux prétérits indiquent une succession : When she arrived, we ate (nous avons mangé après).
fr.example: My phone rang while I was cooking dinner.
fr.exampleTranslation: Mon téléphone a sonné pendant que je préparais le dîner.

zh.name: 现在完成时（经历）
zh.meaning: 现在完成时可以表示到现在为止的人生经历，不说具体时间，常和 ever、never、before、… times 连用。
zh.formation: have / has + 过去分词（I have been to Japan. / Have you ever eaten sushi? / I've never seen snow.）
zh.contrast: 说出具体的过去时间要用一般过去时：I went to Japan in 2019，不说 *I have been to Japan in 2019。have been to 表示去过（已回来），have gone to 表示去了（还在那里）。
zh.example: She has visited three different countries in Europe.
zh.exampleTranslation: 她去过欧洲的三个国家。

en.name: Present perfect: experiences
en.meaning: The present perfect can talk about life experiences up to now, without saying when. It is common with ever, never, before and … times.
en.formation: have / has + past participle (I have been to Japan. / Have you ever eaten sushi? / I've never seen snow.)
en.contrast: With a specific past time, use the past simple: I went to Japan in 2019, not *I have been to Japan in 2019. Have been to = went and came back; have gone to = is there now.
en.example: She has visited three different countries in Europe.
en.exampleTranslation: She has visited three different countries in Europe.

fr.name: Present perfect (expérience)
fr.meaning: Le present perfect peut exprimer une expérience vécue jusqu'à maintenant, sans dire quand. Il s'emploie souvent avec ever, never, before ou … times.
fr.formation: have / has + participe passé (I have been to Japan. / Have you ever eaten sushi? / I've never seen snow.)
fr.contrast: Le passé composé se traduit par le prétérit dès qu'un moment passé est précisé : I went to Japan in 2019, et non *I have been to Japan in 2019. Have been to = y être allé (et revenu) ; have gone to = y être parti.
fr.example: She has visited three different countries in Europe.
fr.exampleTranslation: Elle a visité trois pays d'Europe.

points.pattern: present perfect with just, already, yet
aliases: 现在完成时 刚刚 已经

zh.name: 现在完成时与时间副词
zh.meaning: 现在完成时常和 just（刚刚）、already（已经）、yet（还、已经）连用，表示动作刚完成、已完成或还没完成，强调对现在的影响。
zh.formation: have / has + just / already + 过去分词（I've just eaten）；yet 放在否定句和疑问句句末（Have you finished yet? / I haven't finished yet）
zh.contrast: already 用于肯定句，yet 用于否定句和疑问句，放在句末：I haven't finished yet，不说 *I haven't already finished。just now（刚才）要用一般过去时：I saw him just now。
zh.example: I have already finished my homework, so I can play games.
zh.exampleTranslation: 我已经写完作业了，所以可以玩游戏。

en.name: Present perfect: just, already, yet
en.meaning: The present perfect is often used with just, already and yet to say that something has recently finished, has finished earlier than expected, or hasn't happened.
en.formation: have / has + just / already + past participle (I've just eaten); yet at the end of negatives and questions (Have you finished yet? / I haven't finished yet)
en.contrast: Already is for positive sentences; yet is for negatives and questions, at the end: I haven't finished yet, not *I haven't finished already. Just now (a moment ago) takes the past simple: I saw him just now.
en.example: I have already finished my homework, so I can play games.
en.exampleTranslation: I have already finished my homework, so I can play games.

fr.name: Just, already et yet
fr.meaning: Le present perfect s'emploie souvent avec just, already et yet pour dire qu'une action vient de se terminer, est déjà faite, ou ne l'est pas encore.
fr.formation: have / has + just / already + participe passé (I've just eaten) ; yet en fin de phrase négative ou interrogative (Have you finished yet? / I haven't finished yet)
fr.contrast: Already (déjà) s'emploie à l'affirmative ; yet dans les questions et les négations, en fin de phrase : Have you eaten yet? / I haven't eaten yet. « Venir de » se dit have just + participe : I've just eaten (je viens de manger).
fr.example: I have already finished my homework, so I can play games.
fr.exampleTranslation: J'ai déjà fini mes devoirs, alors je peux jouer aux jeux vidéo.

zh.name: will表将来
zh.meaning: will + 动词原形表示对将来的预测或看法，也用于说话时临时做的决定、提议和承诺。
zh.formation: 主语 + will（'ll）+ 动词原形；否定：won't（will not）；疑问：Will you …?（I'll call you. / It won't be easy.）
zh.contrast: 已经计划好的事用 be going to 或现在进行时：I'm meeting Tom tonight。will 用于看法和临时决定：I think it'll rain / OK, I'll help you。when、if 从句里不用 will：When I get home, I'll call you。
zh.example: I think it will rain this afternoon, so take an umbrella.
zh.exampleTranslation: 我觉得今天下午会下雨，带把伞吧。

en.name: Will for future
en.meaning: Will + base verb gives predictions and opinions about the future. It is also used for instant decisions, offers and promises.
en.formation: subject + will ('ll) + base verb; negative: won't (will not); question: Will you …? (I'll call you. / It won't be easy.)
en.contrast: For plans and arrangements already made, use be going to or the present continuous: I'm meeting Tom tonight. Will is for opinions and instant decisions: I think it'll rain / OK, I'll help you. No will after when or if: When I get home, I'll call you.
en.example: I think it will rain this afternoon, so take an umbrella.
en.exampleTranslation: I think it will rain this afternoon, so take an umbrella.

fr.name: Futur avec will
fr.meaning: Will + base verbale exprime une prédiction ou une opinion sur l'avenir, ainsi qu'une décision prise sur le moment, une offre ou une promesse.
fr.formation: sujet + will ('ll) + base verbale ; négation : won't (will not) ; question : Will you …? (I'll call you. / It won't be easy.)
fr.contrast: Le futur simple ne se traduit pas toujours par will : pour un projet déjà décidé, on dit be going to ou le présent continu (I'm meeting Tom tonight). Après when, pas de will : When I get home, I'll call you (quand je rentrerai).
fr.example: I think it will rain this afternoon, so take an umbrella.
fr.exampleTranslation: Je pense qu'il va pleuvoir cet après-midi, alors prends un parapluie.

zh.name: 第一条件句
zh.meaning: 第一条件句表示将来有可能发生的情况及其可能的结果。
zh.formation: If + 一般现在时, will + 动词原形（If it rains, we'll stay home）；if 从句也可以放在后面：We'll stay home if it rains
zh.contrast: if 从句用一般现在时，不用 will：If it rains，不说 *If it will rain。如果情况不太可能发生或只是想象，用第二条件句：If I had a car, I would drive。
zh.example: If you study hard, you will pass the exam easily.
zh.exampleTranslation: 如果你努力学习，你就会轻松通过考试。

en.name: First conditional
en.meaning: The first conditional talks about a possible future situation and its likely result.
en.formation: If + present simple, will + base verb (If it rains, we'll stay home); the if-clause can come second: We'll stay home if it rains
en.contrast: Use the present simple, not will, in the if-clause: If it rains, not *If it will rain. For unlikely or imaginary situations, use the second conditional: If I had a car, I would drive.
en.example: If you study hard, you will pass the exam easily.
en.exampleTranslation: If you study hard, you will pass the exam easily.

fr.name: Premier conditionnel
fr.meaning: Le premier conditionnel exprime une situation future possible et sa conséquence probable.
fr.formation: If + présent simple, will + base verbale (If it rains, we'll stay home) ; la proposition en if peut venir en second : We'll stay home if it rains
fr.contrast: Comme en français (« si + présent, futur »), pas de will après if : If it rains, et non *If it will rain. Pour une situation peu probable ou imaginaire, on emploie le second conditionnel : If I had a car, I would drive.
fr.example: If you study hard, you will pass the exam easily.
fr.exampleTranslation: Si tu travailles bien, tu réussiras l'examen facilement.

zh.name: should表建议
zh.meaning: should / shouldn't 用来提建议，或说明什么是正确、合适的做法。
zh.formation: 主语 + should / shouldn't + 动词原形（You should rest.）；征求建议：Should I call her? / What should I do?
zh.contrast: should 只是建议，语气比 must 轻得多：You should see a doctor（建议）/ You must stop here（规定，必须）。should 后面不加 to：You should go，不说 *You should to go。
zh.example: You should drink more water when you have a cold.
zh.exampleTranslation: 你感冒的时候应该多喝水。

en.name: Should for advice
en.meaning: Should / shouldn't give advice or say what is right or a good idea.
en.formation: subject + should / shouldn't + base verb (You should rest.); asking for advice: Should I call her? / What should I do?
en.contrast: Should is only advice and is much weaker than must: You should see a doctor (advice) vs You must stop here (rule). No to after should: You should go, not *You should to go.
en.example: You should drink more water when you have a cold.
en.exampleTranslation: You should drink more water when you have a cold.

fr.name: Should pour les conseils
fr.meaning: Should / shouldn't servent à donner un conseil ou à dire ce qu'il est bon de faire, comme « tu devrais ».
fr.formation: sujet + should / shouldn't + base verbale (You should rest.) ; demander conseil : Should I call her? / What should I do?
fr.contrast: Should (tu devrais) est un conseil, beaucoup plus faible que must (tu dois) : You should see a doctor / You must stop here. Pas de to après should : You should go.
fr.example: You should drink more water when you have a cold.
fr.exampleTranslation: Tu devrais boire plus d'eau quand tu as un rhume.

points.pattern: must and mustn't for obligation and prohibition

zh.name: must表义务和禁止
zh.meaning: must 表示必须（规定，或说话人认为很重要的事），mustn't 表示禁止、不允许。
zh.formation: 主语 + must / mustn't + 动词原形（You must wear a seatbelt. / You mustn't smoke here.）
zh.contrast: must 没有过去式，过去的义务用 had to：I had to work yesterday。mustn't（禁止）和 don't have to（不必）意思完全不同。
zh.example: Visitors must turn off their phones inside the museum.
zh.exampleTranslation: 参观者必须在博物馆内关闭手机。

en.name: Must and mustn't
en.meaning: Must expresses a strong obligation (a rule, or something the speaker feels is important); mustn't means something is not allowed.
en.formation: subject + must / mustn't + base verb (You must wear a seatbelt. / You mustn't smoke here.)
en.contrast: Must has no past form; for past obligation use had to: I had to work yesterday. Mustn't (not allowed) is very different from don't have to (not necessary).
en.example: Visitors must turn off their phones inside the museum.
en.exampleTranslation: Visitors must turn off their phones inside the museum.

fr.name: Must et mustn't
fr.meaning: Must exprime une obligation forte (une règle, ou ce que le locuteur juge important) ; mustn't exprime une interdiction.
fr.formation: sujet + must / mustn't + base verbale (You must wear a seatbelt. / You mustn't smoke here.)
fr.contrast: Must n'a pas de passé : on dit had to (I had to work yesterday, j'ai dû travailler). Attention : mustn't = il ne faut pas (interdit), alors que don't have to = ce n'est pas nécessaire.
fr.example: Visitors must turn off their phones inside the museum.
fr.exampleTranslation: Les visiteurs doivent éteindre leur téléphone à l'intérieur du musée.

points.pattern: have to and don't have to for obligation

zh.name: have to 表示必须
zh.meaning: have to 表示因规定或客观情况而必须做某事；don't have to 表示“不必、没有必要”。
zh.formation: 主语 + have to / has to + 动词原形；否定：don't / doesn't have to；疑问：Do you have to …?；过去：had to
zh.contrast: don't have to 表示“不必”，mustn't 表示“禁止”：You don't have to come（可以不来）/ You mustn't come（不准来）。have to 可用于各种时态：had to, will have to。
zh.example: We have to wear a uniform at school every Monday.
zh.exampleTranslation: 我们每周一在学校都必须穿校服。

en.name: Have to (obligation)
en.meaning: Have to means something is necessary because of rules or circumstances; don't have to means it is not necessary.
en.formation: subject + have to / has to + base verb; negative: don't / doesn't have to; question: Do you have to …?; past: had to
en.contrast: Don't have to means 'not necessary', mustn't means 'not allowed': You don't have to come (you can choose) vs You mustn't come (it's forbidden). Have to works in all tenses: had to, will have to.
en.example: We have to wear a uniform at school every Monday.
en.exampleTranslation: We have to wear a uniform at school every Monday.

fr.name: Have to (obligation)
fr.meaning: Have to exprime une obligation due à une règle ou aux circonstances ; don't have to signifie que ce n'est pas nécessaire.
fr.formation: sujet + have to / has to + base verbale ; négation : don't / doesn't have to ; question : Do you have to …? ; passé : had to
fr.contrast: Don't have to = ce n'est pas obligatoire, mustn't = c'est interdit : You don't have to come (tu n'es pas obligé de venir) / You mustn't come (tu ne dois pas venir). Have to existe à tous les temps : had to, will have to.
fr.example: We have to wear a uniform at school every Monday.
fr.exampleTranslation: Nous devons porter un uniforme à l'école tous les lundis.

points.pattern: could and couldn't for past ability

zh.name: 过去能力 could
zh.meaning: could / couldn't 表示过去的一般能力，即过去会或不会做某事。
