zh.formation: 主语 + could / couldn't + 动词原形（She could read at four. / I couldn't sleep last night.）
zh.contrast: 过去某一次成功做成某事，用 was able to 或 managed to，不用 could：The door was locked, but I managed to open it。否定 couldn't 两种情况都可以用。
zh.example: I could swim very well when I was ten.
zh.exampleTranslation: 我十岁的时候游泳就游得很好。

en.name: Could for past ability
en.meaning: Could / couldn't describe general abilities someone had, or didn't have, in the past.
en.formation: subject + could / couldn't + base verb (She could read at four. / I couldn't sleep last night.)
en.contrast: For one specific success in the past, use was able to or managed to, not could: The door was locked, but I managed to open it. Couldn't works in both cases.
en.example: I could swim very well when I was ten.
en.exampleTranslation: I could swim very well when I was ten.

fr.name: Could pour la capacité passée
fr.meaning: Could / couldn't expriment une capacité générale qu'on avait, ou non, dans le passé (« je savais / je pouvais »).
fr.formation: sujet + could / couldn't + base verbale (She could read at four. / I couldn't sleep last night.)
fr.contrast: Pour une réussite ponctuelle (« j'ai réussi à »), on dit was able to ou managed to, pas could : The door was locked, but I managed to open it. Couldn't convient dans les deux cas.
fr.example: I could swim very well when I was ten.
fr.exampleTranslation: Je savais très bien nager quand j'avais dix ans.

zh.name: 目的不定式
zh.meaning: 用 to + 动词原形说明做某事的目的，相当于“为了……”。
zh.formation: 动作 + to + 动词原形（I went to the shop to buy milk）；更正式：in order to；否定目的：so as not to / in order not to
zh.contrast: 表示目的不用 for + 动词：I came here to study，不说 *for study / *for to study。for 后面接名词：I went out for some milk。
zh.example: She went to the shop to buy some milk.
zh.exampleTranslation: 她去商店买了些牛奶。

en.name: Infinitive of purpose
en.meaning: To + base verb explains why someone does something; it means 'in order to'.
en.formation: action + to + base verb (I went to the shop to buy milk); more formal: in order to; negative purpose: so as not to / in order not to
en.contrast: Don't use for + verb for purpose: I came here to study, not *for study or *for to study. For goes with a noun: I went out for some milk.
en.example: She went to the shop to buy some milk.
en.exampleTranslation: She went to the shop to buy some milk.

fr.name: Infinitif de but
fr.meaning: To + base verbale explique pourquoi on fait une action ; c'est l'équivalent de « pour + infinitif ».
fr.formation: action + to + base verbale (I went to the shop to buy milk) ; plus formel : in order to ; but négatif : so as not to / in order not to
fr.contrast: « Pour + infinitif » se dit to + verbe, et non *for + verbe : I came here to study, et non *for study. For s'emploie devant un nom : I went out for some milk (pour acheter du lait).
fr.example: She went to the shop to buy some milk.
fr.exampleTranslation: Elle est allée au magasin pour acheter du lait.

zh.name: 动词 + to 不定式
zh.meaning: want、hope、decide、plan、need、learn、agree、promise、refuse 等动词后面接另一个动词时，要用 to + 动词原形。
zh.formation: 动词 + to + 动词原形（I want to go. / She decided to stay.）；否定：动词 + not to（He promised not to be late）
zh.contrast: enjoy、finish、mind、avoid 等动词后面要用 -ing：I enjoy reading，不说 *I enjoy to read。to 不能省略：I want to go，不说 *I want go。
zh.example: He wants to learn Spanish this year.
zh.exampleTranslation: 他今年想学西班牙语。

en.name: Verbs + to-infinitive
en.meaning: Verbs such as want, hope, decide, plan, need, learn, agree, promise and refuse take to + base verb when another verb follows.
en.formation: verb + to + base verb (I want to go. / She decided to stay.); negative: verb + not to (He promised not to be late)
en.contrast: Verbs like enjoy, finish, mind and avoid take -ing instead: I enjoy reading, not *I enjoy to read. Don't drop to: I want to go, not *I want go.
en.example: He wants to learn Spanish this year.
en.exampleTranslation: He wants to learn Spanish this year.

fr.name: Verbes + to + infinitif
fr.meaning: Des verbes comme want, hope, decide, plan, need, learn, agree, promise et refuse sont suivis de to + base verbale quand un autre verbe suit.
fr.formation: verbe + to + base verbale (I want to go. / She decided to stay.) ; négation : verbe + not to (He promised not to be late)
fr.contrast: Le « de » français (décider de, refuser de) se traduit par to : She decided to stay. Mais enjoy, finish, mind, avoid prennent -ing : I enjoy reading, et non *I enjoy to read.
fr.example: He wants to learn Spanish this year.
fr.exampleTranslation: Il veut apprendre l'espagnol cette année.

zh.name: 动词 + -ing
zh.meaning: enjoy、finish、mind、avoid、keep、practise、suggest、can't stand 等动词后面接另一个动词时，要用 -ing 形式。
zh.formation: 动词 + 动词-ing（They enjoy playing tennis. / Do you mind waiting?）；否定：动词 + not + -ing（I suggest not going）
zh.contrast: want、decide、hope 等动词后面用 to + 动词原形。look forward to 里的 to 是介词，后面要用 -ing：I look forward to seeing you，不说 *to see you。
zh.example: They enjoy playing tennis on Sundays.
zh.exampleTranslation: 他们喜欢在星期天打网球。

en.name: Verbs followed by -ing
en.meaning: Verbs such as enjoy, finish, mind, avoid, keep, practise, suggest and can't stand take an -ing form when another verb follows.
en.formation: verb + verb-ing (They enjoy playing tennis. / Do you mind waiting?); negative: verb + not + -ing (I suggest not going)
en.contrast: Verbs like want, decide and hope take to + base verb. In look forward to, to is a preposition, so -ing follows: I look forward to seeing you, not *to see you.
en.example: They enjoy playing tennis on Sundays.
en.exampleTranslation: They enjoy playing tennis on Sundays.

fr.name: Verbes suivis de -ing
fr.meaning: Des verbes comme enjoy, finish, mind, avoid, keep, practise, suggest et can't stand sont suivis d'une forme en -ing quand un autre verbe suit.
fr.formation: verbe + verbe-ing (They enjoy playing tennis. / Do you mind waiting?) ; négation : verbe + not + -ing (I suggest not going)
fr.contrast: L'infinitif français devient -ing après ces verbes : J'ai fini de manger = I finished eating, et non *I finished to eat. Dans look forward to, to est une préposition : I look forward to seeing you.
fr.example: They enjoy playing tennis on Sundays.
fr.exampleTranslation: Ils aiment jouer au tennis le dimanche.

zh.name: 限制性定语从句
zh.meaning: 限制性定语从句放在名词后面，用 who（人）、which（物）或 that（人或物）引导，说明指的是哪一个人或物。
zh.formation: 名词 + who / which / that + 从句（The man who lives next door …）；关系词作宾语时可省略：the book (that) I bought
zh.contrast: 英语定语从句放在名词后面，不像中文放在前面。从句里不要重复代词：the man who lives here，不说 *the man who he lives here。用逗号隔开的补充说明是非限制性从句，不能用 that。
zh.example: The man who lives next door is a doctor.
zh.exampleTranslation: 住在隔壁的那位男士是个医生。

en.name: Defining relative clauses
en.meaning: A defining relative clause comes after a noun and tells us which person or thing we mean. Use who for people, which for things, and that for both.
en.formation: noun + who / which / that + clause (The man who lives next door …); when it is the object, the pronoun can be dropped: the book (that) I bought
en.contrast: Don't repeat a pronoun inside the clause: the man who lives here, not *the man who he lives here. Clauses between commas that add extra information are non-defining and can't use that.
en.example: The man who lives next door is a doctor.
en.exampleTranslation: The man who lives next door is a doctor.

fr.name: Relatives déterminatives
fr.meaning: La relative déterminative suit le nom et précise de quelle personne ou chose on parle : who pour les personnes, which pour les choses, that pour les deux.
fr.formation: nom + who / which / that + proposition (The man who lives next door …) ; s'il est complément, le pronom peut disparaître : the book (that) I bought
fr.contrast: « Qui » et « que » ne correspondent pas à who et which : on choisit selon personne ou chose. Le pronom complément peut être omis (the book I bought = le livre que j'ai acheté), ce qui est impossible en français.
fr.example: The man who lives next door is a doctor.
fr.exampleTranslation: L'homme qui habite à côté est médecin.

zh.name: where 引导的定语从句
zh.meaning: where 引导的定语从句修饰表示地点的名词，相当于 in which / at which。
zh.formation: 地点名词 + where + 主语 + 动词（the park where we met / the town where I grew up）
zh.contrast: 从句里缺主语或宾语时不用 where，要用 which / that：the city (that) I visited，不说 *the city where I visited；但 the city where I live（live 后不缺宾语）。
zh.example: This is the park where we first met.
zh.exampleTranslation: 这就是我们初次相遇的公园。

en.name: Relative clauses with where
en.meaning: A where clause describes a place noun; where means 'in which' or 'at which'.
en.formation: place noun + where + subject + verb (the park where we met / the town where I grew up)
en.contrast: If the clause needs a subject or object, use which/that, not where: the city (that) I visited, not *the city where I visited — but the city where I live.
en.example: This is the park where we first met.
en.exampleTranslation: This is the park where we first met.

fr.name: Propositions relatives avec where
fr.meaning: Une relative en where décrit un nom de lieu ; where signifie « où », c'est-à-dire « dans lequel / auquel ».
fr.formation: nom de lieu + where + sujet + verbe (the park where we met / the town where I grew up)
fr.contrast: Where ne remplace pas un complément d'objet : the city (that) I visited (la ville que j'ai visitée), et non *the city where I visited. « Le jour où » se dit the day when, pas *the day where.
fr.example: This is the park where we first met.
fr.exampleTranslation: C'est le parc où nous nous sommes rencontrés pour la première fois.

aliases: too much, too many, enough nouns

zh.name: too 和 enough
zh.meaning: too + 形容词表示“太……”（超过需要，结果不好）；形容词 + enough 表示“足够……”。
zh.formation: too + 形容词 (+ to + 动词)（too hot to drink）；形容词 + enough (+ to + 动词)（old enough to drive）；enough + 名词（enough money）
zh.contrast: too 带有否定意味，不等于 very：中文“太好了”是 It's great / very good，不说 *It's too good。enough 放在形容词后面：old enough，不说 *enough old。
zh.example: This coffee is too hot to drink, but that tea is warm enough.
zh.exampleTranslation: 这杯咖啡太烫了，没法喝，但那杯茶温度刚好。

en.name: Too and enough
en.meaning: Too + adjective means more than is right or possible, often with a negative result. Adjective + enough means as much as needed.
en.formation: too + adjective (+ to + verb) (too hot to drink); adjective + enough (+ to + verb) (old enough to drive); enough + noun (enough money)
en.contrast: Too is negative and is not the same as very: It's very hot (just a fact) vs It's too hot to drink (a problem). Enough goes after an adjective: old enough, not *enough old.
en.example: This coffee is too hot to drink, but that tea is warm enough.
en.exampleTranslation: This coffee is too hot to drink, but that tea is warm enough.

fr.name: Too et enough
fr.meaning: Too + adjectif signifie « trop », souvent avec une conséquence négative. Adjectif + enough signifie « assez ».
fr.formation: too + adjectif (+ to + verbe) (too hot to drink) ; adjectif + enough (+ to + verbe) (old enough to drive) ; enough + nom (enough money)
fr.contrast: Contrairement à « assez grand », enough se place après l'adjectif : old enough, et non *enough old. Devant un nom, il se place avant : enough money (assez d'argent).
fr.example: This coffee is too hot to drink, but that tea is warm enough.
fr.exampleTranslation: Ce café est trop chaud pour le boire, mais ce thé est assez chaud.

zh.name: 不定代词
zh.meaning: something、anyone、nobody、everywhere 等不定代词泛指人、物或地点，不具体说明是哪一个；作主语时谓语动词用单数。
zh.formation: some- / any- / no- / every- + -body / -one / -thing / -where；动词用单数：Everyone is here.；形容词放在后面：something interesting
zh.contrast: some- 和 any-：some-（something, someone）用于肯定句和提议；any-（anything, anyone）用于否定句和疑问句；no- 本身就是否定（nothing）。
zh.example: Is there anything interesting in that box on the table?
zh.exampleTranslation: 桌上那个盒子里有什么有趣的东西吗？

en.name: Indefinite Pronouns
en.meaning: Words like something, anyone, nobody and everywhere refer to people, things or places without saying which. As subjects they take a singular verb.
en.formation: some- / any- / no- / every- + -body / -one / -thing / -where; singular verb: Everyone is here.; adjective after: something interesting
en.contrast: some- vs any-: some- (something, someone) is for positive sentences and offers; any- (anything, anyone) is for negatives and questions; no- words (nothing) are already negative.
en.example: Is there anything interesting in that box on the table?
en.exampleTranslation: Is there anything interesting in that box on the table?

fr.name: Pronoms indéfinis
fr.meaning: Des mots comme something, anyone, nobody ou everywhere désignent des personnes, des choses ou des lieux sans préciser lesquels. Sujets, ils prennent un verbe au singulier.
fr.formation: some- / any- / no- / every- + -body / -one / -thing / -where ; verbe au singulier : Everyone is here. ; adjectif après : something interesting
fr.contrast: some- ou any- : some- (something, someone) s'emploie dans les phrases affirmatives et les offres ; any- (anything, anyone) dans les négations et les questions ; les mots en no- (nothing) sont déjà négatifs.
fr.example: Is there anything interesting in that box on the table?
fr.exampleTranslation: Est-ce qu'il y a quelque chose d'intéressant dans cette boîte sur la table ?

zh.name: 方式副词
zh.meaning: 方式副词说明动作“怎么做”，通常由形容词加 -ly 构成，放在动词或宾语后面。
zh.formation: quick → quickly；happy → happily（y 变 i）；gentle → gently（-le 变 -ly）；She speaks English well.
zh.contrast: 例外：good → well，fast → fast，hard → hard（hardly 意为“几乎不”），late → late（lately 意为“最近”）；friendly、lovely 是形容词。副词不放在动词和宾语之间：She speaks English well，不说 *She speaks well English。
zh.example: The little boy smiled happily when he received a new toy.
zh.exampleTranslation: 那个小男孩收到新玩具时开心地笑了。

en.name: Adverbs of manner
en.meaning: Adverbs of manner say how something is done. Most add -ly to an adjective and come after the verb or its object.
en.formation: quick → quickly; happy → happily (y → i); gentle → gently (-le → -ly); She speaks English well.
en.contrast: Exceptions: good → well, fast → fast, hard → hard (hardly means 'almost not'), late → late (lately means 'recently'); friendly and lovely are adjectives. Don't put the adverb between the verb and object: She speaks English well, not *She speaks well English.
en.example: The little boy smiled happily when he received a new toy.
en.exampleTranslation: The little boy smiled happily when he received a new toy.

fr.name: Adverbes de manière
fr.meaning: Les adverbes de manière disent comment on fait quelque chose. La plupart ajoutent -ly à l'adjectif et se placent après le verbe ou son complément.
fr.formation: quick → quickly ; happy → happily (y → i) ; gentle → gently (-le → -ly) ; She speaks English well.
fr.contrast: Exceptions : good → well, fast → fast, hard → hard (hardly = à peine), late → late (lately = récemment) ; friendly et lovely sont des adjectifs. Pas d'adverbe entre le verbe et le complément : She speaks English well, et non *She speaks well English.
fr.example: The little boy smiled happily when he received a new toy.
fr.exampleTranslation: Le petit garçon a souri joyeusement quand il a reçu un nouveau jouet.

zh.name: 一般现在时被动语态
zh.meaning: 一般现在时被动语态表示主语是动作的承受者，用于经常发生的事或事实，重点在动作对象而不在执行者。
zh.formation: am / is / are + 过去分词（English is spoken here. / The rooms are cleaned every day.）；需要说明执行者时用 by
zh.contrast: 被动语态不能漏掉 be：Vegetables are sold here，不说 *Vegetables sold here。happen、arrive 等不及物动词没有被动：It happened，不说 *It was happened。
zh.example: Fresh vegetables are sold at the market every morning.
zh.exampleTranslation: 每天早上市场上都有新鲜蔬菜出售。

en.name: Present simple passive
en.meaning: The present simple passive makes the receiver of the action the subject. It is used for regular actions and facts when the doer is unknown or unimportant.
en.formation: am / is / are + past participle (English is spoken here. / The rooms are cleaned every day.); add by + doer only if needed
en.contrast: Don't leave out be: Vegetables are sold here, not *Vegetables sold here. Verbs with no object, like happen and arrive, have no passive: It happened, not *It was happened.
en.example: Fresh vegetables are sold at the market every morning.
en.exampleTranslation: Fresh vegetables are sold at the market every morning.

fr.name: Passif au présent simple
fr.meaning: Le passif au présent simple fait du sujet celui qui subit l'action. On l'emploie pour des faits ou des actions habituelles quand l'auteur est inconnu ou peu important.
fr.formation: am / is / are + participe passé (English is spoken here. / The rooms are cleaned every day.) ; by + auteur seulement si nécessaire
fr.contrast: Le français emploie souvent « on » là où l'anglais met un passif : On parle anglais ici = English is spoken here. Pas de passif avec happen ou arrive : It happened, et non *It was happened.
fr.example: Fresh vegetables are sold at the market every morning.
fr.exampleTranslation: Des légumes frais sont vendus au marché tous les matins.

zh.name: 一般过去时被动语态
zh.meaning: 一般过去时被动语态表示主语在过去承受了某个动作，常用于不知道或不必说出执行者的时候。
zh.formation: was / were + 过去分词（The window was broken. / These houses were built in 1990.）；+ by + 执行者
zh.contrast: 中文常常不用“被”，英语却要用被动：这座桥是 1900 年建的 = The bridge was built in 1900，不说 *The bridge built in 1900。执行者重要时才加 by。
zh.example: The old wooden bridge was built by local farmers last year.
zh.exampleTranslation: 这座古老的木桥是当地农民去年建造的。

en.name: Past simple passive
en.meaning: The past simple passive says what was done to the subject in the past, often when the doer is unknown or unimportant.
en.formation: was / were + past participle (The window was broken. / These houses were built in 1990.); + by + doer
en.contrast: Don't drop be: The bridge was built in 1900, not *The bridge built in 1900. Add by + doer only when it matters. Common examples: I was born in…, It was invented by…
en.example: The old wooden bridge was built by local farmers last year.
en.exampleTranslation: The old wooden bridge was built by local farmers last year.

fr.name: Passif au prétérit
fr.meaning: Le passif au prétérit indique ce que le sujet a subi dans le passé, souvent quand l'auteur est inconnu ou peu important.
fr.formation: was / were + participe passé (The window was broken. / These houses were built in 1990.) ; + by + auteur
fr.contrast: « A été construit » se dit was built (prétérit), sauf lien avec le présent (has been built). « On m'a volé mon vélo » se dit My bike was stolen.
fr.example: The old wooden bridge was built by local farmers last year.
fr.exampleTranslation: Le vieux pont en bois a été construit par des agriculteurs du coin l'an dernier.

points.pattern: a few, a little, few, little
aliases: a few a little some any
some any a few a little

zh.name: a few 和 a little
zh.meaning: a few（+ 可数复数）和 a little（+ 不可数）表示“有一些”，语气肯定；few 和 little 不加 a，表示“很少、几乎没有”，语气否定。
zh.formation: a few / few + 可数名词复数（a few friends）；a little / little + 不可数名词（a little time）；常说 very few / very little
zh.contrast: 有没有 a 意思相反：I have a few friends（有几个朋友）/ I have few friends（几乎没有朋友）。a little 修饰形容词时表示“有点儿”：a little tired。
zh.example: I have a few friends here, but very little free time.
zh.exampleTranslation: 我在这里有几个朋友，但空闲时间很少。

en.name: A few / a little
en.meaning: A few (with plural nouns) and a little (with uncountable nouns) mean 'some' and sound positive. Few and little without a mean 'not many / not much' and sound negative.
en.formation: a few / few + plural noun (a few friends); a little / little + uncountable noun (a little time); often very few / very little
en.contrast: The a changes the meaning: I have a few friends (some — good) vs I have few friends (almost none). Before an adjective, a little means 'slightly': a little tired.
en.example: I have a few friends here, but very little free time.
en.exampleTranslation: I have a few friends here, but very little free time.

fr.name: A few / a little
fr.meaning: A few (nom pluriel) et a little (nom indénombrable) signifient « quelques / un peu » et sont positifs. Few et little sans a signifient « peu de », avec un sens négatif.
fr.formation: a few / few + nom pluriel (a few friends) ; a little / little + nom indénombrable (a little time) ; souvent very few / very little
fr.contrast: Le a change le sens : a few friends (quelques amis) / few friends (peu d'amis). Ne confondez pas avec la taille : a little time = un peu de temps, mais a small house = une petite maison.
fr.example: I have a few friends here, but very little free time.
fr.exampleTranslation: J'ai quelques amis ici, mais très peu de temps libre.

aliases: 两者都 任何一个 都不
les deux soit ni l un ni l autre

zh.name: both、either、neither
zh.meaning: both、either、neither 都指两个人或物：both 是“两者都”，either 是“两者中任一个”，neither 是“两者都不”。
zh.formation: both + 复数名词 / both of them；either / neither + 单数名词（either day）；either / neither of + 复数；both … and，either … or，neither … nor
zh.contrast: “两个都不”用 neither，不用 both … not：Neither of them likes it，不说 *Both of them don't like it。neither 本身是否定，动词不再加 not。三者以上用 all / none。
zh.example: Both of my sisters live in London, but neither of them likes the city.
zh.exampleTranslation: 我的两个姐妹都住在伦敦，但她们都不喜欢这座城市。

en.name: Both, either, neither
en.meaning: Both, either and neither refer to two people or things: both means the two together, either means one or the other, neither means not one and not the other.
en.formation: both + plural noun / both of them; either / neither + singular noun (either day); either / neither of + plural; both … and, either … or, neither … nor
en.contrast: For 'not one and not the other', use neither, not both … not: Neither of them likes it, not *Both of them don't like it. Neither is already negative, so no extra not. For three or more, use all / none.
en.example: Both of my sisters live in London, but neither of them likes the city.
en.exampleTranslation: Both of my sisters live in London, but neither of them likes the city.

fr.name: Both, either, neither
fr.meaning: Both, either et neither parlent de deux personnes ou choses : both = les deux, either = l'un ou l'autre, neither = ni l'un ni l'autre.
fr.formation: both + nom pluriel / both of them ; either / neither + nom singulier (either day) ; either / neither of + pluriel ; both … and, either … or, neither … nor
fr.contrast: Pas de double négation comme avec « ne… aucun » : Neither of them likes it (aucune des deux ne l'aime), et non *Neither of them doesn't like it. Pour trois ou plus : all / none.
fr.example: Both of my sisters live in London, but neither of them likes the city.
fr.exampleTranslation: Mes deux sœurs habitent à Londres, mais aucune des deux n'aime la ville.

zh.name: 运动介词
zh.meaning: 表示移动方向的介词：across 横穿（从一边到另一边），through 穿过（从内部通过），along 沿着，into 进入，past 经过。
zh.formation: 移动动词 + 介词 + 名词（walk across the road / drive through the tunnel / run along the beach / go into the shop）
zh.contrast: in / on 表示位置，into / onto 表示进入、移到上面：She is in the room（在里面）/ She ran into the room（跑进去）。across 是在平面上横穿，through 是穿过有边界的空间（through the forest）。
zh.example: We walked along the river and then went across the bridge.
zh.exampleTranslation: 我们沿着河边散步，然后走过了桥。

en.name: Prepositions of movement
en.meaning: These prepositions show the direction of movement: across (from one side to the other), through (inside something, from one end to the other), along (following a line), into (entering), past (going by).
en.formation: movement verb + preposition + noun (walk across the road / drive through the tunnel / run along the beach / go into the shop)
en.contrast: In and on show position; into and onto show movement: She is in the room vs She ran into the room. Across is over a surface; through is inside a space with sides (through the forest).
en.example: We walked along the river and then went across the bridge.
en.exampleTranslation: We walked along the river and then went across the bridge.

fr.name: Prépositions de mouvement
fr.meaning: Ces prépositions indiquent la direction d'un déplacement : across (d'un côté à l'autre), through (à travers, par l'intérieur), along (le long de), into (en entrant dans), past (devant, en passant).
fr.formation: verbe de mouvement + préposition + nom (walk across the road / drive through the tunnel / run along the beach / go into the shop)
fr.contrast: Le français met la direction dans le verbe (« traverser la rue en courant »), l'anglais dans la préposition : run across the street. In indique la position, into le mouvement : She ran into the room (elle est entrée en courant).
fr.example: We walked along the river and then went across the bridge.
fr.exampleTranslation: Nous avons marché le long de la rivière, puis nous avons traversé le pont.

zh.name: 短语动词
zh.meaning: 短语动词由动词 + 小品词（off, up, on, out 等）构成，整体意思常常和单个词不同，如 give up（放弃）、look after（照顾）。
zh.formation: 动词 + 小品词（turn off, get up, look for）；宾语是名词时可放中间或后面：turn off the light / turn the light off
zh.contrast: 宾语是代词时，必须放在动词和小品词中间：turn it off，不说 *turn off it。但 look for、look after 等不能分开：look for it，不说 *look it for。
zh.example: Please turn off the lights before you leave the room.
zh.exampleTranslation: 离开房间前请把灯关掉。

en.name: Common phrasal verbs
en.meaning: A phrasal verb is a verb + particle (off, up, on, out…) whose meaning is often different from the separate words, e.g. give up (stop trying), look after (take care of).
en.formation: verb + particle (turn off, get up, look for); a noun object can go before or after the particle: turn off the light / turn the light off
en.contrast: A pronoun object must go between the verb and particle: turn it off, not *turn off it. Some phrasal verbs can't be separated: look for it, not *look it for.
en.example: Please turn off the lights before you leave the room.
en.exampleTranslation: Please turn off the lights before you leave the room.

fr.name: Verbes à particule courants
fr.meaning: Un verbe à particule associe un verbe et une particule (off, up, on, out…), souvent avec un sens différent des mots séparés : give up (abandonner), look after (s'occuper de).
fr.formation: verbe + particule (turn off, get up, look for) ; un nom complément peut se placer avant ou après la particule : turn off the light / turn the light off
fr.contrast: Un pronom complément se place entre le verbe et la particule : turn it off, et non *turn off it. Certains verbes ne se séparent pas : look for it (le chercher), et non *look it for.
fr.example: Please turn off the lights before you leave the room.
fr.exampleTranslation: Éteins les lumières avant de quitter la pièce, s'il te plaît.

points.pattern: making polite requests (Could you... / Would you...?)

zh.name: 礼貌请求
zh.meaning: Could you / Would you + 动词原形用来礼貌地请别人做事，比祈使句和 Can you 更客气。
zh.formation: Could / Would you + 动词原形 …?（Could you open the window?）；Would you mind + 动词-ing?（Would you mind waiting?）；请求许可：Could I / May I …?
zh.contrast: Can you …? 比较随意，Could / Would you …? 更礼貌。回答 Would you mind …? 时，No, not at all 表示“不介意，可以”。这里的 could 不表示过去。
zh.example: Could you help me carry this heavy bag, please?
zh.exampleTranslation: 你能帮我提一下这个重袋子吗？

en.name: Polite requests
en.meaning: Could you / Would you + base verb ask someone politely to do something. They are softer than an imperative or Can you…?
en.formation: Could / Would you + base verb …? (Could you open the window?); Would you mind + verb-ing? (Would you mind waiting?); asking permission: Could I / May I …?
en.contrast: Can you…? is casual; Could you / Would you…? are more polite. To Would you mind…?, No, not at all means 'Yes, I'll do it'. Could here is not past.
en.example: Could you help me carry this heavy bag, please?
en.exampleTranslation: Could you help me carry this heavy bag, please?

fr.name: Demandes polies
fr.meaning: Could you / Would you + base verbale servent à demander poliment un service, comme « pourriez-vous… ? ». C'est plus doux qu'un impératif ou que Can you…?
fr.formation: Could / Would you + base verbale …? (Could you open the window?) ; Would you mind + verbe-ing? (Would you mind waiting?) ; demander la permission : Could I / May I …?
fr.contrast: Can you…? est familier ; Could you / Would you…? sont plus polis. À Would you mind…? (ça vous dérange de…), on répond No, not at all pour dire oui.
fr.example: Could you help me carry this heavy bag, please?
fr.exampleTranslation: Tu pourrais m'aider à porter ce sac lourd, s'il te plaît ?

zh.name: 反义疑问句
zh.meaning: 反义疑问句是在陈述句后加的简短问句，用来确认信息或希望对方同意，相当于中文的“……，对吧？”
zh.formation: 肯定陈述 + 否定附加问句（You're tired, aren't you?）；否定陈述 + 肯定附加问句（She doesn't smoke, does she?）；用陈述句中的助动词或 be，没有就用 do / does / did
zh.contrast: 中文只有一个“对吧”，英语的附加问句要随助动词和人称变化。特殊：I'm late, aren't I?；Let's go, shall we?。回答按事实：She doesn't smoke, does she? — No, she doesn't（对，她不抽）。
zh.example: You speak English very well, don't you?
zh.exampleTranslation: 你英语说得很好，对吧？

en.name: Question tags
en.meaning: A question tag is a short question added to a statement to check information or ask for agreement.
en.formation: positive statement + negative tag (You're tired, aren't you?); negative statement + positive tag (She doesn't smoke, does she?); use the statement's auxiliary or be, otherwise do / does / did
en.contrast: The tag is not fixed: it changes with the auxiliary and the subject. Special cases: I'm late, aren't I? / Let's go, shall we? Answer by the facts: She doesn't smoke, does she? — No, she doesn't.
en.example: You speak English very well, don't you?
en.exampleTranslation: You speak English very well, don't you?

fr.name: Question tags
fr.meaning: Le question tag est une courte question ajoutée à une affirmation pour vérifier une information ou demander l'accord, comme « n'est-ce pas ? ».
fr.formation: affirmation positive + tag négatif (You're tired, aren't you?) ; affirmation négative + tag positif (She doesn't smoke, does she?) ; on reprend l'auxiliaire ou be, sinon do / does / did
fr.contrast: « N'est-ce pas » est invariable, mais le tag anglais change selon l'auxiliaire et le sujet. Cas spéciaux : I'm late, aren't I? / Let's go, shall we? On répond selon les faits : She doesn't smoke, does she? — No, she doesn't (non, elle ne fume pas).
fr.example: You speak English very well, don't you?
fr.exampleTranslation: Tu parles très bien anglais, n'est-ce pas ?

aliases: so do i neither do i

zh.name: so/neither 简短回应
zh.meaning: So + 助动词 + 主语表示“某人也是”（肯定），Neither / Nor + 助动词 + 主语表示“某人也不”（否定），用来避免重复。
zh.formation: So / Neither + 助动词或 be + 主语（I'm tired. — So am I. / I can't swim. — Neither can I.）；助动词要和前一句一致，前一句没有就用 do / does / did
zh.contrast: 助动词要和前一句对应：I like it. — So do I，不说 *So am I。要倒装：So do I，不说 *So I do。neither 后用肯定形式：Neither do I，不说 *Neither don't I。口语也说 Me too / Me neither。
zh.example: I love drinking coffee, and so does my sister.
zh.exampleTranslation: 我很喜欢喝咖啡，我姐姐也是。

en.name: So and neither responses
en.meaning: So + auxiliary + subject means 'the same is true' (positive); Neither / Nor + auxiliary + subject means 'the same is true' (negative). They avoid repeating the sentence.
en.formation: So / Neither + auxiliary or be + subject (I'm tired. — So am I. / I can't swim. — Neither can I.); match the first auxiliary, or use do / does / did
en.contrast: The auxiliary must match the first sentence: I like it. — So do I, not *So am I. Keep the inverted order: So do I, not *So I do. Neither takes a positive verb: Neither do I, not *Neither don't I. Informal: Me too / Me neither.
en.example: I love drinking coffee, and so does my sister.
en.exampleTranslation: I love drinking coffee, and so does my sister.

fr.name: Réponses avec so et neither
fr.meaning: So + auxiliaire + sujet signifie « moi aussi / lui aussi » ; Neither / Nor + auxiliaire + sujet signifie « moi non plus ». Ils évitent de répéter la phrase.
fr.formation: So / Neither + auxiliaire ou be + sujet (I'm tired. — So am I. / I can't swim. — Neither can I.) ; on reprend l'auxiliaire de la première phrase, sinon do / does / did
fr.contrast: « Moi aussi » change selon l'auxiliaire : I like it. — So do I, mais I'm tired. — So am I. L'ordre est inversé (So do I, et non *So I do), et neither prend un verbe affirmatif : Neither do I. À l'oral : Me too / Me neither.
fr.example: I love drinking coffee, and so does my sister.
fr.exampleTranslation: J'adore boire du café, et ma sœur aussi.

zh.name: 让步连词 although
zh.meaning: although / even though 引导让步从句，表示“虽然、尽管”；even though 语气更强。
zh.formation: Although / Even though + 从句, 主句（Although he is rich, he lives simply.）；也可以放在主句后：He lives simply although he is rich.
zh.contrast: although 和 but 不能同时用：Although he is rich, he lives simply，不说 *Although he is rich, but he lives simply（中文的“虽然……但是……”）。although 后接句子，despite 后接名词或 -ing。
zh.example: Although he is very rich, he lives in a small flat.
zh.exampleTranslation: 虽然他很有钱，但他住在一套小公寓里。

en.name: Although and even though
en.meaning: Although and even though introduce a contrast that is surprising; even though is stronger.
en.formation: Although / Even though + clause, main clause (Although he is rich, he lives simply.); or after the main clause: He lives simply although he is rich.
en.contrast: Don't use although and but together: Although he is rich, he lives simply, not *Although he is rich, but he lives simply. Although takes a clause; despite takes a noun or -ing.
en.example: Although he is very rich, he lives in a small flat.
en.exampleTranslation: Although he is very rich, he lives in a small flat.

fr.name: Although et even though
fr.meaning: Although et even though introduisent une opposition, comme « bien que / même si » ; even though est plus fort.
fr.formation: Although / Even though + proposition, principale (Although he is rich, he lives simply.) ; ou après la principale : He lives simply although he is rich.
fr.contrast: Contrairement à « bien que », although n'exige pas de subjonctif : Although he is rich (bien qu'il soit riche). N'ajoutez pas but dans la principale. Despite (malgré) est suivi d'un nom : despite the rain.
fr.example: Although he is very rich, he lives in a small flat.
fr.exampleTranslation: Bien qu'il soit très riche, il habite dans un petit appartement.

zh.name: so 和 therefore
zh.meaning: so 和 therefore 引出结果，意思是“所以、因此”。so 常用于口语，therefore 较正式。
zh.formation: 原因, so + 结果（It was late, so we went home.）；原因. Therefore, 结果 / 原因; therefore, 结果（较正式）
zh.contrast: so 引出结果，because 引出原因，方向相反：I was ill, so I stayed home = I stayed home because I was ill，两者不能同时用。therefore 是副词，不能像 so 一样只用逗号连接两个句子。
zh.example: She missed her alarm, so she was late for the morning meeting.
zh.exampleTranslation: 她没听到闹钟，所以早上开会迟到了。

en.name: So and therefore
en.meaning: So and therefore introduce a result. So is common in speech; therefore is more formal.
en.formation: cause, so + result (It was late, so we went home.); cause. Therefore, result / cause; therefore, result (formal)
en.contrast: So gives the result, because gives the cause: I was ill, so I stayed home = I stayed home because I was ill — never both together. Therefore is an adverb, so it can't join two clauses with only a comma.
en.example: She missed her alarm, so she was late for the morning meeting.
en.exampleTranslation: She missed her alarm, so she was late for the morning meeting.

fr.name: So et therefore
fr.meaning: So et therefore introduisent une conséquence, comme « donc / alors ». So est courant à l'oral ; therefore est plus soutenu.
fr.formation: cause, so + conséquence (It was late, so we went home.) ; cause. Therefore, conséquence / cause; therefore, conséquence (soutenu)
fr.contrast: So (donc) donne la conséquence, because (parce que) la cause : I was ill, so I stayed home = I stayed home because I was ill. Therefore (par conséquent) ne relie pas deux propositions avec une simple virgule.
fr.example: She missed her alarm, so she was late for the morning meeting.
fr.exampleTranslation: Elle n'a pas entendu son réveil, alors elle est arrivée en retard à la réunion du matin.

zh.name: 现在进行时表将来
zh.meaning: 现在进行时可以表示已经安排好的将来活动，通常有确定的时间，常常是和别人约好的事。
zh.formation: 主语 + am / is / are + 动词-ing + 将来时间（I'm seeing the dentist tomorrow. / What are you doing tonight?）
zh.contrast: be going to 强调自己的打算，现在进行时强调已经约好、安排好：I'm going to call him（打算）/ I'm meeting him at six（已约好）。时刻表上的事用一般现在时：The train leaves at 8。
zh.example: We are meeting our grandparents this Saturday.
zh.exampleTranslation: 我们这个星期六要去看望祖父母。

en.name: Present continuous for future
en.meaning: The present continuous can describe future arrangements that are already fixed, usually with a time and often with other people.
en.formation: subject + am / is / are + verb-ing + future time (I'm seeing the dentist tomorrow. / What are you doing tonight?)
en.contrast: Be going to stresses an intention; the present continuous stresses a fixed arrangement: I'm going to call him (my plan) vs I'm meeting him at six (we've agreed). Timetables use the present simple: The train leaves at 8.
en.example: We are meeting our grandparents this Saturday.
en.exampleTranslation: We are meeting our grandparents this Saturday.

fr.name: Présent continu pour le futur
fr.meaning: Le présent continu peut exprimer un projet futur déjà organisé, en général avec une date et souvent avec d'autres personnes.
fr.formation: sujet + am / is / are + verbe-ing + repère futur (I'm seeing the dentist tomorrow. / What are you doing tonight?)
fr.contrast: Le français dit « je vais voir le dentiste demain » ; l'anglais emploie le présent continu pour un rendez-vous fixé : I'm seeing the dentist tomorrow. Be going to souligne plutôt une intention ; les horaires prennent le présent simple.
fr.example: We are meeting our grandparents this Saturday.
fr.exampleTranslation: Samedi, nous allons voir nos grands-parents.

zh.name: 同级比较as ... as
zh.meaning: as + 形容词 / 副词原级 + as 表示两者程度相同；not as … as 表示“不如……”。
zh.formation: A + be + as + 形容词 + as + B（She is as tall as me）；not as … as（This film isn't as good as the book）；倍数：twice as big as
zh.contrast: 中间用原级，不用比较级：as tall as，不说 *as taller as；后面用 as，不用 than。“和……一样”接名词时用 the same as：the same age as me，不说 *as same as。
zh.example: This film isn't as good as the book.
zh.exampleTranslation: 这部电影没有原著好看。

en.name: (Not) as … as
en.meaning: As + adjective/adverb + as shows two things are equal; not as … as means 'less than'.
en.formation: A + be + as + adjective + as + B (She is as tall as me); not as … as (This film isn't as good as the book); multiples: twice as big as
en.contrast: Use the base form, not the comparative, and as, not than: as tall as, not *as taller as or *as tall than. With a noun, use the same as: the same age as me, not *as same as.
en.example: This film isn't as good as the book.
en.exampleTranslation: This film isn't as good as the book.

fr.name: Comparaison avec as … as
fr.meaning: As + adjectif/adverbe + as exprime l'égalité, comme « aussi … que » ; not as … as signifie « moins … que ».
fr.formation: A + be + as + adjectif + as + B (She is as tall as me) ; not as … as (This film isn't as good as the book) ; multiplication : twice as big as
fr.contrast: « Aussi … que » se dit as … as, jamais *as … than. Avec un nom : the same age as me (le même âge que moi). Not as … as est plus naturel que less … than : not as tall as me.
fr.example: This film isn't as good as the book.
fr.exampleTranslation: Ce film n'est pas aussi bien que le livre.

zh.name: 零条件句
zh.meaning: 零条件句表示总是成立的事实或规律，这里的 if 意思接近 when（每当）。
zh.formation: If / When + 一般现在时, 一般现在时（If you heat ice, it melts.）
zh.contrast: 第一条件句谈将来某一次具体的可能：If it rains tomorrow, we'll stay home。零条件句谈每次都会发生的结果：If it rains, the roads get wet。
zh.example: If you leave chocolate in the sun, it melts quickly.
zh.exampleTranslation: 如果你把巧克力放在太阳下，它很快就会融化。

en.name: Zero conditional
en.meaning: The zero conditional states facts and results that are always true; if means almost the same as when.
en.formation: If / When + present simple, present simple (If you heat ice, it melts.)
en.contrast: The first conditional is about one possible future situation: If it rains tomorrow, we'll stay home. The zero conditional is about what always happens: If it rains, the roads get wet.
en.example: If you leave chocolate in the sun, it melts quickly.
en.exampleTranslation: If you leave chocolate in the sun, it melts quickly.

fr.name: Conditionnel zéro
fr.meaning: Le conditionnel zéro exprime des faits et des résultats toujours vrais ; if a presque le sens de when (« chaque fois que »).
fr.formation: If / When + présent simple, présent simple (If you heat ice, it melts.)
fr.contrast: Le premier conditionnel parle d'une situation future précise : If it rains tomorrow, we'll stay home. Le conditionnel zéro parle de ce qui arrive toujours : If it rains, the roads get wet (quand il pleut, les routes sont mouillées).
fr.example: If you leave chocolate in the sun, it melts quickly.
fr.exampleTranslation: Si on laisse du chocolat au soleil, il fond vite.

zh.name: 主语疑问句和宾语疑问句
zh.meaning: 疑问词作主语时（问“谁做了……”），用陈述句语序，不加 do / does / did；疑问词作宾语时（问“……了谁 / 什么”），要用助动词。
zh.formation: 主语疑问句：Who / What + 动词 …?（Who called you?）；宾语疑问句：Who / What + do / does / did + 主语 + 动词 …?（Who did you call?）
zh.contrast: 主语疑问句不加 did：Who broke the window?，不说 *Who did break the window?。意思也不同：Who loves Anna?（谁爱安娜）/ Who does Anna love?（安娜爱谁）。
zh.example: Who painted this colorful picture on the wall?
zh.exampleTranslation: 墙上这幅色彩鲜艳的画是谁画的？

en.name: Subject and object questions
en.meaning: When who or what is the subject (asking who did something), use normal word order with no do/does/did. When it is the object, use an auxiliary.
en.formation: Subject question: Who / What + verb …? (Who called you?); object question: Who / What + do / does / did + subject + verb …? (Who did you call?)
en.contrast: Don't add did to subject questions: Who broke the window?, not *Who did break the window? The meaning changes: Who loves Anna? (someone loves her) vs Who does Anna love? (she loves someone).
en.example: Who painted this colorful picture on the wall?
en.exampleTranslation: Who painted this colorful picture on the wall?

fr.name: Questions sujet / objet
fr.meaning: Quand who ou what est sujet (« qui a fait… ? »), on garde l'ordre normal sans do/does/did. Quand il est complément, on utilise un auxiliaire.
fr.formation: Question sur le sujet : Who / What + verbe …? (Who called you?) ; question sur l'objet : Who / What + do / does / did + sujet + verbe …? (Who did you call?)
fr.contrast: C'est la différence entre « Qui t'a appelé ? » (Who called you?) et « Qui as-tu appelé ? » (Who did you call?). Pas de did dans une question sur le sujet : *Who did break the window?
fr.example: Who painted this colorful picture on the wall?
fr.exampleTranslation: Qui a peint ce tableau coloré sur le mur ?

zh.name: 相互代词
zh.meaning: each other / one another 表示“互相、彼此”，即两个或多个人对对方做同样的事。
zh.formation: 动词 / 介词 + each other（They love each other. / We talk to each other.）；所有格：each other's
zh.contrast: 反身代词表示对自己做：They looked at themselves（各自看自己）/ They looked at each other（互相看）。each other 放在动词后面：help each other，不说 *each other help。
zh.example: My sister and I help each other with our homework.
zh.exampleTranslation: 我和妹妹互相帮忙做作业。

en.name: Reciprocal pronouns
en.meaning: Each other and one another mean that two or more people do the same thing to the other(s).
en.formation: verb / preposition + each other (They love each other. / We talk to each other.); possessive: each other's
en.contrast: Reflexive pronouns mean doing something to yourself: They looked at themselves (each in the mirror) vs They looked at each other (one at the other). Today each other and one another are mostly interchangeable.
en.example: My sister and I help each other with our homework.
en.exampleTranslation: My sister and I help each other with our homework.

fr.name: Pronoms réciproques
fr.meaning: Each other et one another expriment la réciprocité : deux personnes ou plus font la même action l'une envers l'autre (« l'un l'autre »).
fr.formation: verbe / préposition + each other (They love each other. / We talk to each other.) ; possessif : each other's
fr.contrast: Le « se » français est ambigu (« ils se regardent ») ; l'anglais distingue : They looked at each other (l'un l'autre) / They looked at themselves (eux-mêmes). Each other se place après le verbe : help each other.
fr.example: My sister and I help each other with our homework.
fr.exampleTranslation: Ma sœur et moi, nous nous aidons pour nos devoirs.

zh.name: 现在完成时+for/since
zh.meaning: 现在完成时 + for / since 表示从过去开始、一直持续到现在的状态或动作。for 接一段时间，since 接开始的时间点。
zh.formation: have / has + 过去分词 + for + 一段时间（for five years）/ since + 时间点（since 2020, since I was a child）；提问：How long have you …?
zh.contrast: “我在这儿住了五年了”不能用现在时：I have lived here for five years，不说 *I live here for five years / *I am living here since 2020。for 接时长，since 接起点：for two weeks / since Monday。
zh.example: I have lived in this town for five years.
zh.exampleTranslation: 我在这个小镇住了五年了。

en.name: Present perfect with for, since
en.meaning: The present perfect with for or since describes a situation that started in the past and continues now. For gives the length of time; since gives the starting point.
en.formation: have / has + past participle + for + period (for five years) / since + starting point (since 2020, since I was a child); question: How long have you …?
en.contrast: Don't use a present tense for this: I have lived here for five years, not *I live here for five years or *I am living here since 2020. For + length (for two weeks); since + starting point (since Monday).
en.example: I have lived in this town for five years.
en.exampleTranslation: I have lived in this town for five years.

fr.name: Present perfect avec for, since
fr.meaning: Le present perfect avec for ou since décrit une situation commencée dans le passé qui dure encore. For donne la durée ; since, le point de départ.
fr.formation: have / has + participe passé + for + durée (for five years) / since + point de départ (since 2020, since I was a child) ; question : How long have you …?
fr.contrast: « Depuis » + présent se traduit par le present perfect : J'habite ici depuis cinq ans = I have lived here for five years, et non *I live here since five years. Depuis + durée = for ; depuis + date = since.
fr.example: I have lived in this town for five years.
fr.exampleTranslation: J'habite dans cette ville depuis cinq ans.

zh.name: may / might 表示可能
zh.meaning: may / might + 动词原形表示现在或将来“可能、也许”，might 的可能性稍小一些。
zh.formation: 主语 + may / might + 动词原形（It might rain.）；否定：may not / might not（She might not come.）
zh.contrast: maybe 是副词，放在句首，不能当动词用：Maybe it will rain = It might rain，不说 *It maybe rain。may not 表示“可能不”，can't 表示“不可能”。
zh.example: Take an umbrella because it might rain later.
zh.exampleTranslation: 带把伞吧，因为待会儿可能会下雨。

en.name: May and might (possibility)
en.meaning: May / might + base verb say that something is possible now or in the future; might is slightly less sure.
en.formation: subject + may / might + base verb (It might rain.); negative: may not / might not (She might not come.)
en.contrast: Maybe is an adverb, not a verb: Maybe it will rain = It might rain, not *It maybe rain. May not means 'possibly not'; can't means 'impossible'.
en.example: Take an umbrella because it might rain later.
en.exampleTranslation: Take an umbrella because it might rain later.

fr.name: May et might (possibilité)
fr.meaning: May / might + base verbale expriment une possibilité présente ou future (« il se peut que ») ; might est un peu moins sûr.
fr.formation: sujet + may / might + base verbale (It might rain.) ; négation : may not / might not (She might not come.)
fr.contrast: Maybe (peut-être) est un adverbe : Maybe it will rain = It might rain, et non *It maybe rain. May not = peut-être pas ; can't = impossible.
fr.example: Take an umbrella because it might rain later.
fr.exampleTranslation: Prends un parapluie car il pourrait pleuvoir plus tard.

zh.name: 第二条件句
zh.meaning: 第二条件句表示对现在或将来不太可能、或与事实相反的情况的假设，以及想象中的结果。这里的过去式不表示过去。
zh.formation: If + 一般过去时, would + 动词原形（If I had a car, I would drive to work.）；be 动词常用 were：If I were you, …
zh.contrast: 第一条件句谈真实可能的事：If I have time, I'll help you。第二条件句谈想象的事：If I had time, I'd help you（但我没时间）。if 从句里不用 would：If I had，不说 *If I would have。
zh.example: If I had a million dollars, I would buy a big boat.
zh.exampleTranslation: 如果我有一百万美元，我会买一艘大船。

en.name: Second conditional
en.meaning: The second conditional imagines a situation that is unreal or unlikely now or in the future, and its result. The past tense here does not mean past time.
en.formation: If + past simple, would + base verb (If I had a car, I would drive to work.); be often becomes were: If I were you, …
en.contrast: The first conditional is for real possibilities: If I have time, I'll help you. The second is imaginary: If I had time, I'd help you (but I don't). No would in the if-clause: If I had, not *If I would have.
en.example: If I had a million dollars, I would buy a big boat.
en.exampleTranslation: If I had a million dollars, I would buy a big boat.

fr.name: Second conditionnel
fr.meaning: Le second conditionnel imagine une situation irréelle ou peu probable, au présent ou au futur, et sa conséquence. Le prétérit ne marque pas ici le passé.
fr.formation: If + prétérit, would + base verbale (If I had a car, I would drive to work.) ; be devient souvent were : If I were you, …
fr.contrast: C'est la structure « si + imparfait, conditionnel » : If I had time, I'd help you. Pas de would après if (*If I would have), comme on ne dit pas « si j'aurais ».
fr.example: If I had a million dollars, I would buy a big boat.
fr.exampleTranslation: Si j'avais un million de dollars, j'achèterais un gros bateau.

zh.name: 第三条件句
zh.meaning: 第三条件句假设过去发生了不同的情况，并想象当时会有的不同结果，常表示后悔或庆幸。
zh.formation: If + had + 过去分词, would have + 过去分词（If I had known, I would have called you.）；缩写：I'd have, she'd known
zh.contrast: 第二条件句假设现在：If I had money, I would buy it（现在没钱）。第三条件句假设过去：If I had had money, I would have bought it（当时没钱）。if 从句里的 'd 是 had，主句里的 'd 是 would。
zh.example: If she had left earlier, she would have caught the train.
zh.exampleTranslation: 如果她早点出发，她就能赶上那班火车了。

en.name: Third conditional
en.meaning: The third conditional imagines a different past and its different result. It often expresses regret or relief.
en.formation: If + had + past participle, would have + past participle (If I had known, I would have called you.); short forms: I'd have, she'd known
en.contrast: The second conditional imagines the present: If I had money, I would buy it (I don't now). The third imagines the past: If I had had money, I would have bought it (I didn't then). In the if-clause 'd = had; in the result 'd = would.
en.example: If she had left earlier, she would have caught the train.
en.exampleTranslation: If she had left earlier, she would have caught the train.

fr.name: Troisième conditionnel
fr.meaning: Le troisième conditionnel imagine un passé différent et sa conséquence, souvent pour exprimer un regret ou un soulagement.
fr.formation: If + had + participe passé, would have + participe passé (If I had known, I would have called you.) ; formes courtes : I'd have, she'd known
fr.contrast: C'est « si + plus-que-parfait, conditionnel passé » : If I had known, I would have called you (si j'avais su, je t'aurais appelé). Le second conditionnel parle du présent : If I had money, I would buy it.
fr.example: If she had left earlier, she would have caught the train.
fr.exampleTranslation: Si elle était partie plus tôt, elle aurait attrapé le train.

zh.name: 过去完成时
zh.meaning: 过去完成时表示在过去某个时间或另一个过去动作之前已经发生的事，即“过去的过去”。
zh.formation: 主语 + had + 过去分词（When I arrived, the train had already left.）；否定：hadn't + 过去分词
zh.contrast: 不要因为事情发生得很久就用过去完成时：I visited Rome in 2005，不说 *I had visited Rome in 2005。只有比另一个过去时间更早时才用：When we got there, the film had started（我们到时已开始）/ the film started（我们到了才开始）。
zh.example: When I arrived at the station, the train had already left.
zh.exampleTranslation: 当我到达车站时，火车已经开走了。

en.name: Past perfect
en.meaning: The past perfect shows that something happened before another moment or action in the past.
en.formation: subject + had + past participle (When I arrived, the train had already left.); negative: hadn't + past participle
en.contrast: Don't use it just because something was long ago: I visited Rome in 2005, not *I had visited Rome in 2005. Use it for an earlier past: When we got there, the film had started (before we arrived) vs the film started (after we arrived).
en.example: When I arrived at the station, the train had already left.
en.exampleTranslation: When I arrived at the station, the train had already left.

fr.name: Plus-que-parfait
fr.meaning: Le past perfect indique qu'une action s'est produite avant un autre moment ou une autre action du passé.
fr.formation: sujet + had + participe passé (When I arrived, the train had already left.) ; négation : hadn't + participe passé
fr.contrast: Il correspond souvent au plus-que-parfait : the train had already left (le train était déjà parti). Comparez : When we got there, the film had started (avait commencé) / the film started (a commencé à notre arrivée).
fr.example: When I arrived at the station, the train had already left.
fr.exampleTranslation: Quand je suis arrivé à la gare, le train était déjà parti.

aliases: say vs tell in reported speech

zh.name: 间接引语（陈述句）
zh.meaning: 间接引语转述别人说过的话。转述动词是过去式（said, told）时，从句的时态通常往过去推一步。
zh.formation: said (that) / told + 人 + (that) + 从句；am / is → was，will → would，can → could，现在时 → 过去时，过去时 → 过去完成时（"I'm tired" → She said she was tired）
zh.contrast: tell 后面必须有人：He told me (that) …；say 后面不直接接人：He said (that) …，不说 *He said me。代词和时间也要变："I'll come tomorrow" → He said he would come the next day。
zh.example: He said that he loved reading books in the library.
zh.exampleTranslation: 他说他喜欢在图书馆看书。

en.name: Reported speech: statements
en.meaning: Reported speech tells what someone said without quoting. After a past reporting verb (said, told), the tense usually moves one step back.
en.formation: said (that) / told + person + (that) + clause; am / is → was, will → would, can → could, present → past, past → past perfect ("I'm tired" → She said she was tired)
en.contrast: Tell needs a person: He told me (that)…; say doesn't take a person directly: He said (that)…, not *He said me. Pronouns and time words change too: "I'll come tomorrow" → He said he would come the next day.
en.example: He said that he loved reading books in the library.
en.exampleTranslation: He said that he loved reading books in the library.

fr.name: Discours indirect : affirmations
fr.meaning: Le discours indirect rapporte les paroles de quelqu'un sans les citer. Après un verbe introducteur au passé (said, told), le temps recule en général d'un cran.
fr.formation: said (that) / told + personne + (that) + proposition ; am / is → was, will → would, can → could, présent → prétérit, prétérit → past perfect ("I'm tired" → She said she was tired)
fr.contrast: Tell s'emploie avec la personne : He told me (that)… ; say, sans personne : He said (that)…, et non *He said me. Comme en français, will devient would : He said he would come (il a dit qu'il viendrait).
fr.example: He said that he loved reading books in the library.
fr.exampleTranslation: Il a dit qu'il aimait lire des livres à la bibliothèque.

zh.name: 间接引语（疑问句）
zh.meaning: 转述别人的问题时用陈述句语序，不用 do / did，句末用句号；一般疑问句用 if / whether 引导。
zh.formation: asked (+ 人) + 疑问词 + 主语 + 动词（She asked where I lived）；asked (+ 人) + if / whether + 主语 + 动词（He asked me if I was hungry）；时态同样后移
zh.contrast: 不要保留疑问句语序：She asked me where I lived，不说 *She asked me where did I live。一般疑问句要加 if / whether，不说 *He asked me was I hungry。
zh.example: He asked me if I was hungry.
zh.exampleTranslation: 他问我饿不饿。

en.name: Reported speech: questions
en.meaning: Reported questions use statement word order, with no do/did and no question mark. Yes/no questions are reported with if or whether.
en.formation: asked (+ person) + wh-word + subject + verb (She asked where I lived); asked (+ person) + if / whether + subject + verb (He asked me if I was hungry); tenses move back as in statements
en.contrast: Don't keep question word order: She asked me where I lived, not *She asked me where did I live. Yes/no questions need if or whether: He asked me if I was hungry, not *He asked me was I hungry.
en.example: He asked me if I was hungry.
en.exampleTranslation: He asked me if I was hungry.

fr.name: Discours indirect : questions
fr.meaning: Les questions rapportées prennent l'ordre d'une affirmation, sans do/did ni point d'interrogation. Les questions fermées sont introduites par if ou whether (« si »).
fr.formation: asked (+ personne) + mot interrogatif + sujet + verbe (She asked where I lived) ; asked (+ personne) + if / whether + sujet + verbe (He asked me if I was hungry) ; les temps reculent comme pour les affirmations
fr.contrast: Comme en français (« il m'a demandé où j'habitais »), pas d'inversion : She asked me where I lived, et non *where did I live. « Si » se dit if ou whether : He asked me if I was hungry.
fr.example: He asked me if I was hungry.
fr.exampleTranslation: Il m'a demandé si j'avais faim.

zh.name: 非限制性定语从句
zh.meaning: 非限制性定语从句用逗号隔开，对已经明确的人或物补充额外信息；去掉它，句子意思仍然完整。
zh.formation: 名词, who / which / whose / where + 从句,（My brother, who lives in London, is an engineer.）
zh.contrast: 非限制性从句不能用 that，关系词也不能省略：Paris, which I love, …，不说 *Paris, that I love, …。有无逗号意思不同：my brother who lives in London（我有几个哥哥，指住伦敦的那个）/ my brother, who lives in London（只有一个哥哥）。
zh.example: My elder brother, who lives in London, is an engineer.
zh.exampleTranslation: 我哥哥住在伦敦，是一名工程师。

en.name: Non-defining relative clauses
en.meaning: A non-defining relative clause, set off by commas, adds extra information about a person or thing that is already clear. Without it, the sentence still makes sense.
en.formation: noun, who / which / whose / where + clause, (My brother, who lives in London, is an engineer.)
en.contrast: Never use that, and never drop the pronoun: Paris, which I love, …, not *Paris, that I love, … Commas change the meaning: my brother who lives in London (I have several) vs my brother, who lives in London (I have one).
en.example: My elder brother, who lives in London, is an engineer.
en.exampleTranslation: My elder brother, who lives in London, is an engineer.

fr.name: Relatives explicatives
fr.meaning: La relative explicative, entre virgules, ajoute une information sur une personne ou une chose déjà identifiée. Sans elle, la phrase reste complète.
fr.formation: nom, who / which / whose / where + proposition, (My brother, who lives in London, is an engineer.)
fr.contrast: Jamais de that ni de pronom omis : Paris, which I love, …, et non *Paris, that I love, … Les virgules changent le sens : my brother who lives in London (j'en ai plusieurs) / my brother, who lives in London (je n'en ai qu'un).
fr.example: My elder brother, who lives in London, is an engineer.
fr.exampleTranslation: Mon frère aîné, qui vit à Londres, est ingénieur.

zh.name: used to 表示过去习惯
zh.meaning: used to + 动词原形表示过去经常做、现在已经不做的事，或过去存在、现在已改变的状态。
zh.formation: used to + 动词原形（I used to play football.）；否定：didn't use to；疑问：Did you use to …?
zh.contrast: used to 只用于过去，现在的习惯用 usually：I usually get up at 7，不说 *I use to get up at 7。be used to + -ing 表示“习惯于”：I'm used to getting up early。
zh.example: I used to walk to school when I was a child.
zh.exampleTranslation: 我小时候常常走路上学。

en.name: Used to for past habits
en.meaning: Used to + base verb describes past habits or states that are no longer true.
en.formation: used to + base verb (I used to play football.); negative: didn't use to; question: Did you use to …?
en.contrast: Used to is only for the past; for present habits use usually: I usually get up at 7, not *I use to get up at 7. Be used to + -ing means 'be accustomed to': I'm used to getting up early.
en.example: I used to walk to school when I was a child.
en.exampleTranslation: I used to walk to school when I was a child.

fr.name: Used to (habitudes passées)
fr.meaning: Used to + base verbale décrit une habitude ou un état passé qui n'existe plus, souvent rendu par l'imparfait.
fr.formation: used to + base verbale (I used to play football.) ; négation : didn't use to ; question : Did you use to …?
fr.contrast: Used to n'existe qu'au passé ; pour une habitude actuelle, on dit usually : I usually get up at 7, et non *I use to get up at 7. Be used to + -ing signifie « avoir l'habitude de » : I'm used to getting up early.
fr.example: I used to walk to school when I was a child.
fr.exampleTranslation: J'allais à l'école à pied quand j'étais enfant.

points.pattern: be used to and get used to

zh.name: be / get used to
zh.meaning: be used to 表示“已经习惯于”（状态），get used to 表示“逐渐习惯”（过程）；这里的 to 是介词，后接名词或 -ing。
zh.formation: be used to + 名词 / 动词-ing（I'm used to the noise / to working late）；get used to + 名词 / 动词-ing（You'll get used to it.）
zh.contrast: 这里的 to 是介词，后面不能接动词原形：I'm used to getting up early，不说 *I'm used to get up early。used to + 动词原形表示过去的习惯：I used to get up early（以前常早起）。
zh.example: She is getting used to waking up early every morning.
zh.exampleTranslation: 她正逐渐习惯每天早上早起。

en.name: Be / get used to
en.meaning: Be used to means 'be accustomed to' (a state); get used to means 'become accustomed to' (a process). Here to is a preposition, followed by a noun or -ing.
en.formation: be used to + noun / verb-ing (I'm used to the noise / to working late); get used to + noun / verb-ing (You'll get used to it.)
en.contrast: To is a preposition here, so no base verb: I'm used to getting up early, not *I'm used to get up early. Used to + base verb is a past habit: I used to get up early (I did, but not now).
en.example: She is getting used to waking up early every morning.
en.exampleTranslation: She is getting used to waking up early every morning.

fr.name: Be / get used to
fr.meaning: Be used to signifie « avoir l'habitude de » (un état) ; get used to signifie « s'habituer à » (un processus). To est ici une préposition, suivie d'un nom ou d'un verbe en -ing.
fr.formation: be used to + nom / verbe-ing (I'm used to the noise / to working late) ; get used to + nom / verbe-ing (You'll get used to it.)
fr.contrast: To est une préposition : I'm used to getting up early, et non *I'm used to get up early. Used to + base verbale exprime une habitude passée : I used to get up early (avant, je me levais tôt).
fr.example: She is getting used to waking up early every morning.
fr.exampleTranslation: Elle commence à s'habituer à se lever tôt tous les matins.

aliases: actions in progress in the future

zh.name: 将来进行时
zh.meaning: 将来进行时表示将来某个时间点正在进行的动作。
zh.formation: will be + 动词-ing（This time tomorrow I'll be lying on the beach.）；否定：won't be + -ing
zh.contrast: will + 动词原形表示到那时才发生的动作：When you arrive, I'll cook dinner（你到了我再做）/ When you arrive, I'll be cooking dinner（你到时我正在做）。
zh.example: At this time tomorrow, we will be flying to Paris.
zh.exampleTranslation: 明天这个时候，我们正在飞往巴黎的路上。

en.name: Future continuous
en.meaning: The future continuous describes an action that will be in progress at a certain time in the future.
en.formation: will be + verb-ing (This time tomorrow I'll be lying on the beach.); negative: won't be + -ing
en.contrast: Will + base verb is an action that happens at that time: When you arrive, I'll cook dinner (after you arrive) vs When you arrive, I'll be cooking dinner (already in progress).
en.example: At this time tomorrow, we will be flying to Paris.
en.exampleTranslation: At this time tomorrow, we will be flying to Paris.

fr.name: Futur continu
fr.meaning: Le futur continu décrit une action qui sera en cours à un moment donné du futur (« je serai en train de »).
fr.formation: will be + verbe-ing (This time tomorrow I'll be lying on the beach.) ; négation : won't be + -ing
fr.contrast: Le français n'a qu'un futur : « je préparerai le dîner ». L'anglais distingue : When you arrive, I'll cook dinner (après ton arrivée) / I'll be cooking dinner (déjà en train de le faire).
fr.example: At this time tomorrow, we will be flying to Paris.
fr.exampleTranslation: Demain à cette heure-ci, nous serons dans l'avion pour Paris.

zh.name: 将来完成时
zh.meaning: 将来完成时表示到将来某个时间之前，某个动作将已经完成。
zh.formation: will have + 过去分词，常与 by + 时间连用（By 2030, I will have finished university.）
zh.contrast: 常和 by（不迟于）连用，不要和 until（一直到）混淆：I'll have finished by Friday（周五前完成）/ I'll work until Friday（一直工作到周五）。
zh.example: By next month, I will have finished this book.
zh.exampleTranslation: 到下个月，我就会读完这本书了。

en.name: Future perfect
en.meaning: The future perfect says that an action will be finished before a certain time in the future.
en.formation: will have + past participle, often with by + time (By 2030, I will have finished university.)
en.contrast: It usually goes with by (no later than), not until (up to that time): I'll have finished by Friday vs I'll work until Friday.
en.example: By next month, I will have finished this book.
en.exampleTranslation: By next month, I will have finished this book.

fr.name: Futur antérieur
fr.meaning: Le future perfect indique qu'une action sera terminée avant un moment donné du futur, comme le futur antérieur.
fr.formation: will have + participe passé, souvent avec by + moment (By 2030, I will have finished university.)
fr.contrast: By signifie « d'ici / au plus tard », until signifie « jusqu'à » : I'll have finished by Friday (j'aurai fini d'ici vendredi) / I'll work until Friday (je travaillerai jusqu'à vendredi).
fr.example: By next month, I will have finished this book.
fr.exampleTranslation: D'ici le mois prochain, j'aurai fini ce livre.

aliases: must, might, could, can't for deduction
certainty and possibility in the present

zh.name: 现在推测 must/can't
zh.meaning: must、might、may、could、can't + 动词原形根据证据推测现在的情况：must 表示“一定”，might / may / could 表示“可能”，can't 表示“不可能”。
zh.formation: must / might / may / could / can't + be / 动词原形（He must be tired. / She can't be at home.）；正在进行：must be + -ing（They must be sleeping）
zh.contrast: 推测时 must 的否定是 can't，不是 mustn't：She can't be at home（她不可能在家），不说 *She mustn't be at home（mustn't 表示禁止）。
zh.example: She isn't at work today, so she must be sick.
zh.exampleTranslation: 她今天不在公司，所以她一定生病了。

en.name: Modals of deduction: present
en.meaning: Must, might, may, could and can't + base verb make guesses about the present based on evidence: must = sure it's true, might/may/could = possible, can't = sure it's not true.
en.formation: must / might / may / could / can't + be / base verb (He must be tired. / She can't be at home.); in progress: must be + -ing (They must be sleeping)
en.contrast: The opposite of must here is can't, not mustn't: She can't be at home (it's impossible), not *She mustn't be at home (mustn't means 'not allowed').
en.example: She isn't at work today, so she must be sick.
en.exampleTranslation: She isn't at work today, so she must be sick.

fr.name: Modaux de déduction (présent)
fr.meaning: Must, might, may, could et can't + base verbale servent à faire une déduction sur le présent : must = sûrement, might/may/could = peut-être, can't = sûrement pas.
fr.formation: must / might / may / could / can't + be / base verbale (He must be tired. / She can't be at home.) ; action en cours : must be + -ing (They must be sleeping)
fr.contrast: « Elle doit être malade » = She must be ill, mais la déduction négative « elle ne peut pas être chez elle » = She can't be at home, et non *She mustn't be (qui exprime une interdiction).
fr.example: She isn't at work today, so she must be sick.
fr.exampleTranslation: Elle n'est pas au travail aujourd'hui, elle doit donc être malade.

aliases: must have, might have, can't have

zh.name: 过去推测：must have
zh.meaning: must / might / could / can't + have + 过去分词根据证据推测过去发生的事。
zh.formation: must have + 过去分词（一定已经）；might / could have + 过去分词（可能已经）；can't / couldn't have + 过去分词（不可能）
zh.contrast: must have done 是推测，had to do 是过去不得不做：He must have left（他肯定走了）/ He had to leave（他不得不走）。否定推测用 can't have，不用 mustn't have。should have done 表示责备，不是推测。
zh.example: He didn't answer the phone; he must have gone to sleep.
zh.exampleTranslation: 他没接电话，一定已经睡着了。

en.name: Modals of deduction: past
en.meaning: Must / might / could / can't + have + past participle make guesses about the past based on evidence.
en.formation: must have + past participle (sure it happened); might / could have + past participle (possible); can't / couldn't have + past participle (sure it didn't happen)
en.contrast: Must have done is a guess; had to do is a past obligation: He must have left (I'm sure he left) vs He had to leave (he was obliged to). For negative guesses use can't have, not mustn't have.
en.example: He didn't answer the phone; he must have gone to sleep.
en.exampleTranslation: He didn't answer the phone; he must have gone to sleep.

fr.name: Modaux de déduction (passé)
fr.meaning: Must / might / could / can't + have + participe passé servent à faire une déduction sur le passé.
fr.formation: must have + participe passé (a sûrement…) ; might / could have + participe passé (a peut-être…) ; can't / couldn't have + participe passé (n'a sûrement pas…)
fr.contrast: « Il a dû partir » est ambigu en français : déduction = He must have left ; obligation = He had to leave. Pour une déduction négative : can't have, et non *mustn't have.
fr.example: He didn't answer the phone; he must have gone to sleep.
fr.exampleTranslation: Il n'a pas répondu au téléphone ; il a dû s'endormir.

aliases: wish / if only for present and future wishes

zh.name: wish：对现在的愿望
zh.meaning: wish + 过去式表示希望现在的情况和事实不同，常带遗憾；这里的过去式不表示过去。
zh.formation: wish (that) + 主语 + 过去式（I wish I lived near the sea.）；be 常用 were：I wish I were taller；能力：I wish I could …
zh.contrast: 中文“希望”有两种说法：可能实现的事用 hope：I hope you pass the exam；不真实或做不到的事用 wish：I wish I had more time。不说 *I wish you pass the exam。
zh.example: I wish I lived closer to the beach.
zh.exampleTranslation: 我要是能住在海滩附近就好了。

en.name: Wish for the present
en.meaning: Wish + past tense says we want the present to be different from reality. The past form here does not mean past time.
en.formation: wish (that) + subject + past tense (I wish I lived near the sea.); be often becomes were: I wish I were taller; ability: I wish I could …
en.contrast: For things that may really happen, use hope: I hope you pass the exam. For things that are not true or not possible, use wish: I wish I had more time. Not *I wish you pass the exam.
en.example: I wish I lived closer to the beach.
en.exampleTranslation: I wish I lived closer to the beach.

fr.name: Wish pour le présent
fr.meaning: Wish + prétérit exprime le souhait que la situation présente soit différente, comme « si seulement… ». Le prétérit ne marque pas ici le passé.
fr.formation: wish (that) + sujet + prétérit (I wish I lived near the sea.) ; be devient souvent were : I wish I were taller ; capacité : I wish I could …
fr.contrast: Pour une chose possible, « souhaiter / espérer » se dit hope : I hope you pass the exam. Wish s'emploie pour l'irréel : I wish I had more time (j'aimerais avoir plus de temps). Pas de *I wish you pass.
fr.example: I wish I lived closer to the beach.
fr.exampleTranslation: Si seulement j'habitais plus près de la plage.

zh.name: wish：对过去的遗憾
zh.meaning: wish + 过去完成时（had + 过去分词）表示对过去的事感到后悔，希望当时的情况不同。
zh.formation: wish (that) + 主语 + had + 过去分词（I wish I had studied harder.）；否定：I wish I hadn't said that.；也可用 If only …
zh.contrast: 对过去的遗憾要用过去完成时：I wish I had gone，不说 *I wish I went（那是对现在的愿望）。意思相近：I should have studied harder。
zh.example: I wish I had studied harder for the exam.
zh.exampleTranslation: 我真希望考试前更努力地复习了。

en.name: Wish for past regrets
en.meaning: Wish + past perfect (had + past participle) expresses regret about the past: we want something to have happened differently.
en.formation: wish (that) + subject + had + past participle (I wish I had studied harder.); negative: I wish I hadn't said that.; also If only …
en.contrast: For past regrets use the past perfect: I wish I had gone, not *I wish I went (that is a present wish). A similar meaning: I should have studied harder.
en.example: I wish I had studied harder for the exam.
en.exampleTranslation: I wish I had studied harder for the exam.

fr.name: Wish pour regretter le passé
fr.meaning: Wish + past perfect (had + participe passé) exprime un regret sur le passé, comme « si seulement j'avais… ».
fr.formation: wish (that) + sujet + had + participe passé (I wish I had studied harder.) ; négation : I wish I hadn't said that. ; aussi If only …
fr.contrast: Pour un regret passé, il faut le past perfect : I wish I had gone (j'aurais aimé y aller), et non *I wish I went (souhait présent). Sens proche : I should have studied harder (j'aurais dû).
fr.example: I wish I had studied harder for the exam.
fr.exampleTranslation: Si seulement j'avais plus révisé pour l'examen.

zh.name: 使役动词 have 和 get
zh.meaning: have / get + 宾语 + 过去分词表示请别人（通常付钱）为自己做某事，而不是自己做。get 更口语化。
zh.formation: have / get + 物 + 过去分词（I had my hair cut. / We're getting the kitchen painted.）
zh.contrast: 中文“我剪了头发”通常是别人剪的：I had my hair cut，不说 *I cut my hair（那是自己剪）。have + 人 + 动词原形表示让某人做：I had the mechanic check the brakes。
zh.example: I need to have my car repaired this week.
zh.exampleTranslation: 我这周得找人把车修一下。

en.name: Causative have / get
en.meaning: Have / get + object + past participle means we arrange for someone else to do something for us, often for money. Get is more informal.
en.formation: have / get + thing + past participle (I had my hair cut. / We're getting the kitchen painted.)
en.contrast: I had my hair cut means a hairdresser did it; I cut my hair means I did it myself. Have + person + base verb means asking someone to do it: I had the mechanic check the brakes.
en.example: I need to have my car repaired this week.
en.exampleTranslation: I need to have my car repaired this week.

fr.name: Causatif have / get
fr.meaning: Have / get + objet + participe passé signifie qu'on fait faire quelque chose par quelqu'un d'autre, souvent contre paiement (« faire + infinitif »). Get est plus familier.
fr.formation: have / get + chose + participe passé (I had my hair cut. / We're getting the kitchen painted.)
fr.contrast: « Je me suis fait couper les cheveux » = I had my hair cut ; I cut my hair = je les ai coupés moi-même. L'ordre est fixe : objet puis participe (have my car repaired, et non *have repaired my car).
fr.example: I need to have my car repaired this week.
fr.exampleTranslation: Je dois faire réparer ma voiture cette semaine.

points.pattern: connectors of contrast (despite and in spite of)

zh.name: despite 表示让步
zh.meaning: despite / in spite of 表示“尽管”，后面接名词、代词或动词-ing，不接完整的句子。
zh.formation: Despite / In spite of + 名词 / -ing（Despite the rain, … / In spite of feeling tired, …）；接句子要用 despite the fact that + 句子
zh.contrast: despite 后面不加 of：despite the rain，不说 *despite of the rain；in spite of 才有 of。although 后面接完整句子：Although it rained, …，不说 *Despite it rained。
zh.example: Despite the heavy rain, we enjoyed our walk in the park.
zh.exampleTranslation: 尽管下着大雨，我们还是很享受在公园里的散步。

en.name: Despite and in spite of
en.meaning: Despite and in spite of mean 'although', but they are followed by a noun, pronoun or -ing form, not a full clause.
en.formation: Despite / In spite of + noun / -ing (Despite the rain, … / In spite of feeling tired, …); before a clause: despite the fact that + clause
en.contrast: No of after despite: despite the rain, not *despite of the rain (in spite of keeps of). Although takes a full clause: Although it rained, …, not *Despite it rained.
en.example: Despite the heavy rain, we enjoyed our walk in the park.
en.exampleTranslation: Despite the heavy rain, we enjoyed our walk in the park.

fr.name: Despite et in spite of
fr.meaning: Despite et in spite of signifient « malgré » : ils sont suivis d'un nom, d'un pronom ou d'une forme en -ing, pas d'une proposition.
fr.formation: Despite / In spite of + nom / -ing (Despite the rain, … / In spite of feeling tired, …) ; devant une proposition : despite the fact that + proposition
fr.contrast: Pas de of après despite : despite the rain, et non *despite of the rain (mais in spite of). Devant une proposition, utilisez although : Although it rained, …, et non *Despite it rained.
fr.example: Despite the heavy rain, we enjoyed our walk in the park.
fr.exampleTranslation: Malgré la forte pluie, nous avons profité de notre promenade dans le parc.

zh.name: so that 表目的
zh.meaning: so that + 从句表示目的，意思是“以便、好让”，从句里常用 can / could / will / would。
zh.formation: 主句 + so that + 主语 + can / could / will / would + 动词原形（I'll leave early so that I can catch the bus.）；过去用 could / would
zh.contrast: 主语相同时常用 to + 动词：She got up early to catch the train；主语不同时用 so that：I'll speak slowly so that you can understand。so that（目的）和 so（结果）不同：It rained, so we stayed home。
zh.example: She woke up early so that she could catch the first train.
zh.exampleTranslation: 她很早就起床了，好赶上头班火车。

en.name: So that (purpose)
en.meaning: So that + clause expresses purpose ('in order that'). The clause usually has can, could, will or would.
en.formation: main clause + so that + subject + can / could / will / would + base verb (I'll leave early so that I can catch the bus.); in the past use could / would
en.contrast: With the same subject, to + verb is simpler: She got up early to catch the train. With a different subject, use so that: I'll speak slowly so that you can understand. So that (purpose) is not so (result): It rained, so we stayed home.
en.example: She woke up early so that she could catch the first train.
en.exampleTranslation: She woke up early so that she could catch the first train.

fr.name: So that (but)
fr.meaning: So that + proposition exprime le but, comme « pour que / afin que ». La proposition contient souvent can, could, will ou would.
fr.formation: principale + so that + sujet + can / could / will / would + base verbale (I'll leave early so that I can catch the bus.) ; au passé : could / would
fr.contrast: « Pour que + subjonctif » se traduit par so that + modal : I'll speak slowly so that you can understand (pour que tu comprennes). Avec le même sujet, to suffit : She got up early to catch the train.
fr.example: She woke up early so that she could catch the first train.
fr.exampleTranslation: Elle s'est levée tôt pour pouvoir prendre le premier train.

zh.name: 现在进行时被动语态
zh.meaning: 现在进行时被动语态表示某事此刻或这段时间正在被做。
zh.formation: am / is / are + being + 过去分词（The road is being repaired. / Are you being served?）
zh.contrast: 一般现在时被动表示经常的情况：The room is cleaned every day；进行时被动表示正在进行：The room is being cleaned now（现在不能进去）。别漏掉 being。
zh.example: A new bridge is being built across the river.
zh.exampleTranslation: 河上正在修建一座新桥。

en.name: Present continuous passive
en.meaning: The present continuous passive says that something is being done now or around now.
en.formation: am / is / are + being + past participle (The road is being repaired. / Are you being served?)
en.contrast: The present simple passive is for regular facts: The room is cleaned every day. The continuous passive is for now: The room is being cleaned (you can't go in yet). Don't drop being.
en.example: A new bridge is being built across the river.
en.exampleTranslation: A new bridge is being built across the river.

fr.name: Passif au présent continu
fr.meaning: Le passif au présent continu indique qu'une action est en train d'être faite en ce moment.
fr.formation: am / is / are + being + participe passé (The road is being repaired. / Are you being served?)
fr.contrast: Le français dit souvent « en cours de » ou « on est en train de » : The road is being repaired = la route est en travaux. Sans being, c'est une habitude : The room is cleaned every day.
fr.example: A new bridge is being built across the river.
fr.exampleTranslation: Un nouveau pont est en construction sur la rivière.

zh.name: 过去进行时被动语态
zh.meaning: 过去进行时被动语态表示过去某个时刻某事正在被做。
zh.formation: was / were + being + 过去分词（The house was being painted when we arrived.）
zh.contrast: 一般过去时被动表示动作已完成：My car was repaired yesterday（修好了）；过去进行时被动表示当时正在进行：My car was being repaired（当时还在修）。
zh.example: My car was being repaired when you called me.
zh.exampleTranslation: 你给我打电话的时候，我的车正在修。

en.name: Past continuous passive
