en.meaning: The past continuous passive says that something was being done at a moment in the past.
en.formation: was / were + being + past participle (The house was being painted when we arrived.)
en.contrast: The past simple passive shows a finished action: My car was repaired yesterday (it's done). The continuous passive shows it was in progress: My car was being repaired (the work wasn't finished).
en.example: My car was being repaired when you called me.
en.exampleTranslation: My car was being repaired when you called me.

fr.name: Passif au passé continu
fr.meaning: Le passif au passé continu indique qu'une action était en train d'être faite à un moment du passé.
fr.formation: was / were + being + participe passé (The house was being painted when we arrived.)
fr.contrast: C'est souvent l'imparfait : My car was being repaired (ma voiture était en réparation). Le passif au prétérit indique une action terminée : My car was repaired yesterday (a été réparée hier).
fr.example: My car was being repaired when you called me.
fr.exampleTranslation: Ma voiture était en réparation quand tu m'as appelé.

zh.name: 现在完成时被动语态
zh.meaning: 现在完成时被动语态表示某事已经被做了，结果和现在有关，不说具体时间。
zh.formation: have / has + been + 过去分词（The windows have been cleaned. / Has the email been sent yet?）
zh.contrast: 有具体的过去时间时用一般过去时被动：The windows were cleaned yesterday，不说 *have been cleaned yesterday。
zh.example: All the windows have been cleaned for the party.
zh.exampleTranslation: 为了派对，所有的窗户都已经擦干净了。

en.name: Present perfect passive
en.meaning: The present perfect passive says that something has been done, with a result that matters now and no specific time.
en.formation: have / has + been + past participle (The windows have been cleaned. / Has the email been sent yet?)
en.contrast: With a specific past time, use the past simple passive: The windows were cleaned yesterday, not *have been cleaned yesterday.
en.example: All the windows have been cleaned for the party.
en.exampleTranslation: All the windows have been cleaned for the party.

fr.name: Passif au present perfect
fr.meaning: Le passif au present perfect indique qu'une action a été faite et que le résultat compte maintenant, sans moment précis.
fr.formation: have / has + been + participe passé (The windows have been cleaned. / Has the email been sent yet?)
fr.contrast: « Ont été nettoyées » se traduit par have been cleaned sans date, mais par were cleaned avec un moment passé : The windows were cleaned yesterday.
fr.example: All the windows have been cleaned for the party.
fr.exampleTranslation: Toutes les fenêtres ont été nettoyées pour la fête.

zh.name: all, every, each
zh.meaning: all 指全部（接复数或不可数名词）；every 和 each 都指“每一个”，接单数名词：every 着眼于整体，each 着眼于一个一个的个体。
zh.formation: all + 复数 / 不可数名词（all students, all the time）；every / each + 单数名词 + 单数动词（Every student has a book.）；each of / all of + the / 代词
zh.contrast: every 和 each 后面用单数名词和单数动词：Every student is here，不说 *Every students are here。可以说 each of them，但不说 *every of them。两个人或物只用 each（each hand）。
zh.example: Every student in the classroom received a new notebook.
zh.exampleTranslation: 教室里的每个学生都收到了一本新笔记本。

en.name: All, every, each
en.meaning: All means the whole group (with plural or uncountable nouns). Every and each mean all members, with a singular noun: every sees the group as a whole, each looks at members one by one.
en.formation: all + plural / uncountable noun (all students, all the time); every / each + singular noun + singular verb (Every student has a book.); each of / all of + the / pronoun
en.contrast: Every and each take a singular noun and verb: Every student is here, not *Every students are here. You can say each of them but not *every of them. For two things, only each works (each hand).
en.example: Every student in the classroom received a new notebook.
en.exampleTranslation: Every student in the classroom received a new notebook.

fr.name: All, every, each
fr.meaning: All désigne la totalité (nom pluriel ou indénombrable). Every et each signifient « chaque / tous les », avec un nom singulier : every voit le groupe entier, each considère les éléments un par un.
fr.formation: all + nom pluriel / indénombrable (all students, all the time) ; every / each + nom singulier + verbe au singulier (Every student has a book.) ; each of / all of + the / pronom
fr.contrast: « Tous les élèves » = all the students ou every student (au singulier) : Every student is here, et non *Every students are. On dit each of them, mais pas *every of them. Pour deux éléments, seulement each.
fr.example: Every student in the classroom received a new notebook.
fr.exampleTranslation: Chaque élève de la classe a reçu un nouveau cahier.

zh.name: 反身代词
zh.meaning: 反身代词（myself, yourself, himself, herself, itself, ourselves, yourselves, themselves）用于主语和宾语是同一人或物时，也可以强调“亲自”。
zh.formation: 动词 + 反身代词（I cut myself.）；强调：I made it myself.；by + 反身代词 = 独自（She lives by herself.）
zh.contrast: 很多动词在英语里不用反身代词：I feel tired，不说 *I feel myself tired；get up、relax 也一样。但 enjoy 要有宾语：Enjoy yourself!。互相做某事用 each other：They help each other。
zh.example: I cut myself while I was cooking dinner last night.
zh.exampleTranslation: 昨晚我做饭时切到自己了。

en.name: Reflexive pronouns
en.meaning: Reflexive pronouns (myself, yourself, himself, herself, itself, ourselves, yourselves, themselves) are used when the subject and object are the same, or to stress 'personally'.
en.formation: verb + reflexive pronoun (I cut myself.); emphasis: I made it myself.; by + reflexive = alone (She lives by herself.)
en.contrast: Many verbs don't take a reflexive in English: I feel tired, not *I feel myself tired; also get up, relax. But enjoy needs an object: Enjoy yourself! For doing something to one another, use each other.
en.example: I cut myself while I was cooking dinner last night.
en.exampleTranslation: I cut myself while I was cooking dinner last night.

fr.name: Pronoms réfléchis
fr.meaning: Les pronoms réfléchis (myself, yourself, himself, herself, itself, ourselves, yourselves, themselves) s'emploient quand le sujet et le complément sont la même personne, ou pour insister (« moi-même »).
fr.formation: verbe + pronom réfléchi (I cut myself.) ; insistance : I made it myself. ; by + pronom réfléchi = seul (She lives by herself.)
fr.contrast: Beaucoup de verbes pronominaux français ne le sont pas en anglais : je me sens fatigué = I feel tired, je me lève = I get up, je me souviens = I remember. « Ils se parlent » (l'un l'autre) = They talk to each other.
fr.example: I cut myself while I was cooking dinner last night.
fr.exampleTranslation: Je me suis coupé en préparant le dîner hier soir.

aliases: give something to someone vs give someone something

zh.name: 双宾语动词
zh.meaning: give、send、show、tell、buy、make 等动词可以接两个宾语：间接宾语（人）和直接宾语（物）。
zh.formation: 动词 + 人 + 物（She gave me a book）；动词 + 物 + to / for + 人（She gave a book to me / She bought a cake for me）；give、send、show 用 to，buy、make、get 用 for
zh.contrast: explain、describe、suggest、say 不能直接接人作宾语：Explain the rule to me，不说 *Explain me the rule。物是代词时用 to / for 结构：Give it to me。
zh.example: She bought her best friend a wonderful birthday present.
zh.exampleTranslation: 她给最好的朋友买了一份很棒的生日礼物。

en.name: Verbs with two objects
en.meaning: Verbs such as give, send, show, tell, buy and make can take two objects: an indirect object (the person) and a direct object (the thing).
en.formation: verb + person + thing (She gave me a book); verb + thing + to / for + person (She gave a book to me / She bought a cake for me); give, send, show take to; buy, make, get take for
en.contrast: Explain, describe, suggest and say can't take the person directly: Explain the rule to me, not *Explain me the rule. When the thing is a pronoun, use to/for: Give it to me.
en.example: She bought her best friend a wonderful birthday present.
en.exampleTranslation: She bought her best friend a wonderful birthday present.

fr.name: Verbes à double objet
fr.meaning: Des verbes comme give, send, show, tell, buy ou make peuvent avoir deux compléments : la personne (complément indirect) et la chose (complément direct).
fr.formation: verbe + personne + chose (She gave me a book) ; verbe + chose + to / for + personne (She gave a book to me / She bought a cake for me) ; give, send, show → to ; buy, make, get → for
fr.contrast: « Expliquer quelque chose à quelqu'un » : Explain the rule to me, et non *Explain me the rule (de même describe, suggest, say). Pas de préposition si la personne vient en premier : She gave me a book, et non *She gave to me a book.
fr.example: She bought her best friend a wonderful birthday present.
fr.exampleTranslation: Elle a acheté un magnifique cadeau d'anniversaire à sa meilleure amie.

points.pattern: zero article with names and places

zh.name: 专有名词的零冠词
zh.meaning: 大多数人名、城市名、国家名、街道名、湖泊和单座山的名字前不用冠词。
zh.formation: 无冠词 + 人名 / 城市 / 大多数国家 / 街道 / 单座山 / 湖（Tom, London, Japan, Oxford Street, Mount Fuji, Lake Geneva）
zh.contrast: 例外要加 the：含 States、Kingdom、Republic 或复数形式的国名（the USA, the UK, the Netherlands）；河流、海洋、山脉（the Thames, the Pacific, the Alps）。
zh.example: London is a very busy city with a long history.
zh.exampleTranslation: 伦敦是一个历史悠久且非常繁忙的城市。

en.name: Zero article with names
en.meaning: Most names of people, cities, countries, streets, lakes and single mountains take no article.
en.formation: no article + person / city / most countries / street / single mountain / lake (Tom, London, Japan, Oxford Street, Mount Fuji, Lake Geneva)
en.contrast: Exceptions with the: countries with States, Kingdom, Republic or a plural form (the USA, the UK, the Netherlands); rivers, seas, oceans and mountain ranges (the Thames, the Pacific, the Alps).
en.example: London is a very busy city with a long history.
en.exampleTranslation: London is a very busy city with a long history.

fr.name: Article zéro et noms propres
fr.meaning: La plupart des noms de personnes, de villes, de pays, de rues, de lacs et de montagnes isolées s'emploient sans article.
fr.formation: pas d'article + personne / ville / la plupart des pays / rue / montagne / lac (Tom, London, Japan, Oxford Street, Mount Fuji, Lake Geneva)
fr.contrast: Contrairement au français (la France, le Japon), on dit France, Japan, sans article. Exceptions avec the : the USA, the UK, the Netherlands ; fleuves, mers et chaînes de montagnes (the Thames, the Alps).
fr.example: London is a very busy city with a long history.
fr.exampleTranslation: Londres est une ville très animée, avec une longue histoire.

zh.name: should have 表示责备
zh.meaning: should have + 过去分词表示过去本该做却没做（批评或后悔）；shouldn't have + 过去分词表示过去不该做却做了。
zh.formation: should have + 过去分词（You should have told me.）；shouldn't have + 过去分词（I shouldn't have eaten so much.）
zh.contrast: should have done 是“本该做”（实际没做），must have done 是“一定做过”（推测）：You should have called（你本该打电话）/ You must have called（你肯定打过）。could have done 表示“本来可以”。
zh.example: You should have asked me before you used my computer.
zh.exampleTranslation: 你用我的电脑之前应该先问问我。

en.name: Should have (past criticism)
en.meaning: Should have + past participle says something was the right thing to do but didn't happen (criticism or regret); shouldn't have says something happened but was wrong.
en.formation: should have + past participle (You should have told me.); shouldn't have + past participle (I shouldn't have eaten so much.)
en.contrast: Should have done = it was a good idea, but you didn't; must have done = I'm sure you did: You should have called (you didn't) vs You must have called (I think you did). Could have done = it was possible.
en.example: You should have asked me before you used my computer.
en.exampleTranslation: You should have asked me before you used my computer.

fr.name: Should have (reproche, regret)
fr.meaning: Should have + participe passé exprime ce qu'il aurait fallu faire (reproche ou regret) ; shouldn't have, ce qu'il n'aurait pas fallu faire.
fr.formation: should have + participe passé (You should have told me.) ; shouldn't have + participe passé (I shouldn't have eaten so much.)
fr.contrast: « Tu aurais dû » = You should have…, mais « tu as dû » (déduction) = You must have… : You should have called (tu aurais dû appeler) / You must have called (tu as dû appeler). Could have = tu aurais pu.
fr.example: You should have asked me before you used my computer.
fr.exampleTranslation: Tu aurais dû me demander avant d'utiliser mon ordinateur.

aliases: prefer doing vs prefer to do

zh.name: would rather 宁愿
zh.meaning: prefer、would prefer、would rather 都表示“更喜欢、宁愿”：prefer 表示一般的偏好，would prefer / would rather 表示这一次的选择。
zh.formation: prefer + 名词 / -ing + to …（I prefer tea to coffee）；would prefer + to + 动词原形（I'd prefer to stay）；would rather + 动词原形 + than …（I'd rather stay than go）
zh.contrast: would rather 后接动词原形，不加 to：I'd rather stay，不说 *I'd rather to stay；would prefer 后要加 to：I'd prefer to stay。比较时用 prefer A to B，would rather A than B。
zh.example: I would rather stay at home and read a book tonight.
zh.exampleTranslation: 我今晚宁愿待在家里看书。

en.name: Prefer and would rather
en.meaning: Prefer, would prefer and would rather all show what we like more: prefer is a general preference; would prefer and would rather are about a particular choice.
en.formation: prefer + noun / -ing + to … (I prefer tea to coffee); would prefer + to + base verb (I'd prefer to stay); would rather + base verb + than … (I'd rather stay than go)
en.contrast: Would rather takes the base verb with no to: I'd rather stay, not *I'd rather to stay. Would prefer needs to: I'd prefer to stay. Compare: prefer A to B, but would rather A than B.
en.example: I would rather stay at home and read a book tonight.
en.exampleTranslation: I would rather stay at home and read a book tonight.

fr.name: Prefer et would rather
fr.meaning: Prefer, would prefer et would rather expriment une préférence : prefer, en général ; would prefer et would rather, pour un choix précis (« je préférerais »).
fr.formation: prefer + nom / -ing + to … (I prefer tea to coffee) ; would prefer + to + base verbale (I'd prefer to stay) ; would rather + base verbale + than … (I'd rather stay than go)
fr.contrast: Would rather est suivi de la base verbale sans to : I'd rather stay, et non *I'd rather to stay ; would prefer prend to : I'd prefer to stay. « Préférer A à B » : prefer A to B, mais would rather A than B.
fr.example: I would rather stay at home and read a book tonight.
fr.exampleTranslation: Ce soir, je préférerais rester à la maison et lire un livre.

zh.name: whose 引导的定语从句
zh.meaning: whose 引导定语从句，表示所属关系，意思是“……的”，可以指人也可以指物。
zh.formation: 名词 + whose + 名词 + 从句（the woman whose car was stolen / a house whose windows are blue）
zh.contrast: whose 后面必须紧跟名词，不要写成 who's（= who is）。从句里不要再加物主代词：a woman whose car was stolen，不说 *a woman who her car was stolen。
zh.example: I met a woman whose car was stolen outside the supermarket.
zh.exampleTranslation: 我遇到了一位女士，她的车在超市外面被偷了。

en.name: Relative clauses with whose
en.meaning: Whose introduces a relative clause that shows possession ('of whom / of which'). It is used for people and things.
en.formation: noun + whose + noun + clause (the woman whose car was stolen / a house whose windows are blue)
en.contrast: Whose is always followed by a noun; don't confuse it with who's (who is). Don't add a possessive: a woman whose car was stolen, not *a woman who her car was stolen.
en.example: I met a woman whose car was stolen outside the supermarket.
en.exampleTranslation: I met a woman whose car was stolen outside the supermarket.

fr.name: Relatives avec whose
fr.meaning: Whose introduit une relative qui exprime la possession, comme « dont + nom ». Il s'emploie pour les personnes et les choses.
fr.formation: nom + whose + nom + proposition (the woman whose car was stolen / a house whose windows are blue)
fr.contrast: Whose ne traduit « dont » que pour la possession : la femme dont la voiture… = the woman whose car… Mais « le film dont je t'ai parlé » = the film (that) I told you about. Ne confondez pas avec who's (who is).
fr.example: I met a woman whose car was stolen outside the supermarket.
fr.exampleTranslation: J'ai rencontré une femme dont la voiture a été volée devant le supermarché.

zh.name: -ever 词
zh.meaning: whatever、whoever、wherever、whenever、however 表示“无论什么 / 谁 / 哪里 / 何时 / 怎样”，也可以表示“任何……都可以”。
zh.formation: -ever 词 + 主语 + 动词（Call me whenever you need help. / Sit wherever you like.）；也可说 no matter what / when / where
zh.contrast: when 指某一次具体的时间：Call me when you arrive（到了打给我）；whenever 指“任何时候”：Call me whenever you need help。where 与 wherever 也一样。
zh.example: You can call me whenever you need help.
zh.exampleTranslation: 无论你什么时候需要帮助，都可以给我打电话。

en.name: -ever words
en.meaning: Whatever, whoever, wherever, whenever and however mean 'no matter what / who / where / when / how' or 'any … at all'. They introduce a clause.
en.formation: -ever word + subject + verb (Call me whenever you need help. / Sit wherever you like.); also no matter what / when / where
en.contrast: When refers to one particular time: Call me when you arrive. Whenever means 'any time': Call me whenever you need help. Likewise where (one place) vs wherever (any place).
en.example: You can call me whenever you need help.
en.exampleTranslation: You can call me whenever you need help.

fr.name: Mots en -ever
fr.meaning: Whatever, whoever, wherever, whenever et however signifient « quoi que / qui que / où que / chaque fois que / de quelque façon que », ou « n'importe quel… ».
fr.formation: mot en -ever + sujet + verbe (Call me whenever you need help. / Sit wherever you like.) ; aussi no matter what / when / where
fr.contrast: When renvoie à un moment précis : Call me when you arrive (quand tu arrives). Whenever signifie « chaque fois que / n'importe quand » : Call me whenever you need help. Pas de subjonctif : whatever you do (quoi que tu fasses).
fr.example: You can call me whenever you need help.
fr.exampleTranslation: Tu peux m'appeler chaque fois que tu as besoin d'aide.

aliases: what a nice day, how interesting
exclamatory sentences with what and how
what a day and how nice

zh.name: what和how感叹句
zh.meaning: what 和 how 开头的感叹句用来表达惊讶、赞美等强烈感情。
zh.formation: What + a / an + 形容词 + 单数名词（What a nice day!）；What + 形容词 + 复数 / 不可数名词（What nice people! / What bad weather!）；How + 形容词 / 副词（How kind! / How fast he runs!）
zh.contrast: what 后面接名词短语，how 后面接形容词或副词：What a beautiful day! / How beautiful!，不说 *What beautiful! / *How a beautiful day!。不可数名词前不加 a：What bad weather!。感叹句不倒装：What a cake she made!
zh.example: What a delicious cake she made for the party!
zh.exampleTranslation: 她为派对做的蛋糕真好吃啊！

en.name: Exclamations with what and how
en.meaning: Exclamations with what and how express strong feelings such as surprise or admiration.
en.formation: What + a / an + adjective + singular noun (What a nice day!); What + adjective + plural / uncountable noun (What nice people! / What bad weather!); How + adjective / adverb (How kind! / How fast he runs!)
en.contrast: What goes with a noun phrase, how with an adjective or adverb: What a beautiful day! / How beautiful!, not *What beautiful! or *How a beautiful day! No a with uncountable nouns: What bad weather! No question word order: What a cake she made!
en.example: What a delicious cake she made for the party!
en.exampleTranslation: What a delicious cake she made for the party!

fr.name: Exclamations avec what et how
fr.meaning: Les exclamations en what et how expriment une émotion forte comme la surprise ou l'admiration (« Quel… ! », « Comme… ! »).
fr.formation: What + a / an + adjectif + nom singulier (What a nice day!) ; What + adjectif + nom pluriel / indénombrable (What nice people! / What bad weather!) ; How + adjectif / adverbe (How kind! / How fast he runs!)
fr.contrast: « Quel » se traduit par what (+ a devant un nom singulier comptable) : What a nice day!, mais What bad weather! (indénombrable). « Comme c'est beau ! » = How beautiful!, et non *What beautiful!
fr.example: What a delicious cake she made for the party!
fr.exampleTranslation: Quel délicieux gâteau elle a fait pour la fête !

zh.name: by、until、during
zh.meaning: during 和 while 表示“在……期间”，by 表示“不迟于（截止时间）”，until 表示“一直到”。
zh.formation: during + 名词（during the film）；while + 句子（while I was sleeping）；by + 时间点（by Friday）；until / till + 时间点（until 6 p.m.）
zh.contrast: by 是截止时间，until 是一直持续到：Finish it by Friday（周五前完成）/ I'll wait until Friday（一直等到周五）。during 说明“什么时候”，for 说明“多长时间”：during the holiday / for two weeks；during 后接名词，while 后接句子。
zh.example: I will finish the report by Friday afternoon.
zh.exampleTranslation: 我会在星期五下午之前完成这份报告。

en.name: During, while, by, until
en.meaning: During and while mean 'in the time of'; by means 'not later than' (a deadline); until means 'up to' a time.
en.formation: during + noun (during the film); while + clause (while I was sleeping); by + point in time (by Friday); until / till + point in time (until 6 p.m.)
en.contrast: By is a deadline; until is a continuing state: Finish it by Friday vs I'll wait until Friday. During says when, for says how long: during the holiday / for two weeks. During takes a noun, while takes a clause.
en.example: I will finish the report by Friday afternoon.
en.exampleTranslation: I will finish the report by Friday afternoon.

fr.name: During, while, by, until
fr.meaning: During et while signifient « pendant » ; by signifie « au plus tard, d'ici » (une échéance) ; until signifie « jusqu'à ».
fr.formation: during + nom (during the film) ; while + proposition (while I was sleeping) ; by + moment (by Friday) ; until / till + moment (until 6 p.m.)
fr.contrast: « Pendant » a trois traductions : during + nom (during the film), while + proposition (while I was sleeping), for + durée (for two weeks). By = d'ici / au plus tard (by Friday) ; until = jusqu'à (until Friday).
fr.example: I will finish the report by Friday afternoon.
fr.exampleTranslation: Je finirai le rapport d'ici vendredi après-midi.

zh.name: 转述动词
zh.meaning: agree、refuse、promise、suggest、admit、deny 等转述动词可以概括别人说的话，比 say 更准确，后面接 to + 动词或 -ing。
zh.formation: agree / refuse / promise / offer + to + 动词原形（She refused to help）；suggest / admit / deny + 动词-ing（He admitted taking it）；advise / warn / remind + 人 + to + 动词原形
zh.contrast: suggest 后面不能用“人 + to do”：She suggested going / She suggested (that) we go，不说 *She suggested us to go。说“建议某人做”可以用 advise：She advised us to go。
zh.example: She refused to share her answers with him.
zh.exampleTranslation: 她拒绝和他分享她的答案。

en.name: Reporting verbs
en.meaning: Reporting verbs such as agree, refuse, promise, suggest, admit and deny summarise what someone said more precisely than say. They are followed by to + verb or -ing.
en.formation: agree / refuse / promise / offer + to + base verb (She refused to help); suggest / admit / deny + verb-ing (He admitted taking it); advise / warn / remind + person + to + base verb
en.contrast: Suggest can't take person + to: She suggested going / She suggested (that) we go, not *She suggested us to go. To tell someone what to do, use advise: She advised us to go.
en.example: She refused to share her answers with him.
en.exampleTranslation: She refused to share her answers with him.

fr.name: Verbes introducteurs
fr.meaning: Des verbes introducteurs comme agree, refuse, promise, suggest, admit ou deny résument des paroles plus précisément que say. Ils sont suivis de to + verbe ou de -ing.
fr.formation: agree / refuse / promise / offer + to + base verbale (She refused to help) ; suggest / admit / deny + verbe-ing (He admitted taking it) ; advise / warn / remind + personne + to + base verbale
fr.contrast: « Suggérer à quelqu'un de faire » ne se traduit pas mot à mot : She suggested going / She suggested (that) we go, et non *She suggested us to go. Pour un conseil : She advised us to go.
fr.example: She refused to share her answers with him.
fr.exampleTranslation: Elle a refusé de lui montrer ses réponses.

points.pattern: conditionals with unless, provided that, as long as

zh.name: unless 和条件连词
zh.meaning: unless 意思是“除非、如果不”（= if … not）；provided (that) 和 as long as 意思是“只要、前提是”。
zh.formation: unless + 一般现在时, will …（We'll be late unless we hurry.）；as long as / provided (that) + 一般现在时（You can go out as long as you're back by ten.）
zh.contrast: unless 本身已含否定，从句不再用 not：unless we hurry，不说 *unless we don't hurry。和 if 一样，unless 后面不用 will：unless it rains，不说 *unless it will rain。
zh.example: We will miss the train unless we leave right now.
zh.exampleTranslation: 除非我们现在就出发，否则我们会赶不上火车的。

en.name: Unless, as long as, provided
en.meaning: Unless means 'if … not'. Provided (that) and as long as mean 'only if'.
en.formation: unless + present simple, will … (We'll be late unless we hurry.); as long as / provided (that) + present simple (You can go out as long as you're back by ten.)
en.contrast: Unless is already negative, so no extra not: unless we hurry, not *unless we don't hurry. As with if, no will after unless: unless it rains, not *unless it will rain.
en.example: We will miss the train unless we leave right now.
en.exampleTranslation: We will miss the train unless we leave right now.

fr.name: Unless, as long as, provided
fr.meaning: Unless signifie « à moins que / si … ne … pas ». Provided (that) et as long as signifient « à condition que / pourvu que ».
fr.formation: unless + présent simple, will … (We'll be late unless we hurry.) ; as long as / provided (that) + présent simple (You can go out as long as you're back by ten.)
fr.contrast: Unless contient déjà la négation : unless we hurry (si on ne se dépêche pas), et non *unless we don't hurry. Ni subjonctif ni will : unless it rains (à moins qu'il ne pleuve).
fr.example: We will miss the train unless we leave right now.
fr.exampleTranslation: Nous raterons le train si nous ne partons pas tout de suite.

points.pattern: infinitives and gerunds with change in meaning
aliases: remember to do vs remember doing
stop to do vs stop doing

zh.name: to do 与 -ing 辨析
zh.meaning: remember、forget、stop、try、regret 后面可接 to do 或 -ing，但意思不同：to do 多指之后要做的事，-ing 多指已经做过或正在做的事。
zh.formation: remember / forget to do（记得 / 忘了去做）vs remember / forget doing（记得 / 忘了做过）；stop doing（停止做）vs stop to do（停下来去做）；try to do（努力做）vs try doing（试着做做看）
zh.contrast: 最典型的一对：He stopped smoking（他戒烟了）/ He stopped to smoke（他停下来抽烟）。I remember meeting her（记得见过她）/ Remember to call her（记得给她打电话）。
zh.example: Please remember to lock the door before you go to bed.
zh.exampleTranslation: 睡觉前请记得锁门。

en.name: To do or -ing (meaning)
en.meaning: Remember, forget, stop, try and regret can take to do or -ing, with different meanings: to do usually looks ahead, -ing looks back or at the activity itself.
en.formation: remember / forget to do (a task) vs remember / forget doing (a memory); stop doing (quit) vs stop to do (stop in order to); try to do (make an effort) vs try doing (as an experiment)
en.contrast: The classic pair: He stopped smoking (he quit) vs He stopped to smoke (he paused in order to smoke). I remember meeting her (a memory) vs Remember to call her (a task).
en.example: Please remember to lock the door before you go to bed.
en.exampleTranslation: Please remember to lock the door before you go to bed.

fr.name: To ou -ing (sens)
fr.meaning: Remember, forget, stop, try et regret acceptent to + verbe ou -ing, avec des sens différents : to regarde vers l'avenir, -ing vers le passé ou l'activité elle-même.
fr.formation: remember / forget to do (penser à / oublier de faire) vs remember / forget doing (se souvenir d'avoir fait) ; stop doing (arrêter de) vs stop to do (s'arrêter pour) ; try to do (essayer de) vs try doing (essayer, pour voir)
fr.contrast: La paire classique : He stopped smoking (il a arrêté de fumer) / He stopped to smoke (il s'est arrêté pour fumer). I remember meeting her (je me souviens de l'avoir rencontrée) / Remember to call her (pense à l'appeler).
fr.example: Please remember to lock the door before you go to bed.
fr.exampleTranslation: N'oublie pas de fermer la porte à clé avant d'aller te coucher.

aliases: much, a lot, slightly with comparatives

zh.name: 比较级修饰语
zh.meaning: 在比较级前加 much、far、a lot、a bit、slightly、even 等词，说明差别大还是小。
zh.formation: much / far / a lot + 比较级（much faster）；a bit / a little / slightly + 比较级（a bit cheaper）；even + 比较级（even better）
zh.contrast: very 不能修饰比较级：much faster，不说 *very faster（中文“快很多”）。长形容词：much more expensive，不说 *very more expensive。
zh.example: Your car is much faster than mine.
zh.exampleTranslation: 你的车比我的快得多。

en.name: Modifying comparatives
en.meaning: Words like much, far, a lot, a bit, slightly and even go before a comparative to show whether the difference is big or small.
en.formation: much / far / a lot + comparative (much faster); a bit / a little / slightly + comparative (a bit cheaper); even + comparative (even better)
en.contrast: Very can't modify a comparative: much faster, not *very faster. With long adjectives: much more expensive, not *very more expensive.
en.example: Your car is much faster than mine.
en.exampleTranslation: Your car is much faster than mine.

fr.name: Nuancer un comparatif
fr.meaning: Des mots comme much, far, a lot, a bit, slightly ou even se placent devant un comparatif pour indiquer si la différence est grande ou petite.
fr.formation: much / far / a lot + comparatif (much faster) ; a bit / a little / slightly + comparatif (a bit cheaper) ; even + comparatif (even better)
fr.contrast: « Beaucoup plus » se dit much (ou far, a lot) + comparatif : much faster, et non *very faster. « Encore mieux » = even better.
fr.example: Your car is much faster than mine.
fr.exampleTranslation: Ta voiture est beaucoup plus rapide que la mienne.

zh.name: 转述命令和请求
zh.meaning: 转述命令和请求时，把祈使句变成“tell / ask + 人 + to + 动词原形”。
zh.formation: tell / ask / order / advise + 人 + to + 动词原形（She told me to wait.）；否定：+ not to + 动词原形（He asked us not to shout.）
zh.contrast: 否定把 not 放在 to 前面：He told us not to run，不说 *He told us don't run。say 不能这样用：She told me to go，不说 *She said me to go。
zh.example: The teacher told us to open our books.
zh.exampleTranslation: 老师让我们打开书。

en.name: Reported commands and requests
en.meaning: To report an order or request, change the imperative into tell / ask + person + to + base verb.
en.formation: tell / ask / order / advise + person + to + base verb (She told me to wait.); negative: + not to + base verb (He asked us not to shout.)
en.contrast: For the negative, put not before to: He told us not to run, not *He told us don't run. Say doesn't work this way: She told me to go, not *She said me to go.
en.example: The teacher told us to open our books.
en.exampleTranslation: The teacher told us to open our books.

fr.name: Ordres et demandes rapportés
fr.meaning: Pour rapporter un ordre ou une demande, l'impératif devient tell / ask + personne + to + base verbale (« dire / demander à quelqu'un de faire »).
fr.formation: tell / ask / order / advise + personne + to + base verbale (She told me to wait.) ; négation : + not to + base verbale (He asked us not to shout.)
fr.contrast: « Dire à quelqu'un de faire » = tell someone to do, et non *say someone to do. « De ne pas » = not to : He told us not to run (il nous a dit de ne pas courir).
fr.example: The teacher told us to open our books.
fr.exampleTranslation: Le professeur nous a dit d'ouvrir nos livres.

points.pattern: passives with modals (must be done, should be done)

zh.name: 情态动词被动语态
zh.meaning: 情态动词被动语态表示某事必须 / 应该 / 可以被做，重点在动作的对象。
zh.formation: 情态动词 + be + 过去分词（It must be signed. / It can be done. / It should be cleaned.）；过去：should have been + 过去分词
zh.contrast: 不能漏掉 be，也不能用动词原形：The form must be signed，不说 *must signed / *must be sign。物作主语时要用被动：The work can be done today，不说 *The work can do today。
zh.example: This form must be signed by the manager.
zh.exampleTranslation: 这张表格必须由经理签字。

en.name: Passive with modals
en.meaning: Modal passives say that something must, should or can be done, focusing on the thing rather than the doer.
en.formation: modal + be + past participle (It must be signed. / It can be done. / It should be cleaned.); past: should have been + past participle
en.contrast: Don't drop be or use the base verb: The form must be signed, not *must signed or *must be sign. A thing as subject needs the passive: The work can be done today, not *The work can do today.
en.example: This form must be signed by the manager.
en.exampleTranslation: This form must be signed by the manager.

fr.name: Passif avec modaux
fr.meaning: Le passif avec un modal indique qu'une chose doit, devrait ou peut être faite, en mettant l'accent sur la chose plutôt que sur l'auteur.
fr.formation: modal + be + participe passé (It must be signed. / It can be done. / It should be cleaned.) ; passé : should have been + participe passé
fr.contrast: Comme « doit être signé » : must be signed, avec be et le participe. « On peut le faire aujourd'hui » se dit souvent au passif : It can be done today, et non *It can do today.
fr.example: This form must be signed by the manager.
fr.exampleTranslation: Ce formulaire doit être signé par le directeur.

zh.name: 现在完成进行时
zh.meaning: 现在完成进行时表示从过去开始、一直持续到现在（或刚刚结束）的动作，强调过程和时间长度。
zh.formation: have / has + been + 动词-ing（I've been waiting for an hour. / How long have you been learning English?）
zh.contrast: 现在完成时强调结果或数量：I've written three emails；完成进行时强调过程：I've been writing emails all morning。know、like 等状态动词用现在完成时：I've known her for years，不说 *I've been knowing her。
zh.example: I have been waiting for the bus for twenty minutes.
zh.exampleTranslation: 我等公交车已经等了二十分钟了。

en.name: Present perfect continuous
en.meaning: The present perfect continuous describes an activity that started in the past and has continued until now (or just stopped), stressing duration.
en.formation: have / has + been + verb-ing (I've been waiting for an hour. / How long have you been learning English?)
en.contrast: The present perfect simple stresses a result or number: I've written three emails. The continuous stresses the activity: I've been writing emails all morning. State verbs use the simple form: I've known her for years, not *I've been knowing her.
en.example: I have been waiting for the bus for twenty minutes.
en.exampleTranslation: I have been waiting for the bus for twenty minutes.

fr.name: Present perfect continu
fr.meaning: Le present perfect continu décrit une activité commencée dans le passé qui dure jusqu'à maintenant (ou vient de s'arrêter), en insistant sur la durée.
fr.formation: have / has + been + verbe-ing (I've been waiting for an hour. / How long have you been learning English?)
fr.contrast: « J'attends depuis une heure » = I've been waiting for an hour, et non *I wait since an hour. Le present perfect simple insiste sur le résultat (I've written three emails), le continu sur l'activité (I've been writing emails all morning).
fr.example: I have been waiting for the bus for twenty minutes.
fr.exampleTranslation: J'attends le bus depuis vingt minutes.

zh.name: be supposed to
zh.meaning: be supposed to + 动词原形表示按规定、安排或大家的期待“应该”做某事；was / were supposed to 常表示本该发生却没有发生。
zh.formation: am / is / are supposed to + 动词原形（You're supposed to wear a helmet.）；过去：was / were supposed to（The train was supposed to arrive at six.）
zh.contrast: 不要漏掉 be 和 -d：We are supposed to go，不说 *We suppose to go。should 是说话人的建议，be supposed to 是规则或别人的期待；was supposed to 往往暗示“结果没做到”。
zh.example: We are supposed to wear safety glasses in the lab.
zh.exampleTranslation: 在实验室里我们应该戴护目镜。

en.name: Be supposed to
en.meaning: Be supposed to + base verb says what is expected because of a rule, plan or arrangement. Was/were supposed to often means it was expected but didn't happen.
en.formation: am / is / are supposed to + base verb (You're supposed to wear a helmet.); past: was / were supposed to (The train was supposed to arrive at six.)
en.contrast: Don't drop be or -d: We are supposed to go, not *We suppose to go. Should is the speaker's advice; be supposed to is a rule or someone else's expectation. Was supposed to usually means it didn't happen.
en.example: We are supposed to wear safety glasses in the lab.
en.exampleTranslation: We are supposed to wear safety glasses in the lab.

fr.name: Be supposed to
fr.meaning: Be supposed to + base verbale signifie « être censé » : ce qui est attendu selon une règle, un plan ou un accord. Au passé, cela signifie souvent que ça ne s'est pas fait.
fr.formation: am / is / are supposed to + base verbale (You're supposed to wear a helmet.) ; passé : was / were supposed to (The train was supposed to arrive at six.)
fr.contrast: N'oubliez ni be ni -d : We are supposed to go, et non *We suppose to go. Should est un conseil du locuteur ; be supposed to, une règle ou une attente. The train was supposed to arrive at six = il devait arriver à six heures (mais non).
fr.example: We are supposed to wear safety glasses in the lab.
fr.exampleTranslation: Nous sommes censés porter des lunettes de protection dans le laboratoire.

zh.name: had better 最好
zh.meaning: had better + 动词原形表示“最好……”，是语气很强的建议或警告，暗示不这样做会有麻烦。
zh.formation: 主语 + had better（'d better）+ 动词原形（You'd better hurry.）；否定：had better not + 动词原形（You'd better not be late.）
zh.contrast: 虽然有 had，却指现在或将来，不指过去。后面不加 to：You'd better go，不说 *You'd better to go。否定是 had better not，不说 *hadn't better。比 should 语气强，带警告意味。
zh.example: You had better check the weather before you go out.
zh.exampleTranslation: 你出门前最好看一下天气。

en.name: Had better
en.meaning: Had better + base verb gives strong advice or a warning: something bad may happen if you don't.
en.formation: subject + had better ('d better) + base verb (You'd better hurry.); negative: had better not + base verb (You'd better not be late.)
en.contrast: Despite had, it refers to now or the future, not the past. No to: You'd better go, not *You'd better to go. The negative is had better not, not *hadn't better. It is stronger than should and sounds like a warning.
en.example: You had better check the weather before you go out.
en.exampleTranslation: You had better check the weather before you go out.

fr.name: Had better
fr.meaning: Had better + base verbale donne un conseil appuyé ou un avertissement, comme « tu ferais mieux de » : sinon, il y aura un problème.
fr.formation: sujet + had better ('d better) + base verbale (You'd better hurry.) ; négation : had better not + base verbale (You'd better not be late.)
fr.contrast: Malgré had, il s'agit du présent ou du futur. Pas de to : You'd better go, et non *You'd better to go. Négation : had better not, et non *hadn't better. C'est plus fort que should.
fr.example: You had better check the weather before you go out.
fr.exampleTranslation: Tu ferais mieux de consulter la météo avant de sortir.

zh.name: 动词+宾语+不定式
zh.meaning: want、ask、tell、expect、allow、would like 等动词后面先接宾语（人），再接 to + 动词原形，表示希望 / 要求某人做某事。
zh.formation: 动词 + 宾语 + to + 动词原形（I want you to come. / She asked me to help.）；否定：+ not to（He told me not to wait.）
zh.contrast: to 不能省略：I want you to come，不说 *I want you come；也不用 that 从句：不说 *I want that you come。但 make 和 let 后面不加 to：She made me wait / Let me go。
zh.example: She wants her brother to help her with the project.
zh.exampleTranslation: 她想让弟弟帮她做这个项目。

en.name: Verb + object + to-infinitive
en.meaning: Verbs such as want, ask, tell, expect, allow and would like take an object (the person) and then to + base verb.
en.formation: verb + object + to + base verb (I want you to come. / She asked me to help.); negative: + not to (He told me not to wait.)
en.contrast: Don't drop to: I want you to come, not *I want you come, and don't use a that-clause: not *I want that you come. But make and let take no to: She made me wait / Let me go.
en.example: She wants her brother to help her with the project.
en.exampleTranslation: She wants her brother to help her with the project.

fr.name: Verbe + complément + infinitif
fr.meaning: Des verbes comme want, ask, tell, expect, allow ou would like sont suivis d'un complément (la personne) puis de to + base verbale.
fr.formation: verbe + complément + to + base verbale (I want you to come. / She asked me to help.) ; négation : + not to (He told me not to wait.)
fr.contrast: « Je veux que tu viennes » se dit I want you to come, et non *I want that you come. Mais make et let n'ont pas de to : She made me wait (elle m'a fait attendre), Let me go.
fr.example: She wants her brother to help her with the project.
fr.exampleTranslation: Elle veut que son frère l'aide pour son projet.

zh.name: -ed 和 -ing 形容词
zh.meaning: -ed 形容词描述人的感受（感到……），-ing 形容词描述引起这种感受的人或事物（令人……）。
zh.formation: bored / boring，interested / interesting，tired / tiring，excited / exciting，surprised / surprising（I'm interested in the film. / The film is interesting.）
zh.contrast: 中文“我很无聊”是 I'm bored（我感到无聊），不说 *I'm boring（那是“我这个人很无趣”）。人也可以用 -ing：He is boring = 他让别人觉得乏味。
zh.example: The lesson was boring, so all the students were bored.
zh.exampleTranslation: 这节课很无聊，所以学生们都觉得没意思。

en.name: -ed and -ing adjectives
en.meaning: -ed adjectives describe how a person feels; -ing adjectives describe the person or thing that causes the feeling.
en.formation: bored / boring, interested / interesting, tired / tiring, excited / exciting, surprised / surprising (I'm interested in the film. / The film is interesting.)
en.contrast: I'm bored means I feel bored; I'm boring means I make other people bored. People can be -ing too: He is boring = he makes others feel bored.
en.example: The lesson was boring, so all the students were bored.
en.exampleTranslation: The lesson was boring, so all the students were bored.

fr.name: Adjectifs en -ed et -ing
fr.meaning: Les adjectifs en -ed décrivent ce que ressent une personne ; ceux en -ing décrivent la personne ou la chose qui provoque ce sentiment.
fr.formation: bored / boring, interested / interesting, tired / tiring, excited / exciting, surprised / surprising (I'm interested in the film. / The film is interesting.)
fr.contrast: « Je m'ennuie » = I'm bored ; I'm boring signifie « je suis ennuyeux ». De même : I'm interested (ça m'intéresse) / It's interesting (c'est intéressant).
fr.example: The lesson was boring, so all the students were bored.
fr.exampleTranslation: Le cours était ennuyeux, alors tous les élèves s'ennuyaient.

points.pattern: make and let + object + base verb

zh.name: make 和 let
zh.meaning: make + 人 + 动词原形表示“迫使、让（不得不）”某人做某事；let + 人 + 动词原形表示“允许”某人做某事。
zh.formation: make + 宾语 + 动词原形（She made me wait.）；let + 宾语 + 动词原形（Let me help you.）；被动：be made to do（I was made to wait.）
zh.contrast: make 和 let 后面不加 to：She made me cry，不说 *made me to cry；Let me go，不说 *Let me to go。但 make 的被动要加 to：He was made to apologise。let 没有被动，用 be allowed to：I was allowed to leave。
zh.example: My parents made me do my homework, but then they let me watch TV.
zh.exampleTranslation: 我父母逼我先写作业，写完后才让我看电视。

en.name: Make and let
en.meaning: Make + person + base verb means force someone to do something; let + person + base verb means allow them to do it.
en.formation: make + object + base verb (She made me wait.); let + object + base verb (Let me help you.); passive: be made to do (I was made to wait.)
en.contrast: No to after make or let: She made me cry, not *made me to cry; Let me go, not *Let me to go. But the passive of make takes to: He was made to apologise. Let has no passive; use be allowed to: I was allowed to leave.
en.example: My parents made me do my homework, but then they let me watch TV.
en.exampleTranslation: My parents made me do my homework, but then they let me watch TV.

fr.name: Make et let
fr.meaning: Make + personne + base verbale signifie « obliger / faire faire » ; let + personne + base verbale signifie « laisser, permettre ».
fr.formation: make + complément + base verbale (She made me wait.) ; let + complément + base verbale (Let me help you.) ; passif : be made to do (I was made to wait.)
fr.contrast: « Faire pleurer quelqu'un » = make someone cry, sans to ; « laisser partir » = let someone go, et non *let someone to go. Au passif : He was made to apologise (avec to) ; pour let, on dit be allowed to.
fr.example: My parents made me do my homework, but then they let me watch TV.
fr.exampleTranslation: Mes parents m'ont obligé à faire mes devoirs, mais ensuite ils m'ont laissé regarder la télé.

zh.name: 混合条件句
zh.meaning: 混合条件句把不同时间混在一起：过去的假设 → 现在的结果，或现在的情况 → 过去的结果。
zh.formation: 过去 → 现在：If + had + 过去分词, would + 动词原形（If I had slept, I wouldn't be tired now）；现在 → 过去：If + 过去式, would have + 过去分词（If I were braver, I would have said something）
zh.contrast: 第三条件句的结果也在过去：If I had studied, I would have passed（当时会通过）。混合条件句的结果在现在：If I had studied, I would know the answer now（现在就会知道）。
zh.example: If I had studied harder last night, I would know the answer to this question now.
zh.exampleTranslation: 如果我昨晚更努力地学习了，我现在就会知道这个问题的答案了。

en.name: Mixed conditionals
en.meaning: Mixed conditionals mix times: an unreal past condition with a present result, or an unreal present situation with a past result.
en.formation: past → present: If + had + past participle, would + base verb (If I had slept, I wouldn't be tired now); present → past: If + past simple, would have + past participle (If I were braver, I would have said something)
en.contrast: In the third conditional the result is also past: If I had studied, I would have passed (then). In a mixed conditional the result is now: If I had studied, I would know the answer now.
en.example: If I had studied harder last night, I would know the answer to this question now.
en.exampleTranslation: If I had studied harder last night, I would know the answer to this question now.

fr.name: Conditionnels mixtes
fr.meaning: Les conditionnels mixtes mélangent les temps : une condition passée irréelle avec un résultat présent, ou une situation présente irréelle avec un résultat passé.
fr.formation: passé → présent : If + had + participe passé, would + base verbale (If I had slept, I wouldn't be tired now) ; présent → passé : If + prétérit, would have + participe passé (If I were braver, I would have said something)
fr.contrast: Comme en français : « si j'avais dormi, je ne serais pas fatigué maintenant » (plus-que-parfait + conditionnel présent). Dans le troisième conditionnel, le résultat est passé : If I had studied, I would have passed.
fr.example: If I had studied harder last night, I would know the answer to this question now.
fr.exampleTranslation: Si j'avais mieux étudié hier soir, je connaîtrais la réponse à cette question maintenant.

zh.name: 间接疑问句
zh.meaning: 间接疑问句是把问题放进另一个句子里（如 Could you tell me …? / I don't know …），用陈述句语序，听起来更礼貌。
zh.formation: Do you know / Could you tell me / I wonder + 疑问词 / if + 主语 + 动词（Do you know where she lives? / I wonder if he's coming.）
zh.contrast: 间接疑问句不倒装，也不用 do / does / did：Could you tell me where the station is?，不说 *where is the station?；Do you know what time it starts?，不说 *what time does it start?
zh.example: Could you please tell me where the nearest train station is?
zh.exampleTranslation: 请问您能告诉我最近的火车站在哪儿吗？

en.name: Embedded questions
en.meaning: An embedded question is a question inside another sentence (Could you tell me…?, I don't know…). It uses statement word order and sounds more polite.
en.formation: Do you know / Could you tell me / I wonder + question word / if + subject + verb (Do you know where she lives? / I wonder if he's coming.)
en.contrast: No inversion and no do/does/did: Could you tell me where the station is?, not *where is the station? Do you know what time it starts?, not *what time does it start?
en.example: Could you please tell me where the nearest train station is?
en.exampleTranslation: Could you please tell me where the nearest train station is?

fr.name: Questions indirectes
fr.meaning: Une question indirecte est intégrée dans une autre phrase (Could you tell me…?, I don't know…). Elle prend l'ordre d'une affirmation et paraît plus polie.
fr.formation: Do you know / Could you tell me / I wonder + mot interrogatif / if + sujet + verbe (Do you know where she lives? / I wonder if he's coming.)
fr.contrast: Pas d'inversion ni de do/does/did, comme dans « Savez-vous où elle habite ? » : Could you tell me where the station is?, et non *where is the station?
fr.example: Could you please tell me where the nearest train station is?
fr.exampleTranslation: Pourriez-vous me dire où se trouve la gare la plus proche ?

zh.name: 越……越……（the more）
zh.meaning: the + 比较级 …, the + 比较级 … 表示“越……就越……”，两件事一起变化。
zh.formation: The + 比较级 + 主语 + 动词, the + 比较级 + 主语 + 动词（The more you practise, the better you get.）；短语：the sooner the better
zh.contrast: 两个部分都要有 the：The more you read, the more you learn，不说 *More you read, more you learn。比较级不能叠加：the better，不说 *the more better。“越来越”用“比较级 and 比较级”：bigger and bigger。
zh.example: The more you practise, the better you become.
zh.exampleTranslation: 你练得越多，就会变得越好。

en.name: The more…, the better…
en.meaning: The + comparative …, the + comparative … shows that two things change together: when one increases, so does the other.
en.formation: The + comparative + subject + verb, the + comparative + subject + verb (The more you practise, the better you get.); short phrase: the sooner the better
en.contrast: Both halves need the: The more you read, the more you learn, not *More you read, more you learn. Don't double the comparative: the better, not *the more better. For gradual change use comparative and comparative: bigger and bigger.
en.example: The more you practise, the better you become.
en.exampleTranslation: The more you practise, the better you become.

fr.name: The more…, the more…
fr.meaning: The + comparatif …, the + comparatif … exprime que deux choses varient ensemble, comme « plus…, plus… ».
fr.formation: The + comparatif + sujet + verbe, the + comparatif + sujet + verbe (The more you practise, the better you get.) ; expression : the sooner the better
fr.contrast: « Plus…, plus… » se dit the more…, the more…, avec the dans les deux parties : The more you read, the more you learn. « De plus en plus » se dit comparatif and comparatif : bigger and bigger.
fr.example: The more you practise, the better you become.
fr.exampleTranslation: Plus tu t'entraînes, plus tu progresses.

zh.name: 过去将来时
zh.meaning: 过去将来时站在过去某个时间看“将来”，用 would 或 was / were going to；常用于转述，或表示原来打算但没实现的事。
zh.formation: would + 动词原形（He said he would help.）；was / were going to + 动词原形（I was going to call you, but I forgot.）
zh.contrast: 从过去看将来要用 would：She said she would come（只有那件事现在仍在将来时才可用 will）。was going to 常表示“原本打算，但没做成”。
zh.example: She said she would call me, but she didn't.
zh.exampleTranslation: 她说会给我打电话，但她没打。

en.name: Future in the past
en.meaning: The future in the past looks forward from a past moment, using would or was / were going to. It is common in reported speech and for plans that didn't happen.
en.formation: would + base verb (He said he would help.); was / were going to + base verb (I was going to call you, but I forgot.)
en.contrast: Seen from the past, will becomes would: She said she would come (will is possible only if it's still in the future). Was going to often means the plan didn't happen: I was going to call you, but I forgot.
en.example: She said she would call me, but she didn't.
en.exampleTranslation: She said she would call me, but she didn't.

fr.name: Futur dans le passé
fr.meaning: Le futur dans le passé regarde vers l'avenir depuis un moment passé, avec would ou was / were going to. On l'emploie au discours indirect et pour des projets non réalisés.
fr.formation: would + base verbale (He said he would help.) ; was / were going to + base verbale (I was going to call you, but I forgot.)
fr.contrast: C'est le conditionnel de « il a dit qu'il viendrait » : He said he would come. Was going to correspond à « j'allais… » et indique souvent un projet abandonné : I was going to call you, but I forgot.
fr.example: She said she would call me, but she didn't.
fr.exampleTranslation: Elle a dit qu'elle m'appellerait, mais elle ne l'a pas fait.

zh.name: 分词短语
zh.meaning: 分词短语用 -ing 形式或过去分词代替状语从句，说明时间、原因或伴随情况，使句子更简洁。
zh.formation: -ing（主动）：Feeling tired, she went to bed.；过去分词（被动）：Written in 1990, the book is still popular.；完成式：Having finished, he left.
zh.contrast: 分词的逻辑主语必须是主句的主语：Walking home, I saw an accident，不说 *Walking home, the rain started（雨不会走路）。主动意义用 -ing，被动意义用过去分词。
zh.example: Sitting by the window, the student noticed the first snow of the winter falling outside.
zh.exampleTranslation: 那个学生坐在窗边，注意到外面正飘着这个冬天的第一场雪。

en.name: Participle clauses
en.meaning: A participle clause uses an -ing form or past participle instead of a full adverbial clause, to give time, reason or background more briefly.
en.formation: -ing (active): Feeling tired, she went to bed.; past participle (passive): Written in 1990, the book is still popular.; perfect: Having finished, he left.
en.contrast: The participle's subject must be the subject of the main clause: Walking home, I saw an accident, not *Walking home, the rain started. Use -ing for active meaning and the past participle for passive.
en.example: Sitting by the window, the student noticed the first snow of the winter falling outside.
en.exampleTranslation: Sitting by the window, the student noticed the first snow of the winter falling outside.

fr.name: Propositions participiales
fr.meaning: Une proposition participiale remplace une subordonnée circonstancielle par une forme en -ing ou un participe passé, pour exprimer le temps, la cause ou les circonstances plus brièvement.
fr.formation: -ing (actif) : Feeling tired, she went to bed. ; participe passé (passif) : Written in 1990, the book is still popular. ; forme parfaite : Having finished, he left.
fr.contrast: Comme en français, le sujet du participe doit être celui de la principale : Walking home, I saw an accident, et non *Walking home, the rain started. -ing = actif ; participe passé = passif.
fr.example: Sitting by the window, the student noticed the first snow of the winter falling outside.
fr.exampleTranslation: Assis près de la fenêtre, l'élève a vu tomber dehors la première neige de l'hiver.

zh.name: It is said that
zh.meaning: It is said / believed / thought / reported that … 用来客观地转述大家的说法或看法，不说明是谁说的，常见于新闻和正式文体。
zh.formation: It + be + said / believed / thought / reported / expected + that + 从句（It is said that the hotel is haunted.）
zh.contrast: 也可以用人或物作主语，后接 to 不定式：He is said to be very rich（= It is said that he is very rich）。日常口语常直接说 People say …。
zh.example: It is believed that the company will launch a new phone soon.
zh.exampleTranslation: 据信该公司不久将推出一款新手机。

en.name: It is said that…
en.meaning: It is said / believed / thought / reported that … reports what people in general say or think, without naming them. It is common in news and formal writing.
en.formation: It + be + said / believed / thought / reported / expected + that + clause (It is said that the hotel is haunted.)
en.contrast: The person or thing can also be the subject, followed by a to-infinitive: He is said to be very rich (= It is said that he is very rich). In everyday speech people often say People say…
en.example: It is believed that the company will launch a new phone soon.
en.exampleTranslation: It is believed that the company will launch a new phone soon.

fr.name: It is said that…
fr.meaning: It is said / believed / thought / reported that … rapporte ce que les gens disent ou pensent en général, sans les nommer, comme « on dit que ». C'est fréquent dans la presse.
fr.formation: It + be + said / believed / thought / reported / expected + that + proposition (It is said that the hotel is haunted.)
fr.contrast: « On dit que » se traduit par It is said that…, ou avec la personne comme sujet + to : He is said to be very rich (on dit qu'il est très riche). Ne traduisez pas « on » par *one says.
fr.example: It is believed that the company will launch a new phone soon.
fr.exampleTranslation: On pense que l'entreprise lancera bientôt un nouveau téléphone.

zh.name: 分裂句
zh.meaning: 分裂句把一句话拆成两部分来强调其中某个成分，常见形式有 It is / was … that / who … 和 What … is …。
zh.formation: It + be + 被强调部分 + that / who + 其余部分（It was Sarah who helped me.）；What + 从句 + be + 被强调部分（What I need is a holiday.）
zh.contrast: 不能省掉 who / that：It was Sarah who helped me，不说 *It was Sarah helped me。中文“是……的”强调时间时，要说 It was yesterday that I arrived，不要直译。
zh.example: It was Sarah who helped me finish the difficult project yesterday.
zh.exampleTranslation: 昨天帮我完成那个难项目的，正是萨拉。

en.name: Cleft sentences
en.meaning: A cleft sentence splits one idea into two parts to emphasise one element. Common forms are It is/was … that/who … and What … is …
en.formation: It + be + focus + that / who + rest (It was Sarah who helped me.); What + clause + be + focus (What I need is a holiday.)
en.contrast: Don't drop who/that: It was Sarah who helped me, not *It was Sarah helped me. Emphatic do stresses only the verb (I did help), while a cleft can focus on a subject, object or time.
en.example: It was Sarah who helped me finish the difficult project yesterday.
en.exampleTranslation: It was Sarah who helped me finish the difficult project yesterday.

fr.name: Phrases clivées
fr.meaning: La phrase clivée découpe une idée en deux parties pour mettre un élément en relief, comme « c'est … qui / que ». Formes courantes : It is/was … that/who … et What … is …
fr.formation: It + be + élément mis en relief + that / who + reste (It was Sarah who helped me.) ; What + proposition + be + élément (What I need is a holiday. = Ce dont j'ai besoin, c'est de vacances.)
fr.contrast: « C'est … qui » correspond à It is … who, mais be suit le temps du récit : It was Sarah who helped me (c'est Sarah qui m'a aidé). Ne supprimez pas who/that : *It was Sarah helped me.
fr.example: It was Sarah who helped me finish the difficult project yesterday.
fr.exampleTranslation: C'est Sarah qui m'a aidé à finir ce projet difficile hier.

zh.name: 否定倒装
zh.meaning: 否定或限制意义的词（never, rarely, hardly, not only, only then 等）放在句首表示强调时，后面要部分倒装，多用于正式或书面语。
zh.formation: 否定词 + 助动词 / be / 情态动词 + 主语 + 动词（Never have I seen … / Not only did he win, but he also … / Hardly had we arrived when …）
zh.contrast: 没有助动词时要加 do / does / did：Rarely do I eat meat，不说 *Rarely I eat meat。否定词不在句首时不倒装：I have never seen such a park。
zh.example: Never have I seen such a beautiful park.
zh.exampleTranslation: 我从来没见过这么美的公园。

en.name: Negative inversion
en.meaning: When a negative or limiting word (never, rarely, hardly, not only, only then…) starts the sentence for emphasis, the auxiliary comes before the subject. It is formal or literary.
en.formation: negative word + auxiliary / be / modal + subject + verb (Never have I seen … / Not only did he win, but he also … / Hardly had we arrived when …)
en.contrast: If there is no auxiliary, add do/does/did: Rarely do I eat meat, not *Rarely I eat meat. When the negative word isn't first, use normal order: I have never seen such a park.
en.example: Never have I seen such a beautiful park.
en.exampleTranslation: Never have I seen such a beautiful park.

fr.name: Inversion après négation
fr.meaning: Quand un mot négatif ou restrictif (never, rarely, hardly, not only, only then…) ouvre la phrase pour insister, l'auxiliaire passe devant le sujet. C'est un style soutenu.
fr.formation: mot négatif + auxiliaire / be / modal + sujet + verbe (Never have I seen … / Not only did he win, but he also … / Hardly had we arrived when …)
fr.contrast: Comme « Jamais n'ai-je vu… » en français soutenu, mais obligatoire en anglais après ces mots. Sans auxiliaire, ajoutez do/does/did : Rarely do I eat meat, et non *Rarely I eat meat.
fr.example: Never have I seen such a beautiful park.
fr.exampleTranslation: Jamais je n'ai vu un parc aussi beau.

points.pattern: result clauses with so and such

zh.name: so / such … that
zh.meaning: so … that 和 such … that 表示“如此……以至于……”，说明程度和由此产生的结果。
zh.formation: so + 形容词 / 副词 + that（It was so hot that …）；such + (a / an) + 形容词 + 名词 + that（It was such a hot day that …）；so many / much + 名词 + that
zh.contrast: so 接形容词或副词，such 接名词短语：so hot / such a hot day，不说 *so hot day / *such hot。单数可数名词前用 such a：such a good film。口语中 that 常省略：I was so tired I fell asleep。
zh.example: The coffee was so hot that I had to wait ten minutes to drink it.
zh.exampleTranslation: 咖啡太烫了，我只好等了十分钟才喝。

en.name: So / such … that
en.meaning: So … that and such … that show a high degree and the result it causes.
en.formation: so + adjective / adverb + that (It was so hot that …); such + (a / an) + adjective + noun + that (It was such a hot day that …); so many / much + noun + that
en.contrast: So goes with an adjective or adverb, such with a noun phrase: so hot / such a hot day, not *so hot day or *such hot. Use such a before a singular countable noun. In speech that is often dropped: I was so tired I fell asleep.
en.example: The coffee was so hot that I had to wait ten minutes to drink it.
en.exampleTranslation: The coffee was so hot that I had to wait ten minutes to drink it.

fr.name: So / such … that
fr.meaning: So … that et such … that expriment un haut degré et la conséquence qui en découle, comme « si / tellement … que ».
fr.formation: so + adjectif / adverbe + that (It was so hot that …) ; such + (a / an) + adjectif + nom + that (It was such a hot day that …) ; so many / much + nom + that
fr.contrast: « Si / tellement » se dit so devant un adjectif (so hot) et such devant un nom (such a hot day), et non *so hot day. Such se place avant l'article : such a good film (un si bon film).
fr.example: The coffee was so hot that I had to wait ten minutes to drink it.
fr.exampleTranslation: Le café était si chaud que j'ai dû attendre dix minutes avant de le boire.

points.pattern: stative and dynamic verbs with multiple meanings
aliases: verbs with state and action meanings

zh.name: 状态动词与动作动词
zh.meaning: 有些动词（think, have, see, taste, look 等）有两种意思：表示状态时不用进行时，表示动作时可以用进行时。
zh.formation: think：I think it's good（认为）/ I'm thinking about it（考虑）；have：I have a car（拥有）/ I'm having lunch（吃）；see：I see（明白）/ I'm seeing the doctor（看医生）；taste：It tastes sweet / I'm tasting the soup
zh.contrast: 表示状态时不能用进行时：I have a car，不说 *I'm having a car；I think you're right，不说 *I'm thinking you're right。know、want、believe、belong 只有状态意义，从不用进行时。
zh.example: I think this movie is wonderful, and I am thinking about seeing it again.
zh.exampleTranslation: 我认为这部电影很精彩，而且我正在考虑再去看一遍。

en.name: State and action verbs
en.meaning: Some verbs (think, have, see, taste, look…) have a state meaning, which is not used in the continuous, and an action meaning, which is.
en.formation: think: I think it's good (opinion) / I'm thinking about it (considering); have: I have a car (own) / I'm having lunch (eating); see: I see (understand) / I'm seeing the doctor (meeting); taste: It tastes sweet / I'm tasting the soup
en.contrast: The state meaning is never continuous: I have a car, not *I'm having a car; I think you're right, not *I'm thinking you're right. Know, want, believe and belong are state-only verbs.
en.example: I think this movie is wonderful, and I am thinking about seeing it again.
en.exampleTranslation: I think this movie is wonderful, and I am thinking about seeing it again.

fr.name: Verbes d'état et d'action
fr.meaning: Certains verbes (think, have, see, taste, look…) ont un sens d'état, sans forme continue, et un sens d'action, compatible avec la forme continue.
fr.formation: think : I think it's good (opinion) / I'm thinking about it (réflexion) ; have : I have a car (possession) / I'm having lunch (repas) ; see : I see (je comprends) / I'm seeing the doctor (rendez-vous) ; taste : It tastes sweet / I'm tasting the soup
fr.contrast: Au sens d'état, pas de forme continue : I have a car, et non *I'm having a car ; I think you're right (je pense que tu as raison), et non *I'm thinking you're right. Know, want, believe ne sont jamais continus.
fr.example: I think this movie is wonderful, and I am thinking about seeing it again.
fr.exampleTranslation: Je trouve ce film génial, et je pense aller le revoir.

zh.name: 助动词 do 表示强调
zh.meaning: 在肯定句的动词原形前加 do / does / did（说话时重读），用来强调、确认或反驳对方，相当于“确实、真的”。
zh.formation: do / does / did + 动词原形（I do like it. / She does work hard. / I did call you!）；祈使句：Do sit down.
zh.contrast: did 后面的动词用原形：I did call you，不说 *I did called you。be 和情态动词不用 do，直接重读：I AM listening，不说 *I do am listening。
zh.example: I don't eat much meat, but I do like chicken.
zh.exampleTranslation: 我不怎么吃肉，但我确实很喜欢鸡肉。

en.name: Emphatic do
en.meaning: Do / does / did before a base verb in a positive sentence (stressed in speech) adds emphasis, confirms something or contradicts what someone said.
en.formation: do / does / did + base verb (I do like it. / She does work hard. / I did call you!); imperatives: Do sit down.
en.contrast: After did, use the base verb: I did call you, not *I did called you. Be and modals don't take do; just stress them: I AM listening, not *I do am listening.
en.example: I don't eat much meat, but I do like chicken.
en.exampleTranslation: I don't eat much meat, but I do like chicken.

fr.name: Do d'insistance
fr.meaning: Do / does / did devant la base verbale dans une phrase affirmative (accentué à l'oral) sert à insister, confirmer ou contredire, comme « vraiment / bel et bien ».
fr.formation: do / does / did + base verbale (I do like it. / She does work hard. / I did call you!) ; impératif : Do sit down. (Asseyez-vous donc.)
fr.contrast: Le français insiste avec « bien / vraiment » : Je t'ai bien appelé = I did call you, et non *I did called you. Pas de do avec be ou un modal : on accentue le verbe (I AM listening).
fr.example: I don't eat much meat, but I do like chicken.
fr.exampleTranslation: Je ne mange pas beaucoup de viande, mais j'aime vraiment le poulet.

aliases: 带介词的关系代词从句

zh.name: 介词+whom/which
zh.meaning: 关系从句中的介词可以放在 whom / which 前面（正式），也可以放在从句末尾（口语）。
zh.formation: 正式：名词 + 介词 + whom / which + 从句（the manager with whom I spoke）；口语：名词 + (who / that) + 从句 + 介词（the manager (who) I spoke with）
zh.contrast: 介词前置时只能用 whom（人）或 which（物），不能用 who 或 that：with whom，不说 *with who / *with that。口语里更常把介词放在句末：the house (that) I grew up in。
zh.example: This is the manager with whom I discussed the new project.
zh.exampleTranslation: 这就是和我讨论过新项目的那位经理。

en.name: Relative clauses with prepositions
en.meaning: In a relative clause, the preposition can go before whom / which (formal) or at the end of the clause (everyday English).
en.formation: formal: noun + preposition + whom / which + clause (the manager with whom I spoke); informal: noun + (who / that) + clause + preposition (the manager (who) I spoke with)
en.contrast: After a preposition, use only whom (people) or which (things), never who or that: with whom, not *with who or *with that. In speech the preposition usually goes at the end: the house (that) I grew up in.
en.example: This is the manager with whom I discussed the new project.
en.exampleTranslation: This is the manager with whom I discussed the new project.

fr.name: Relatives avec préposition
fr.meaning: Dans une relative, la préposition peut se placer devant whom / which (style soutenu) ou à la fin de la proposition (anglais courant).
fr.formation: soutenu : nom + préposition + whom / which + proposition (the manager with whom I spoke) ; courant : nom + (who / that) + proposition + préposition (the manager (who) I spoke with)
fr.contrast: En français, la préposition vient toujours devant (« avec qui », « dans laquelle »). En anglais courant, elle passe à la fin : the house I grew up in (la maison où j'ai grandi). Après une préposition : whom ou which, jamais that.
fr.example: This is the manager with whom I discussed the new project.
fr.exampleTranslation: Voici le directeur avec qui j'ai parlé du nouveau projet.

points.pattern: habitual past with would and will
aliases: past habits with will and would

zh.name: would 表示过去习惯
zh.meaning: would + 动词原形可以描述过去经常重复的动作，常用于回忆；will 可以描述某人现在的典型习惯。
zh.formation: would + 动词原形（Every summer we would go to the beach.）；will + 动词原形表示现在的习惯（He'll sit there for hours.）
zh.contrast: would 只表示过去重复的动作，不表示过去的状态：I used to live in Paris，不说 *I would live in Paris。used to 两者都可以。would 需要有明确的过去背景，否则容易被理解成条件句。
zh.example: When we were children, we would spend hours playing in the woods.
zh.exampleTranslation: 我们小时候常常在树林里玩上好几个小时。

en.name: Would for past habits
en.meaning: Would + base verb can describe repeated actions in the past, often in memories. Will can describe someone's typical behaviour now.
en.formation: would + base verb (Every summer we would go to the beach.); will + base verb for present habits (He'll sit there for hours.)
en.contrast: Would is only for repeated actions, not past states: I used to live in Paris, not *I would live in Paris. Used to works for both. Would also needs a clear past context, or it sounds conditional.
en.example: When we were children, we would spend hours playing in the woods.
en.exampleTranslation: When we were children, we would spend hours playing in the woods.

fr.name: Would pour l'habitude passée
fr.meaning: Would + base verbale peut décrire des actions répétées dans le passé, souvent dans des souvenirs (comme l'imparfait). Will peut décrire un comportement typique actuel.
fr.formation: would + base verbale (Every summer we would go to the beach.) ; will + base verbale pour une habitude actuelle (He'll sit there for hours.)
fr.contrast: Would ne traduit l'imparfait que pour des actions répétées, pas pour un état : I used to live in Paris (j'habitais à Paris), et non *I would live in Paris. Used to convient dans les deux cas.
fr.example: When we were children, we would spend hours playing in the woods.
fr.exampleTranslation: Quand nous étions enfants, nous passions des heures à jouer dans les bois.

zh.name: 被动动名词与不定式
zh.meaning: 动名词或不定式表示的动作由主语承受时，用被动形式：being + 过去分词，to be + 过去分词。
zh.formation: 动词 + being + 过去分词（She hates being interrupted.）；动词 + to be + 过去分词（He wants to be invited.）；介词后也用 being + 过去分词：without being seen
zh.contrast: 主动和被动意思相反：I don't like interrupting people（我打断别人）/ I don't like being interrupted（别人打断我）。不能省掉 being / to be：不说 *She hates interrupted。
zh.example: She hates being interrupted while she is speaking.
zh.exampleTranslation: 她讨厌在说话时被人打断。

en.name: Passive -ing and infinitives
en.meaning: When the subject receives the action of a gerund or infinitive, use the passive form: being + past participle or to be + past participle.
en.formation: verb + being + past participle (She hates being interrupted.); verb + to be + past participle (He wants to be invited.); after prepositions too: without being seen
en.contrast: Active and passive mean opposite things: I don't like interrupting people (I interrupt them) vs I don't like being interrupted (they interrupt me). Don't drop being / to be: not *She hates interrupted.
en.example: She hates being interrupted while she is speaking.
en.exampleTranslation: She hates being interrupted while she is speaking.

fr.name: Gérondif et infinitif passifs
fr.meaning: Quand le sujet subit l'action d'un gérondif ou d'un infinitif, on emploie la forme passive : being + participe passé ou to be + participe passé.
fr.formation: verbe + being + participe passé (She hates being interrupted.) ; verbe + to be + participe passé (He wants to be invited.) ; après une préposition aussi : without being seen
fr.contrast: Comme « être interrompu », la forme passive est nécessaire : She hates being interrupted, et non *She hates interrupting (qui veut dire qu'elle interrompt les autres). « Sans être vu » = without being seen.
fr.example: She hates being interrupted while she is speaking.
fr.exampleTranslation: Elle déteste être interrompue quand elle parle.

points.pattern: relative clauses referring to a whole sentence
aliases: relative clauses with which referring to a clause

zh.name: which 指代整句
zh.meaning: 用 , which … 指代前面整句话所说的事，并对它进行评价或补充。
zh.formation: 主句, which + 动词 …（He passed the exam, which surprised us. / It rained all day, which was a pity.）
zh.contrast: 指代整句话只能用 which，不能用 what、that 或 it：…, which surprised us，不说 *…, what surprised us / *…, it surprised us（中文的“这让我们……”）。which 前面必须有逗号。
zh.example: He passed the difficult exam, which surprised all of us.
zh.exampleTranslation: 他通过了那场高难度考试，这让我们所有人都很吃惊。

en.name: Which referring to a clause
en.meaning: A clause with , which … can refer back to the whole previous clause and comment on it.
en.formation: main clause, which + verb … (He passed the exam, which surprised us. / It rained all day, which was a pity.)
en.contrast: To refer to a whole clause, use which, not what, that or it: …, which surprised us, not *…, what surprised us. A comma always comes before which.
en.example: He passed the difficult exam, which surprised all of us.
en.exampleTranslation: He passed the difficult exam, which surprised all of us.

fr.name: Which reprenant une phrase
fr.meaning: Une proposition en , which … peut reprendre toute la proposition précédente pour la commenter, comme « ce qui / ce que ».
fr.formation: proposition principale, which + verbe … (He passed the exam, which surprised us. / It rained all day, which was a pity.)
fr.contrast: « Ce qui » se traduit ici par which, et non par what : He passed the exam, which surprised us (ce qui nous a surpris), et non *what surprised us. Toujours une virgule avant which.
fr.example: He passed the difficult exam, which surprised all of us.
fr.exampleTranslation: Il a réussi cet examen difficile, ce qui nous a tous surpris.

zh.name: 进行式和完成式不定式
zh.meaning: 不定式也有进行式（to be doing，表示正在进行）和完成式（to have done，表示发生在谓语动词之前），常跟在 seem、appear、be said 等后面。
zh.formation: to be + 动词-ing（He seems to be sleeping.）；to have + 过去分词（She seems to have forgotten.）；He is said to have left.
zh.contrast: 一般式表示同时：He seems to be tired（现在看起来累）；完成式表示更早：He seems to have been ill（之前好像病过）。to 后面用 have：to have forgotten，不说 *to forgot / *to had forgotten。
zh.example: She seemed to have forgotten about our meeting.
zh.exampleTranslation: 她似乎已经忘记了我们的会议。

en.name: Continuous and perfect infinitives
en.meaning: Infinitives also have a continuous form (to be doing: in progress) and a perfect form (to have done: earlier than the main verb). They often follow seem, appear and be said.
en.formation: to be + verb-ing (He seems to be sleeping.); to have + past participle (She seems to have forgotten.); He is said to have left.
en.contrast: The simple infinitive shows the same time: He seems to be tired (now). The perfect shows an earlier time: He seems to have been ill (before). After to use have, not a past form: to have forgotten, not *to forgot or *to had forgotten.
en.example: She seemed to have forgotten about our meeting.
en.exampleTranslation: She seemed to have forgotten about our meeting.

fr.name: Infinitifs continu et passé
fr.meaning: L'infinitif a aussi une forme continue (to be doing : en cours) et une forme passée (to have done : antérieure au verbe principal), souvent après seem, appear ou be said.
fr.formation: to be + verbe-ing (He seems to be sleeping.) ; to have + participe passé (She seems to have forgotten.) ; He is said to have left.
fr.contrast: C'est l'infinitif passé français : « elle semble avoir oublié » = She seems to have forgotten. L'infinitif simple indique la simultanéité : He seems to be tired (il a l'air fatigué).
fr.example: She seemed to have forgotten about our meeting.
fr.exampleTranslation: Elle semblait avoir oublié notre réunion.

zh.name: It's time + 过去式
zh.meaning: It's time + 主语 + 过去式表示“该做某事了”，常暗示已经有点晚；这里的过去式指的是现在。
zh.formation: It's (high / about) time + 主语 + 一般过去时（It's time we left. / It's high time you got a job.）；It's time + to + 动词原形（It's time to go.）
zh.contrast: 主语后面用过去式，不用现在式：It's time we went，不说 *It's time we go。不说主语时用 It's time to go，语气中性；high time 和 about time 带批评意味。
zh.example: It's late, so it's time we went home.
zh.exampleTranslation: 很晚了，我们该回家了。

en.name: It's time + past
en.meaning: It's time + subject + past simple says something should happen now, or should already have happened. The past form refers to the present.
en.formation: It's (high / about) time + subject + past simple (It's time we left. / It's high time you got a job.); It's time + to + base verb (It's time to go.)
en.contrast: After the subject use the past, not the present: It's time we went, not *It's time we go. It's time to go is neutral; high time and about time sound critical.
en.example: It's late, so it's time we went home.
en.exampleTranslation: It's late, so it's time we went home.

fr.name: It's time + prétérit
fr.meaning: It's time + sujet + prétérit signifie « il est temps que… », souvent avec l'idée que c'est déjà un peu tard. Le prétérit renvoie au présent.
fr.formation: It's (high / about) time + sujet + prétérit (It's time we left. / It's high time you got a job.) ; It's time + to + base verbale (It's time to go.)
fr.contrast: Là où le français met le subjonctif (« il est temps que nous partions »), l'anglais met le prétérit : It's time we left, et non *It's time we leave. Sans sujet : It's time to go.
fr.example: It's late, so it's time we went home.
fr.exampleTranslation: Il est tard, il est temps que nous rentrions.

zh.name: be said to 结构
zh.meaning: 主语 + be said / believed / thought / reported + to 不定式用来转述大家的说法，但让被谈论的人或物作主语，常见于新闻。
zh.formation: 主语 + be + said / believed / thought + to + 动词原形（He is said to be rich.）；说更早的事用 to have + 过去分词（She is believed to have left the country.）
zh.contrast: 和 It is said that … 意思相同，只是主语不同：It is said that he is rich = He is said to be rich。说过去的事要用完成式不定式：He is said to have been rich，不说 *He is said to was rich。
zh.example: The castle is said to be over 800 years old.
zh.exampleTranslation: 据说这座城堡已有八百多年的历史。

en.name: Be said to (passive reporting)
en.meaning: Subject + be said / believed / thought / reported + to-infinitive reports what people say, with the person or thing talked about as the subject. It is common in news.
en.formation: subject + be + said / believed / thought + to + base verb (He is said to be rich.); for an earlier event: to have + past participle (She is believed to have left the country.)
en.contrast: It means the same as It is said that…, with a different subject: It is said that he is rich = He is said to be rich. For an earlier event use the perfect infinitive: He is said to have been rich, not *He is said to was rich.
en.example: The castle is said to be over 800 years old.
en.exampleTranslation: The castle is said to be over 800 years old.

fr.name: Be said to (passif)
fr.meaning: Sujet + be said / believed / thought / reported + to + verbe rapporte ce que disent les gens, avec la personne ou la chose concernée comme sujet. C'est fréquent dans la presse.
fr.formation: sujet + be + said / believed / thought + to + base verbale (He is said to be rich.) ; pour un fait antérieur : to have + participe passé (She is believed to have left the country.)
fr.contrast: « On dit qu'il est riche » peut se dire It is said that he is rich ou He is said to be rich. Pour un fait passé, infinitif passé : He is said to have been rich (on dit qu'il a été riche).
fr.example: The castle is said to be over 800 years old.
fr.exampleTranslation: On dit que ce château a plus de 800 ans.

zh.name: 省略的定语从句
zh.meaning: 定语从句可以简化成分词短语，直接放在名词后面：主动意义用 -ing，被动意义用过去分词，省去关系词和 be。
zh.formation: 名词 + -ing 短语（= who / which + 主动动词）：the man sitting next to me；名词 + 过去分词短语（= who / which + be + 过去分词）：a book written in 1990
zh.contrast: 主动用 -ing，被动用过去分词：the people living here（住在这里的人）/ the cars made in Japan（日本制造的车），不说 *the cars making in Japan。中文定语放在名词前，英语的分词短语放在名词后。
zh.example: The man sitting next to me is a doctor.
zh.exampleTranslation: 坐在我旁边的那个男人是医生。

en.name: Reduced relative clauses
en.meaning: A relative clause can be shortened to a participle phrase after the noun: -ing for an active meaning, a past participle for a passive meaning, with no who/which and no be.
en.formation: noun + -ing phrase (= who / which + active verb): the man sitting next to me; noun + past participle phrase (= who / which + be + past participle): a book written in 1990
en.contrast: Use -ing for active and the past participle for passive: the people living here vs the cars made in Japan, not *the cars making in Japan. The phrase comes after the noun, not before it.
