en.example: The man sitting next to me is a doctor.
en.exampleTranslation: The man sitting next to me is a doctor.

fr.name: Relatives réduites
fr.meaning: Une relative peut se réduire à un groupe participe placé après le nom : -ing pour un sens actif, participe passé pour un sens passif, sans who/which ni be.
fr.formation: nom + groupe en -ing (= who / which + verbe actif) : the man sitting next to me ; nom + participe passé (= who / which + be + participe passé) : a book written in 1990
fr.contrast: C'est comme « l'homme assis à côté de moi » ou « un livre écrit en 1990 ». -ing = actif, participe passé = passif : the cars made in Japan, et non *the cars making in Japan.
fr.example: The man sitting next to me is a doctor.
fr.exampleTranslation: L'homme assis à côté de moi est médecin.

zh.name: 不但……而且……
zh.meaning: not only … but (also) … 表示“不但……而且……”，连接两个同类的成分，强调第二个。
zh.formation: not only + A + but (also) + B，A 和 B 结构相同（She not only sings but also dances.）；放在句首要倒装：Not only does she sing, but she also dances.
zh.contrast: not only 放在句首时，后面要用疑问句语序：Not only did he win，不说 *Not only he won。两部分结构要一致：She is not only clever but also kind（形容词 + 形容词）。
zh.example: She not only speaks French but also teaches it.
zh.exampleTranslation: 她不但会说法语，还教法语。

en.name: Not only … but also
en.meaning: Not only … but (also) … adds a second, often more surprising, point to the first. It links two parts of the same kind.
en.formation: not only + A + but (also) + B, with A and B parallel (She not only sings but also dances.); at the start of a sentence, use inversion: Not only does she sing, but she also dances.
en.contrast: At the start of a sentence, use question word order: Not only did he win, not *Not only he won. Keep the two parts parallel: She is not only clever but also kind.
en.example: She not only speaks French but also teaches it.
en.exampleTranslation: She not only speaks French but also teaches it.

fr.name: Not only … but also
fr.meaning: Not only … but (also) … signifie « non seulement… mais aussi » : on ajoute un second élément, souvent plus fort, au premier.
fr.formation: not only + A + but (also) + B, A et B de même nature (She not only sings but also dances.) ; en tête de phrase, inversion : Not only does she sing, but she also dances.
fr.contrast: En tête de phrase, l'anglais impose l'inversion avec auxiliaire : Not only did he win, et non *Not only he won. Au milieu de la phrase, ordre normal : He not only won but also broke the record.
fr.example: She not only speaks French but also teaches it.
fr.exampleTranslation: Non seulement elle parle français, mais elle l'enseigne aussi.

zh.name: 将来完成进行时
zh.meaning: 将来完成进行时表示到将来某个时间为止，某个动作已经持续了多长时间（可能还会继续），强调时长。
zh.formation: will have been + 动词-ing + for + 时间段（By June, I'll have been living here for a year.）
zh.contrast: 将来完成时强调完成和结果：By June, I'll have written the book；将来完成进行时强调持续时间：By June, I'll have been writing it for two years。
zh.example: By June, I will have been working here for ten years.
zh.exampleTranslation: 到六月，我在这里工作就满十年了。

en.name: Future perfect continuous
en.meaning: The future perfect continuous says how long an activity will have been going on by a certain future time. It stresses duration.
en.formation: will have been + verb-ing + for + period (By June, I'll have been living here for a year.)
en.contrast: The future perfect stresses completion: By June, I'll have written the book. The continuous form stresses duration: By June, I'll have been writing it for two years.
en.example: By June, I will have been working here for ten years.
en.exampleTranslation: By June, I will have been working here for ten years.

fr.name: Future perfect continu
fr.meaning: Le future perfect continu indique depuis combien de temps une activité durera à un moment donné du futur. Il insiste sur la durée.
fr.formation: will have been + verbe-ing + for + durée (By June, I'll have been living here for a year.)
fr.contrast: Le français dit « en juin, cela fera un an que j'habite ici » ; l'anglais : By June, I'll have been living here for a year. Le future perfect simple insiste sur l'achèvement : I'll have written the book.
fr.example: By June, I will have been working here for ten years.
fr.exampleTranslation: En juin, cela fera dix ans que je travaille ici.

points.pattern: needn't have vs didn't need to

zh.name: needn't have 用法
zh.meaning: needn't have + 过去分词表示某事做了，但其实没有必要；didn't need to + 动词原形表示没有必要做（通常也就没做）。
zh.formation: needn't have + 过去分词（You needn't have waited.）；didn't need to + 动词原形（I didn't need to wait, so I went home.）
zh.contrast: needn't have done = 做了，但白做了：I needn't have taken an umbrella（带了伞，结果没下雨）；didn't need to do 一般表示没必要，所以没做：I didn't need to take an umbrella。
zh.example: You needn't have bought flowers, but they're beautiful.
zh.exampleTranslation: 你其实不必买花的，不过花真漂亮。

en.name: Needn't have
en.meaning: Needn't have + past participle means something was done but wasn't necessary. Didn't need to + base verb means it wasn't necessary (and usually wasn't done).
en.formation: needn't have + past participle (You needn't have waited.); didn't need to + base verb (I didn't need to wait, so I went home.)
en.contrast: Needn't have done = you did it, but it was unnecessary: I needn't have taken an umbrella (I took one; it didn't rain). Didn't need to do usually means you didn't do it: I didn't need to take an umbrella.
en.example: You needn't have bought flowers, but they're beautiful.
en.exampleTranslation: You needn't have bought flowers, but they're beautiful.

fr.name: Needn't have
fr.meaning: Needn't have + participe passé signifie qu'on a fait quelque chose d'inutile. Didn't need to + base verbale signifie que ce n'était pas nécessaire (et qu'en général on ne l'a pas fait).
fr.formation: needn't have + participe passé (You needn't have waited.) ; didn't need to + base verbale (I didn't need to wait, so I went home.)
fr.contrast: « Je n'avais pas besoin de prendre un parapluie » est ambigu en français. I needn't have taken an umbrella = je l'ai pris pour rien ; I didn't need to take an umbrella = en général, je ne l'ai pas pris.
fr.example: You needn't have bought flowers, but they're beautiful.
fr.exampleTranslation: Tu n'avais pas besoin d'acheter des fleurs, mais elles sont magnifiques.

zh.name: wish + would
zh.meaning: wish + 某人 + would + 动词原形表示希望别人（或情况）有所改变，常带不满或抱怨。
zh.formation: wish (that) + 他人 / 事物 + would / wouldn't + 动词原形（I wish you would listen. / I wish it would stop raining.）
zh.contrast: wish … would 用于希望别人或情况改变，不用于自己：I wish I could swim / I wish I had a car，不说 *I wish I would have a car。表示状态用过去式：I wish you were here。
zh.example: I wish my neighbours would turn their music down.
zh.exampleTranslation: 我真希望邻居能把音乐调小一点。

en.name: Wish + would
en.meaning: Wish + someone + would + base verb expresses a wish for someone else (or something) to change, often with annoyance.
en.formation: wish (that) + other person / thing + would / wouldn't + base verb (I wish you would listen. / I wish it would stop raining.)
en.contrast: Wish … would is about other people or things changing, not about yourself: I wish I could swim / I wish I had a car, not *I wish I would have a car. For states, use the past: I wish you were here.
en.example: I wish my neighbours would turn their music down.
en.exampleTranslation: I wish my neighbours would turn their music down.

fr.name: Wish + would
fr.meaning: Wish + quelqu'un + would + base verbale exprime le souhait que quelqu'un (ou quelque chose) change, souvent avec agacement (« si seulement tu… »).
fr.formation: wish (that) + autre personne / chose + would / wouldn't + base verbale (I wish you would listen. / I wish it would stop raining.)
fr.contrast: Wish … would porte sur les autres, pas sur soi : I wish I could swim (j'aimerais savoir nager), et non *I wish I would swim. Pour un état, on emploie le prétérit : I wish you were here.
fr.example: I wish my neighbours would turn their music down.
fr.exampleTranslation: J'aimerais bien que mes voisins baissent leur musique.

zh.name: in case 以防
zh.meaning: in case + 从句表示“以防、万一”：为了应对可能发生的情况而提前做某事。
zh.formation: 主句 + in case + 一般现在时（Take a coat in case it gets cold.）；过去：in case + 一般过去时（I took a coat in case it got cold.）；in case of + 名词（in case of fire）
zh.contrast: in case 和 if 不同：Take an umbrella in case it rains（现在就带，以防下雨）/ Take an umbrella if it rains（下雨了才带）。in case 后面不用 will：in case it rains，不说 *in case it will rain。
zh.example: I'll write down the address in case I forget it.
zh.exampleTranslation: 我把地址记下来，以防忘了。

en.name: In case
en.meaning: In case + clause means 'because something might happen': we do something now to be ready for a possible situation.
en.formation: main clause + in case + present simple (Take a coat in case it gets cold.); past: in case + past simple (I took a coat in case it got cold.); in case of + noun (in case of fire)
en.contrast: In case is not if: Take an umbrella in case it rains (take it now, to be safe) vs Take an umbrella if it rains (only if it is raining). No will after in case: in case it rains, not *in case it will rain.
en.example: I'll write down the address in case I forget it.
en.exampleTranslation: I'll write down the address in case I forget it.

fr.name: In case
fr.meaning: In case + proposition signifie « au cas où » : on fait quelque chose maintenant pour être prêt à une situation possible.
fr.formation: principale + in case + présent simple (Take a coat in case it gets cold.) ; passé : in case + prétérit (I took a coat in case it got cold.) ; in case of + nom (in case of fire)
fr.contrast: « Au cas où » est suivi du conditionnel en français, mais in case prend le présent : in case it rains (au cas où il pleuvrait), et non *in case it would rain. In case n'est pas if : on agit maintenant, par précaution.
fr.example: I'll write down the address in case I forget it.
fr.exampleTranslation: Je vais noter l'adresse au cas où je l'oublierais.
